source.title: On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties

summary: Caraiani and Scholze prove that for compact unitary Shimura varieties the torsion in the cohomology localized at a Hecke eigensystem whose Galois representation is decomposed generic at a suitable prime is concentrated in the middle degree, and attach Galois representations to torsion eigensystems (Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 6.3.1), through the Hodge–Tate period map, Igusa varieties and Shin's trace formula. Corrected in place by the independent review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: 164 items, 17 routes (a compact Part II of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration and source routes that widen existing layers), and 100 recorded mistakes. Not formalised.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Galois representations for torsion Hecke eigensystems, and middle-degree concentration under decomposed genericity)
items.statement: Let F be a CM field with totally real subfield F^+, and assume that F contains an imaginary quadratic field 𝒦. Let G be an anisotropic unitary similitude group of dimension n for F that is either (a) associated with a central division algebra over F (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties [Kot92a]), or (b) quasi-split at all finite places, under the extra assumptions of §5.1 (footnote 2): F^+ ≠ Q, and every rational prime ramified in F lies in Spl_{F/F^+}, the set of rational primes q such that every place of F^+ above q splits in F. Let X_Γ = Γ\X be the associated locally symmetric space for a torsion-free congruence subgroup Γ; it is compact. Here l_0 = rk G − rk K_∞ = 0, and q_0 = ½ dim_R X is the middle degree. Let m be a system of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in H^i(X_Γ, F_ℓ). Then (1) there is an associated Galois representation ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ). (2) Suppose there is a rational prime p ≠ ℓ such that F is completely decomposed above p, and ρ_m is unramified and decomposed generic (Definition 1.9) at every place of F above p. Then i = q_0. In case (b) the precise form, Theorem 6.3.1 (Case 2, p. 757), also requires the level to be hyperspecial outside a finite set S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+} of primes, so hyperspecial at every prime outside Spl_{F/F^+}.
items.locator: §1, p. 650 (X_Γ, l_0, q_0); Theorem 1.1 and footnote 2, p. 651; Remarks 1.2–1.6, pp. 651–652; §5.1, p. 730; precise form: §6.3, Theorem 6.3.1 and Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3, pp. 756–758
items.note: The precise form is Theorem 6.3.1 (items 120–121). It concerns the compact PEL Shimura variety S_K, which is |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety, attached to PEL data of type A with F = F^+·𝒦 and 𝒦 imaginary quadratic. Case 1: B is a central division algebra over F and V ≅ B. Case 2: B = F, F^+ ≠ Q, G is quasi-split at all finite places, and F/F^+ is split above every rational prime ramified in F. The level is K = K_S K^S, where S is a finite set of primes containing those at which F or G ramifies and K^S is a product of hyperspecial maximal compact subgroups; in Case 2 one also assumes S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+}. Here m is a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra T^S at the primes of Spl_{𝒦/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}). In Theorem 6.3.1, ρ_m is semisimple and unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, with prescribed characteristic polynomials of Frobenius at the places above Spl_{𝒦/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), and the middle degree is dim S_K. Theorem 1.1 is the case of Remark 6.3.2, where Chebotarev lets one take p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}. Remark 1.2: part (1) can also be deduced from [Sch15a], which works at p = ℓ; the proof here works at p ≠ ℓ. Remark 1.4 (no proof): decomposed genericity follows from a big-image assumption, and a prime p as in the theorem also exists for many reducible ρ_m, for example generic sums of characters. Remark 1.5, made precise in Remark 6.3.3: if the signature of G is (0, n) at all infinite places but one, for example the Harris–Taylor signature (1, n − 1), then one finite place v of F at which ρ_m is unramified and decomposed generic suffices. Remark 1.6 records earlier work in the Harris–Taylor case (Shin, Emerton–Gee, Boyer). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator.

items.name: Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1 (integral and twisted coefficients)
items.statement: Suppose that m satisfies the conclusion of Theorem 1.1, that is, H^i(X_Γ, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for all i ≠ q_0. Then H^i(X_Γ, Z_ℓ)_m = 0 for i ≠ q_0, and H^{q_0}(X_Γ, Z_ℓ)_m is torsion-free (Remark 1.3, stated as a formal consequence). Moreover (Remark 1.7.1), Theorem 1.1 remains true when F_ℓ is replaced by a nontrivial Hecke-equivariant coefficient system. The paper says only that the argument uses the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence and Poincaré duality.
items.note: Neither remark is proved in the paper. Remark 1.3 follows from the universal coefficient sequences 0 → H^i(X_Γ, Z_ℓ)_m/ℓ → H^i(X_Γ, F_ℓ)_m → H^{i+1}(X_Γ, Z_ℓ)_m[ℓ] → 0 and Nakayama's lemma for the finitely generated Z_ℓ-modules H^i(X_Γ, Z_ℓ)_m. IG.7 plans the integral and local-system consequences only for the non-compact datum of the sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Definition 1.9 = Definition 6.2.1 (decomposed generic)
items.statement: Let L be a finite extension of Q_p with residue field F_q, and let ℓ ≠ p. A continuous unramified representation ρ̄ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) is decomposed generic if the eigenvalues λ_1, …, λ_n of ρ̄(Frob) satisfy λ_i/λ_j ∉ {1, q} for all i ≠ j. Here Frob ∈ Gal(L̄/L) is an arithmetic Frobenius. The condition depends only on the semisimplification of ρ̄, and it implies that ρ̄ is semisimple. Hence, for a continuous ρ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), the condition that its reduction ρ̄ be decomposed generic is unambiguous.
items.note: Main consequence (Lemma 6.2.2, item 118): every characteristic-zero lift is a sum of characters with non-cyclotomic ratios, and it corresponds to a generic principal series of GL_n(L). The atlas plans this definition only in a special case. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.7 plans, at a completely split auxiliary prime p ≠ ℓ, the residual condition 'α_i,v ≠ p α_j,v for all i≠j and every v|p', which allows repeated eigenvalues. It adds: 'Compare a stronger decomposed-generic API only as a separate specialization.' That stronger specialization is the natural home of Definition 1.9, but AG2.7 has it only over L = Q_p, at the places above a completely split prime. The paper needs the definition over an arbitrary finite extension L of Q_p. Lemma 6.2.2 is stated in that generality, and Theorem 6.3.1(2) (p. 757) imposes the condition at the places 𝔭_i | u of F above a prime p = uu^c that splits in 𝒦 but need not split completely in F, so the residue field of F_{𝔭_i} can be larger than F_p. The definition is therefore missing, and AG2.7's stronger specialization must be widened to arbitrary p-adic fields. The two papers use the same words differently. In Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne (Definition 4.3.1), 'generic' means only α_i/α_j ≠ q, and 'decomposed generic' is a global condition: some prime splits completely and ρ̄ is generic at every place above it. Here the condition is local, and it also excludes λ_i = λ_j. IG.5 and IG.7 use the weaker condition for the non-compact datum of Caraiani–Scholze's sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Sign conventions: covariant Dieudonné theory with Frobenius divided by p, and µ = µ_h with Newton strata indexed by B(G, µ^{-1})
items.statement: The paper uses covariant Dieudonné theory with the usual Frobenius divided by p. This removes the Tate twist in the duality between covariant and contravariant theory (footnote 18: covariant theory becomes the literal dual of contravariant theory with its usual Frobenius). Thus Q_p/Z_p ↦ (Z_p, F = 1) and µ_{p^∞} ↦ (Z_p, F = p^{-1}), instead of the usual (Z_p, F = p) and (Z_p, F = 1). For G over F̄_p: D(G) ⊂ φ_G(D(G)) ⊂ p^{-1}D(G), pφ_G is the usual Frobenius, and the slopes of D(G)[1/p] lie in [−1, 0]. G is isoclinic of slope λ when D(G)[1/p] is isoclinic of slope −λ, so µ_{p^∞} has slope 1. Passing to vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve sends the isocrystal (Q_p, F = p^{-1}) to O(1): E(Q_p/Z_p) = O_X and E(µ_{p^∞}) = O_X(1) (Example 4.1.3). So the usual slope of a p-divisible group equals the slope of its vector bundle. The cocharacter µ = µ_h of a Shimura datum is the standard one (µ(t) = diag(t, 1) for the modular curve), so the Newton strata are indexed by B(G, µ^{-1}).
items.locator: §1, Notation and conventions, p. 659; §4.1, p. 692 (footnote 18), Example 4.1.3
items.note: R07.2 plans Dieudonné modules 'in the covariant or contravariant convention chosen above', with 'Frobenius/Verschiebung, dimensions, heights, slopes'. VB0 is to 'Pin the convention by the standard rank-r block … Compute the slope of its associated bundle and record any sign reversal explicitly'. Dividing the Frobenius by p renormalizes either convention, and the renormalization must be recorded there. The ShimuraData roadmap fixes the same convention for µ_h: h(z) acts on V^{p,q} by z^{-p} z̄^{-q}, and µ_h(z) = h_C(z, 1). IG.0 builds the Newton map into B(G_{Q_p}, µ^{-1}) 'with the sign of mu recorded', for the non-compact datum. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name.

items.name: Shimura data, the Hodge cocharacter, the parabolics P_µ, P^std_µ and the flag varieties
items.statement: Let (G, X) be a Shimura datum: G a reductive group over Q and X a G(R)-conjugacy class of homomorphisms h : Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R such that (1) Ad∘h defines a Hodge structure of type (−1, 1), (0, 0), (1, −1) on Lie G(R), where type (p, q) means that z acts by z^{-p} z̄^{-q}; (2) h(i) is a Cartan involution of G^ad(R); (3) G^ad has no factor defined over Q whose real points form a compact group. The Hodge cocharacter µ = µ_h : G_m → G_C is minuscule; it is obtained by base change to C and restriction to the first factor of G_m. It defines P^std_µ := {g ∈ G : lim_{t→∞} ad(µ(t))g exists}, the stabilizer of the descending filtration Fil^•(µ) on Rep_C(G), where Fil^p(µ) is the sum of the subspaces of type (p', q') with p' ≥ p. The opposite parabolic is P_µ := {g ∈ G : lim_{t→0} ad(µ(t))g exists}, the stabilizer of the ascending filtration Fil_•(µ), where Fil_p(µ) is the sum of the types (p', q') with p' ≤ p. M_µ := Cent_G(µ) is the Levi component of both. The flag varieties Fl^std_{G,µ} and Fl_{G,µ} parametrize parabolics in these two conjugacy classes. Both are defined over the reflex field E, the minimal field of definition of the conjugacy class {µ}. A base point h identifies Fl^std_{G,µ}(C) ≃ G(C)/P^std_µ(C). The Borel embedding β : X ↪ Fl^std_{G,µ}(C), h ↦ Fil^•(µ_h), is holomorphic, and the opposite filtration defines an antiholomorphic embedding X ↪ Fl_{G,µ}(C).
items.note: D3: 'Construct the parabolic stabilizing the Hodge filtration and the compact dual as a flag variety. Prove the Borel embedding … Descend the flag variety of the appropriate parabolic type to the reflex field'. Since P_µ = P^std_{µ^{-1}}, and the conjugacy class of µ^{-1} has the same field of definition E, D3's construction and descent also give Fl_{G,µ}. The antiholomorphic embedding X ↪ Fl_{G,µ}(C), h ↦ Fil_•(µ_h), is not named in D3 and needs its own short argument: Fil_•(µ_h) is, up to reindexing, the complex conjugate of the Hodge filtration. D4: 'Construct the category of Shimura data'. The ShimuraData roadmap uses the same sign convention (h(z) acts on V^{p,q} by z^{-p} z̄^{-q}, µ_h(z) = h_C(z, 1)). Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups Layer 7 plans 'parabolic subgroups and Levi decomposition' and keeps 'the dynamic approach to parabolics/Levi/unipotent radical'. Tau Ceti already has these subgroups as subgroup functors on points, for a cocharacter of an affine group scheme. TauCeti.Cocharacter.parabolic is the set of points g for which t ↦ l(t)gl(t)^{-1} extends over t = 0, so P_µ = P(µ) and P^std_µ = P(µ^{-1}). TauCeti.Cocharacter.levi is the centralizer, so M_µ, and TauCeti.Cocharacter.leviDecompositionMulEquiv is the Levi decomposition. Tau Ceti does not prove representability, or that these subgroups are parabolic, and has nothing on the flag varieties or the Borel embedding. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator, planning stages, library citations.

items.name: Hodge-type Shimura varieties and Siegel embeddings (Example 2.1.1)
items.statement: Example 2.1.1. For g ≥ 1 let (V, ψ) = (Q^{2g}, ψ((a_i), (b_i)) = Σ_{i=1}^{g} (a_i b_{g+i} − a_{g+i} b_i)) be the split symplectic space of dimension 2g over Q, G̃ := GSp(V, ψ), and X̃ the Siegel double space. Fix the self-dual lattice Λ = Z^{2g} ⊂ V. For every h ∈ X̃, the Hodge structure induced by µ_h on V has type (−1, 0), (0, −1), and V^{(−1,0)}/Λ is a complex abelian variety of dimension g. For a neat compact open K̃ ⊂ G̃(A_f), the Shimura variety S̃_K̃ is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K̃ structure. It has a model over its reflex field Q, and carries a universal abelian variety A and the ample line bundle ω, the determinant of the sheaf of invariant differentials of A. The flag variety Fl_{G̃,µ̃} parametrizes the (maximal) totally isotropic subspaces W ⊂ V. A Shimura datum (G, X) is of Hodge type if it admits a closed embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃, X̃) into some Siegel datum. Then S_K (K neat) carries a universal abelian variety, the restriction of the one over S̃_K̃. Fixing such an embedding gives closed embeddings Fl_{G,µ} ↪ Fl_{G̃,µ̃} and Fl^std_{G,µ} ↪ Fl^std_{G̃,µ̃}. By [Del71, Prop. 1.15] there is a compact open K̃ ⊂ G̃(A_f) with K = K̃ ∩ G(A_f) and a closed embedding S_K ↪ S̃_K̃ ⊗_Q E of Shimura varieties over E.
items.note: ShimuraData D4 defines Hodge type ('Define Hodge type by existence of a morphism of data into a Siegel datum with injective group map'), and D5 constructs 'all Siegel data' with their reflex fields and compact duals. PELModuli M1–M2 plan the moduli functors and representability, M3 the complex uniformization, and M5 'Siegel moduli for every dimension'. ShimuraVarieties V5 plans the Siegel canonical model and V6 'the canonical-model inheritance theorem for a Shimura subdatum'. PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S2 plans the comparison of 'finite-level varieties with their Siegel images'. Deligne's closed-embedding statement [Del71, Prop. 1.15] is planned only implicitly, through V6's inheritance theorem and S2. In the printed 'totally isotropic subspaces', the subspaces must be maximal (Lagrangian, of dimension g). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.2 (Scholze: perfectoid Shimura varieties of Hodge type)
items.statement: Let (G, X) be of Hodge type with a fixed embedding into (G̃, X̃), p a prime, 𝔭 a place of E above p, and Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃} the adic space attached to Fl_{G̃,µ̃} ⊗ E_𝔭. The theorem is part of [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1]. (1) For every sufficiently small tame level K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p) there is a perfectoid space 𝒮_{K^p} over E_𝔭 with 𝒮_{K^p} ∼ lim_{K_p} (S_{K^pK_p} ⊗_E E_𝔭)^ad. (2) There is a G(Q_p)-equivariant Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : 𝒮_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}. (3) π_HT is equivariant for the natural Hecke action of G(A_f^p) on the inverse system of the 𝒮_{K^p} and the trivial action of G(A_f^p) on Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}. On points: for an abelian variety A/C of dimension g, the Tate module has the Hodge–Tate decomposition 0 → (Lie A)(1) → T_pA ⊗_{Z_p} C → (Lie A^∨)^∨ → 0. A point x ∈ 𝒮_{K^p}(C, C^+) given by A/C with a symplectic isomorphism T_pA ≅ Z_p^{2g} (and extra structures) maps to the point of Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}(C, C^+) given by the Hodge–Tate filtration Lie(A) ⊂ C^{2g}. The proof of Proposition 6.1.3 (p. 752) also uses [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1(i)] in the following form. Every point x of Fℓ_{G,µ} has an affinoid étale (in fact open) neighbourhood U such that 𝒮_{K^p} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} U is affinoid perfectoid and equals the preimage of an affinoid étale map 𝒮_{K_pK^p,U} → 𝒮_{K_pK^p}, for every sufficiently small K_p.
items.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.2, p. 662; §6.1, proof of Proposition 6.1.3, p. 752
items.note: Part of [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1]; by footnote 8, the setup differs slightly but the proof works verbatim. S1 plans the Siegel tower and 'a covering of the full tower by translates of these affinoid perfectoid pieces'. S2 plans the Hodge-type tower ('Establish perfectoidness and identify the represented tower sheaf'). S3 plans the period map and its equivariance. T2 plans the Hodge–Tate exact sequence and the flag-valued map on the tower with trivialized Tate module. The last sentence of the statement is not part of Theorem 2.1.2 as printed; it records the form of [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1(i)] used in the proof of Proposition 6.1.3. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 1.10 = Theorems 2.1.2(1) and 2.1.3(1) (Hodge-type perfectoid Shimura varieties; π_HT factors through Fℓ_{G,µ})
items.statement: Let (G, X) be a Shimura datum of Hodge type with reflex field E, p a prime, 𝔭 | p a place of E, and Fℓ_{G,µ} the adic space attached to Fl_{G,µ} ⊗_E E_𝔭. For every sufficiently small compact open K^p ⊂ G(A^p_f) there is a perfectoid space S_{K^p} over E_𝔭 with S_{K^p} ∼ lim_{K_p} (S_{K^pK_p} ⊗_E E_𝔭)^ad (Theorem 2.1.2(1), from [Sch15a]). Fix an embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃, X̃) into Siegel data. The Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃} of Theorem 2.1.2(2) factors through the closed embedding Fℓ_{G,µ} ↪ Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}. The resulting map π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} is independent of the embedding, agrees with the map of [Sch15a] in the Siegel case, and is functorial in the Shimura datum.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.10, p. 654; §2.1, Theorems 2.1.2(1) and 2.1.3(1), p. 662; proof of Theorem 2.1.3(1): §2.3, pp. 667–673 (concluded on p. 673)
items.note: The perfectoid space is Theorem 2.1.2(1) (item 7), quoted from [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1]. The G(Q_p)-equivariance of π_HT, and its equivariance for the Hecke action of G(A^p_f) (trivial on the target), are inherited from Theorem 2.1.2(2)–(3). The factorization uses the P_µ-torsor 𝒫_p of Hodge–Tate frames that respect the étale Hodge tensors s_α,p (Lemmas 2.3.6–2.3.7, with [Bla94]). The commutative square on p. 673 is the compatibility with the Siegel embedding G ↪ GSp(V, ψ), which yields the factorization. Functoriality for a general morphism of Shimura data is asserted in Theorem 1.10 and follows from the functoriality of the same torsor construction, but it is not written out. S2 plans the tower: 'Establish perfectoidness and identify the represented tower sheaf … Prove independence of the symplectic embedding'. S3: 'Construct the Hodge–Tate period map on the open perfectoid tower. Prove its equivariance, functoriality under datum morphisms'. T2: 'For Hodge type prove that the tensor conditions cut out the expected flag variety.' Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.3(2) (automorphic vector bundles are pulled back along π_HT)
items.statement: Fix µ in the given conjugacy class, defined over a finite extension of E. Consider the tensor functor f_p : Rep M_µ ↪ Rep P_µ → {G(Q_p)-equivariant vector bundles on Fℓ_{G,µ}} → {G(Q_p)-equivariant vector bundles on 𝒮_{K^p}}. Its first arrow inflates along P_µ ↠ M_µ, and its last arrow is π_HT^*. Then f_p is isomorphic to the tensor functor f_∞ : Rep M_µ ↪ Rep P^std_µ → {automorphic vector bundles on S_K} → {G(Q_p)-equivariant vector bundles on 𝒮_{K^p}}. The isomorphism is independent of the choice of Siegel embedding and equivariant for the Hecke action of G(A_f^p). Remark 2.1.4: one may avoid choosing µ by replacing Rep M_µ with the category of G-equivariant vector bundles on the space of cocharacters conjugate to µ. Once µ is fixed, that space is G/M_µ, and G-equivariant vector bundles on it are representations of M_µ.
items.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.3(2), Remark 2.1.4, pp. 662–663; proof: Lemmas 2.3.5, 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.9, pp. 670–674
items.note: PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S3: 'Prove its equivariance, functoriality under datum morphisms, and pullback identification of the Levi torsor and its associated algebraic automorphic bundles.' HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2: 'compare its Levi torsor with the de Rham/Hodge torsor, and establish Hecke and base-change compatibility.' Both stages are stated for Hodge type, which is the generality of Theorem 2.1.3. The proof in §2.3 combines Lemmas 2.3.5 and 2.3.8 with Proposition 2.3.9, and each of these has its own item. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles and the standard principal bundle
items.statement: A representation ξ of M_µ becomes a representation of P^std_µ by letting the unipotent radical act trivially. Following [Mil90, §III], when the level K is sufficiently small a representation of P^std_µ defines an automorphic vector bundle on S_K, as follows. There is an equivalence of categories ξ ↦ W(ξ) from Rep_C(P^std_µ) to G_C-equivariant vector bundles on Fl^std_{G,µ}, whose inverse takes the fibre at the point corresponding to µ. Restricting W(ξ) along the image of the Borel embedding gives a G(R)-equivariant vector bundle on X. Passing to S_K(C) = G(Q)\(X × G(A_f)/K) gives the automorphic vector bundle V(ξ) := G(Q)\(W(ξ) × G(A_f)/K). The V(ξ) are algebraic, and if ξ is defined over a finite extension E' of E then V(ξ) is defined over E'. Remark 2.1.5: descent to the reflex field uses Milne's standard principal bundle [Mil90, §IV], a G-torsor over S_K that is an intermediate algebraic object between S_K and Fl^std_{G,µ}. In Hodge type it is the G-torsor G_dR of frames of V_dR respecting the tensors s_α,dR (proof of Lemma 2.3.5), with a canonical map G_dR → Fl^std_{G,µ}. Automorphic vector bundles are obtained by pullback from Fl^std_{G,µ} to G_dR followed by descent to S_K [Mil90, Prop. 3.5]. The diagram S_K ← G_dR → Fl^std_{G,µ} is algebraic and has a model over E [Mil90, Thms 4.1, 4.3].
items.note: B0 plans the equivariant bundles on the compact dual and 'the descended analytic bundle at a neat level'. B1 plans 'the canonical principal bundle and its filtration reduction over the appropriate number field', with algebraicity and descent. B2 plans 'the bundle attached to an algebraic representation of the appropriate parabolic/Levi form' and 'its canonical-model descent'. In the proof of Lemma 2.3.5 (p. 671) the paper prints G/P_µ and Fl_{G,µ} where G/P^std_µ and Fl^std_{G,µ} are meant; this misprint is recorded among the paper's mistakes. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator, planning stages.

items.name: Definition 2.2.1 and the structural de Rham sheaves
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(K, O_K), where K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p. The following sheaves on X_proét come from [Sch13c]. The completed structure sheaf is Ô_X. The tilted integral structure sheaf Ô^+_{X♭} is the inverse perfection of Ô^+_X/p (the inverse limit along Frobenius). Definition 2.2.1: (1) B^+_dR,X is the completion of W(Ô^+_{X♭})[1/p] along the kernel of the natural map θ : W(Ô^+_{X♭})[1/p] → Ô_X. (2) B_dR,X = B^+_dR,X[ξ^{−1}] for any ξ generating ker θ. By [Sch13c, Lemma 6.3], such ξ exists pro-étale locally, is not a zero-divisor and is unique up to a unit. The filtration is Fil^i B_dR,X = ξ^i B^+_dR,X, with gr^0 B_dR,X = Ô_X; for X = Spa(C, O_C) one recovers Fontaine's B_dR. OB^+_dR,X is the sheafification of the following presheaf. Let U = Spa(R, R^+) be affinoid perfectoid, with (R, R^+) the completed direct limit of (R_i, R_i^+). The presheaf sends U to the direct limit over i of the completion of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(k)} W(R^{♭+}))[1/p] along the kernel of θ : (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(k)} W(R^{♭+}))[1/p] → R. Finally OB_dR,X := OB^+_dR,X[ξ^{−1}]. Both carry filtrations and connections ∇ : OB^{(+)}_dR,X → OB^{(+)}_dR,X ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X, with (OB^{(+)}_dR)^{∇=0} = B^{(+)}_dR.
items.note: P8:local-rational: 'Construct the rational structural B_dR and crystalline/semistable period sheaves … Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma.' The paper's presheaf uses the completed tensor product R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(k)} W(R^{♭+}), in agreement with the corrected construction that P8 prescribes. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 2.2.2 (Scholze: relative p-adic de Rham comparison)
items.statement: Let π : X → S be a proper smooth morphism of smooth adic spaces over Spa(K, O_K), where K is complete and discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p. Assume R^iπ_*F_p is locally free on S_proét for all i ≥ 0. Then for all i ≥ 0, R^iπ_*Ẑ_p is de Rham in the sense of [Sch13c, Def. 7.5], with associated filtered module with integrable connection R^iπ_dR*O_X (with its Hodge filtration and Gauss–Manin connection). In particular there is an isomorphism R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} OB_dR,S ≅ R^iπ_dR*O_X ⊗_{O_S} OB_dR,S of sheaves on S_proét, compatible with filtrations and connections [Sch13c, Th. 8.8].
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory P8: 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. This is [Sch13c, Thm 8.8] in its relative form, for proper smooth morphisms of smooth adic spaces over K. 'De Rham' is meant in the sense of [Sch13c, Def. 7.5]. By footnote 9 (p. 665), the local-freeness hypothesis holds when π is algebraizable. It was announced in general by Gabber, and with Q_p-coefficients by Kedlaya–Liu. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.3 (Scholze: the two B^+_dR-lattices)
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.2.2, put M = R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} B^+_dR,S ≅ R^iπ_*B^+_dR,X and M_0 = (R^iπ_dR*O_X ⊗_{O_S} OB^+_dR,S)^{∇=0}; the definition of M_0 does not use the Hodge filtration. There is a canonical isomorphism M ⊗_{B^+_dR,S} B_dR,S ≅ M_0 ⊗_{B^+_dR,S} B_dR,S. For every j ∈ Z, (M ∩ Fil^j M_0)/(M ∩ Fil^{j+1} M_0) = (Fil^{−j} R^iπ_dR*O_X) ⊗_{O_S} Ô_S(j) ⊂ gr^j M_0 = R^iπ_dR*O_X ⊗_{O_S} Ô_S(j). In particular M_0 ⊂ M [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9].
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory P8: 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. Proposition 2.2.3 is [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9]. The paper presents it as a reformulation of the condition that R^iπ_*Ẑ_p and R^iπ_dR*O_X are associated (p. 665), which is what Theorem 2.2.2 asserts. It is therefore part of that comparison. The relative Hodge–Tate filtration with Corollary 2.2.4, and Proposition 2.2.5, are derived from it and have their own items. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: The relative Hodge–Tate filtration and Corollary 2.2.4
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.2.2, the relative Hodge–Tate filtration is the ascending filtration on gr^0 M = R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S given by Fil_{−j}(R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S) = (M ∩ Fil^j M_0)/(Fil^1 M ∩ Fil^j M_0). Here Fil_{−1} = 0, and Fil_i, with i the cohomological degree, is everything. Corollary 2.2.4: for all j ≥ 0 there are canonical isomorphisms gr_j(R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S) ≅ (gr^j R^iπ_dR*O_X) ⊗_{O_S} Ô_S(−j). In particular Fil_0(R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S) = R^iπ_*O_X ⊗_{O_S} Ô_S.
items.note: Generalizes the degree-one Hodge–Tate filtration of [Sch15a] (and that of [Sch13d, §3] over a geometric point) to proper smooth families in every degree. No layer plans this general statement. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2 plans only the degree-one abelian case ('the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site'). HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison ('Derive the Hodge–Tate filtration from the two de Rham lattices') plans only the logarithmic version, for the canonical local systems of Shimura varieties. The paper applies the construction to V_p and its tensor constructions. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.5 (the first step of the relative Hodge–Tate filtration)
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 2.2.2, the first step Fil_0 of the relative Hodge–Tate filtration is given by the natural map R^iπ_*O_X ⊗_{O_S} Ô_S → R^iπ_*Ô_X ≅ R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S, and this map is injective. In [Sch15a], only this first step, for i = 1, was used, and it was defined as this natural map.
items.note: No layer plans this statement in every degree. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2 plans only the degree-one abelian case ('Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site'). T6:comparison plans only the logarithmic version, for canonical local systems. The proof (pp. 666–667) uses two inputs. The first is the relative Poincaré lemma, which has its own item; it identifies M ⊗_{B^+_dR,S} OB^+_dR,S with R^iπ_dR*OB^+_dR,X. The second is the primitive comparison R^iπ_*Ô_X ≅ R^iπ_*Ẑ_{p,X} ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,S}} Ô_S, which PadicHodgeTheory P8 must state as an input of the proper comparison. Injectivity follows from the description of the graded pieces in Corollary 2.2.4. The printed proof writes f for π. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Hodge tensors and the torsors of frames (Lemma 2.3.1)
items.statement: Let (G, X) ↪ (G̃, X̃) be an embedding of Shimura data with G̃ = GSp(V, ψ), and V^⊗ := ⊕_{r,s∈N} V^{⊗r} ⊗ (V^∨)^{⊗s}. By [DMOS82, Prop. 3.1], G ⊂ G̃ is the pointwise stabilizer of a finite collection of tensors (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗. Let A → S_K be the pullback of the universal abelian scheme along S_K ↪ S̃_K̃ ⊗_Q E. Its first relative Betti homology V_B (the dual of R^1π^an_*Q) is a local system of Q-vector spaces on S_K(C). It is identified with the local system given by the G(Q)-representation V and the G(Q)-torsor X × G(A_f)/K → S_K(C). The G(Q)-invariant s_α give global sections (s_α,B) ⊂ V_B^⊗, which are Hodge tensors. Lemma 2.3.1: this G(Q)-torsor is identified with the G(Q)-torsor sending U ⊂ S_K(C) to {β : V × U ≅ V_B|_U | β(s_α) = s_α,B}. For a second symplectic embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃', X̃') with G̃' = GSp(V', ψ'), there is a G-invariant idempotent e ∈ V^⊗ with V' = eV^⊗. Through e, G-invariant tensors in (V')^⊗ transfer to V^⊗, and V'_B = eV_B^⊗ compatibly with the Hodge structures. e is assumed, after adjoining it if necessary, to belong to the family (s_α).
items.note: B1: 'In Hodge type, construct the tensor description using the Betti, de Rham, and étale realizations of Hodge tensors.' The input [DMOS82, Prop. 3.1] has its own item: a reductive subgroup of GL(V) in characteristic zero is the pointwise stabilizer of finitely many tensors. No layer plans it. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2 and Remark 2.3.3 (Kisin, Deligne: de Rham and étale Hodge tensors are defined over E)
items.statement: Let V_dR := (R^1π_dR*O_A)^∨ be the first relative de Rham homology of A, a vector bundle on S_K with integrable connection. Two inputs make the Betti tensors algebraic de Rham tensors. The first is the relative de Rham comparison V^an_dR,C ≅ V_B ⊗_Q O_{S_K(C)}, compatible with the connection. The second is Deligne's equivalence between algebraic vector bundles with regular singular flat connection and analytic vector bundles with flat connection [Del70]. Through them the s_α,B give horizontal sections s_α,dR of (V^an_dR,C)^⊗, and these are algebraic: s_α,dR ⊂ V^⊗_dR,C. Lemma 2.3.2 [Kis10]: the tensors s_α,dR in V^⊗_dR,C are defined over E. Remark 2.3.3: take a second symplectic embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃', X̃'), G̃' = GSp(V', ψ'), with idempotent e ∈ V^⊗ such that V' = eV^⊗. Applying Lemma 2.3.2 to G ↪ GSp(V ⊕ V', ψ ⊕ ψ') shows that the isomorphism V'_dR,C ≅ e_dR V^⊗_dR,C is defined over E. Likewise, let V_p be the Q_p-local system on S_K given by the first relative p-adic étale homology of A. Then the Hodge tensors (s_α,p) ⊂ V_p^⊗ coming from the Betti–étale comparison over C are defined over E.
items.note: [Kis10], via Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolute Hodge [DMOS82], which has its own item. The proof works one component at a time. The Galois group Gal(κ̄/κ) of the function field acts on H^1_ét through K_p ⊂ G(Q_p), so it fixes the G(Q_p)-invariant s_α,p,x. AutomorphicBundles B1 plans the result: 'In Hodge type, construct the tensor description using the Betti, de Rham, and étale realizations of Hodge tensors. Prove the required absolute-Hodge and comparison statements rather than identifying arbitrary Hodge classes with algebraic cycles.' The horizontal sections s_α,dR are algebraic (p. 668) by Deligne's equivalence for flat connections with regular singular points [Del70]. That equivalence has its own item, and no layer plans it over bases of dimension greater than one. When S_K is proper, as in the paper's main theorems, proper GAGA (ComplexComparisonPartII C3) already shows that these sections are algebraic. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Lemmas 2.3.4–2.3.5 (the de Rham torsors P_dR and M_dR)
items.statement: Choose µ in the conjugacy class, defined over a finite extension E'/E, and base change everything to E'. P^std_µ is the stabilizer in G of the descending filtration Fil^•_µ that µ induces on V. The P^std_µ-torsor P_dR over S_K is P_dR(U) = {β : V_dR|_U ≅ V ⊗_Q O_U | β(s_α,dR) = s_α ⊗ 1, β(Fil^•) = Fil^•_µ}, where Fil^• is the Hodge filtration. Such β exist because the Betti–de Rham comparison respects the Hodge filtrations and matches s_α with s_α,dR. Lemma 2.3.4: P_dR is independent of the choice of symplectic embedding G ↪ GSp(V, ψ), via the isomorphism V'_dR ≅ e_dR V_dR^⊗ of Remark 2.3.3. Hence so is the M_µ-torsor M_dR = P_dR ×^{P^std_µ} M_µ, the pushout along P^std_µ ↠ M_µ. It trivializes the graded pieces of the Hodge filtration and, by the Tannakian formalism, is a tensor functor from Rep M_µ to vector bundles on S_K. Lemma 2.3.5: M_dR encodes the tensor functor f_∞ : Rep M_µ → {automorphic vector bundles on S_K} of Theorem 2.1.3. In the proof, the pushout G_dR = P_dR ×^{P^std_µ} G (frames of V_dR respecting the s_α,dR) is Milne's standard principal bundle, with its canonical map to Fl^std_{G,µ}.
items.note: AutomorphicBundles B1: 'Construct the canonical principal bundle and its filtration reduction over the appropriate number field' and 'In Hodge type, construct the tensor description using the Betti, de Rham, and étale realizations of Hodge tensors'. Here G_dR is the canonical principal bundle in its Hodge-type tensor description, and P_dR is its reduction to P^std_µ. Lemma 2.3.4 compares the tensor descriptions coming from two symplectic embeddings. AutomorphicBundles B2: 'Define the bundle attached to an algebraic representation of the appropriate parabolic/Levi form, construct its canonical-model descent'; this is Lemma 2.3.5. The printed text differs in two places, and the statement uses the corrected forms. On p. 670, M_dR is obtained 'from the projection P_µ ↠ M_µ'. But P_dR is a P^std_µ-torsor and the displayed pushout is taken over P^std_µ, so the projection must be P^std_µ ↠ M_µ. On p. 671, G/P_µ and Fl_{G,µ} are printed where G/P^std_µ and Fl^std_{G,µ} are meant. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Blasius: Hodge tensors under the p-adic comparison
items.statement: [Bla94] Let A be an abelian variety over a number field with a Hodge cycle, which is absolute Hodge by Deligne. The p-adic de Rham comparison isomorphism at a place above p carries the p-adic étale component of the cycle to its de Rham component. The paper uses this in the following form. At points of S_K corresponding to abelian varieties defined over number fields, the p-adic de Rham comparison matches s_α,dR with s_α,p (and e_dR with e_p). So at such points s_α,p corresponds to s_α under the Hodge–Tate decomposition. Since these tensors are horizontal sections, the matching holds on all of the adic space 𝒮_K once it is checked at one such point in each connected component of 𝒮_K.
items.note: T1: 'For the Hodge-type application prove compatibility of Hodge tensors with the comparison maps.' This is the statement in the form the paper uses, for the tensors s_α,dR and s_α,p (and e_dR, e_p) on a Hodge-type Shimura variety. Its natural proof is Blasius's theorem at the points defined over number fields, extended to all of 𝒮_K by horizontality. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemmas 2.3.6–2.3.7 (the Hodge–Tate torsor P_p)
items.statement: Let 𝒮_K be the adic space attached to S_K ⊗_E E_𝔭 (after the base change to E' made on p. 669). Let V_p be the Q_p-local system on S_K given by the first relative p-adic étale homology of A, which is the dual of R^1π_*Q_p (p. 669). Pulled back to 𝒮_K, it is a locally free Q̂_p-module on (𝒮_K)_proét. Its relative Hodge–Tate filtration Fil_• on V_p ⊗_{Q̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K} is dual to the relative Hodge–Tate filtration of §2.2 on R^1π_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_{𝒮_K} (the case i = 1): Fil_k is the annihilator of Fil_{−k−1}. At a point given by A/C this filtration is Fil_{−1} = (Lie A)(1) ⊂ T_pA ⊗ C, as on p. 662. It is extended to V_p^⊗ by tensor operations. Regard P_µ as the group U ↦ P_µ(Ô_{𝒮_K}(U)) on (𝒮_K)_proét; note that it is defined with the completed structure sheaf. Set P_p(U) = {β : V_p ⊗_{Q̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U ≅ V ⊗_Q Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U | β(s_α,p ⊗ 1) = s_α ⊗ 1, β(Fil_•) = Fil_•(µ)}, where Fil_•(µ) is the ascending filtration determined by µ on V. Lemma 2.3.6: P_p is a P_µ-torsor. The proof has three steps. First, drop the filtration condition. This gives the G-quasitorsor G_p, the pushout of the G(Q̂_p)-torsor of tensor-preserving isomorphisms V_p ≅ V ⊗_{Q_p} Q̂_p. G_p is a torsor because it has a section over 𝒮_{K^p}. Second, the type of the Hodge–Tate filtration is a discrete invariant, hence constant on each connected component of 𝒮_K, so it suffices to check classical points. Third, let x ∈ 𝒮_K(L, O_L), where L is a finite extension of E_𝔭, let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of L, and pick a point of M_dR(C) above x. Let V = ⊕_j V_j be the weight decomposition of µ, and fix p-power roots of unity in C. The Hodge–Tate decomposition V_{p,x} ⊗_{Q_p} C ≅ ⊕_j V_j ⊗ C(−j) ≅ V ⊗ C takes the Hodge–Tate filtration to Fil_•(µ), and it takes s_α,p to s_α. When x comes from an abelian variety over a number field, the second assertion is Blasius's theorem [Bla94]. The other classical points are reduced to that case by the horizontality argument of the proofs of Lemma 2.3.7 and Proposition 2.3.9. Lemma 2.3.7: P_p is independent of the choice of symplectic embedding. Take a second embedding G ↪ GSp(V', ψ') with idempotent e ∈ V^⊗. The p-adic realization e_p ∈ V_p^⊗ of e gives an isomorphism V'_p ⊗ Ô_{𝒮_K} ≅ e_p(V_p^⊗ ⊗ Ô_{𝒮_K}) matching the tensors. This isomorphism respects the Hodge–Tate filtrations because e_p is the image of e_dR under the p-adic de Rham comparison. This holds at points coming from number fields by [Bla94], and then on all of 𝒮_K by horizontality. Hence the isomorphism induces P_p ≅ P'_p. The inflation G_p = P_p ×^{P_µ} G is U ↦ {β : V_p ⊗_{Q̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U ≅ V ⊗_Q Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U | β(s_α,p ⊗ 1) = s_α ⊗ 1}. The perfectoid Shimura variety 𝒮_{K^p} is a K_p-torsor in (𝒮_K)_proét. G_p(𝒮_{K^p}) has a canonical section, the trivialization of the p-adic Tate module of A over 𝒮_{K^p}, which respects the s_α,p. Write Fℓ_{G,µ} also for the sheaf U ↦ Fℓ_{G,µ}(U) on (𝒮_K)_proét. P_p defines a map G_p → Fℓ_{G,µ}, which is independent of the embedding by Lemma 2.3.7. Together with the canonical section it gives an element of Fℓ_{G,µ}(𝒮_{K^p}), that is, the map π_HT : 𝒮_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} of Theorem 2.1.3(1).
items.locator: §2.3, definition of V_p, p. 669; Lemmas 2.3.6–2.3.7 and the construction of π_HT, pp. 671–673
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2: 'Construct the Hodge–Tate parabolic reduction and Levi torsor' and 'For Hodge type prove that the tensor conditions cut out the expected flag variety'. T2 also plans 'Construct the universal flag-valued map on a tower where the Tate module is trivialized', which is the construction of π_HT from P_p and the canonical section. The filtration used is that of Corollary 2.2.4 for i = 1, dualized and extended to tensors; that corollary has its own item. The printed text differs in one place. V_p is defined as the first relative p-adic étale homology of A (p. 669), but p. 671 calls it 'the relative p-adic étale cohomology'. The homology is meant, and the Hodge–Tate filtration on it is the dual filtration, whose indexing is what makes it correspond to Fil_•(µ). Blasius's theorem [Bla94] concerns abelian varieties over number fields. The proof of Lemma 2.3.6 (p. 672), however, invokes it at every classical point x ∈ 𝒮_K(L, O_L) with L finite over E_𝔭. At the other classical points, the matching of s_α,p with s_α rests on the horizontality argument that the paper gives only later, in the proofs of Lemma 2.3.7 (p. 672) and Proposition 2.3.9 (p. 674). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.8 and Proposition 2.3.9 (M_dR ≅ M_p)
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.8: the M_µ-torsor M_p = P_p ×^{P_µ} M_µ, the pushout along P_µ ↠ M_µ, encodes the tensor functor f_p of Theorem 2.1.3; the paper says the proof is immediate from the definitions. As a sheaf on (𝒮_K)_proét, M_p(U) = {β : gr_•(V_p ⊗_{Q̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K})|_U ≅ gr_•(µ)(V ⊗_Q Ô_{𝒮_K})|_U | β(s_α,p ⊗ 1) = s_α ⊗ 1}. Let 𝒫_dR be the P^std_µ-torsor on (𝒮_K)_proét given by U ↦ {β : V_dR ⊗_{O_{𝒮_K}} Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U ≅ V ⊗_Q Ô_{𝒮_K}|_U | β(s_α,dR ⊗ 1) = s_α ⊗ 1, β(Fil^•) = Fil^•(µ)}, where Fil^• is the Hodge–de Rham filtration. It is the pullback of P_dR from S_K, ringed by O_{S_K}, to (𝒮_K)_proét, ringed by Ô_{𝒮_K}. Its pushout 𝓜_dR to M_µ is the pullback of M_dR. It parametrizes the isomorphisms gr^•(V_dR ⊗ Ô_{𝒮_K}) ≅ gr^•(µ)(V ⊗ Ô_{𝒮_K}) that send s_α,dR to s_α. Proposition 2.3.9: there is a canonical isomorphism 𝓜_dR ≅ M_p of M_µ-torsors on (𝒮_K)_proét, independent of the choice of symplectic embedding. The proof uses three facts. First, the similitude character GSp(V, ψ) → G_m gives rise geometrically to the Tate motive and is independent of the choice of symplectic embedding. Through it, both torsors map to the torsor of trivializations Ô_{𝒮_K}(1) ≅ Ô_{𝒮_K}. Second, for every j ∈ Z the relative p-adic de Rham comparison gives an isomorphism gr^j(V_dR ⊗_{O_{𝒮_K}} Ô_{𝒮_K}) ≅ gr_j(V_p ⊗_{Q̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K})(j). This is Corollary 2.2.4 for i = 1, dualized, because V_dR and V_p are the duals of R^1π_dR*O_A and R^1π_*Q_p. The same holds for V_dR^⊗ and V_p^⊗. Third, by [Bla94] the tensors s_α,dR and s_α,p are matched at points defined over number fields, and hence everywhere. From these isomorphisms and the trivialization Ô_{𝒮_K}(1) ≅ Ô_{𝒮_K} one writes down 𝓜_dR ≅ M_p; independence of the embedding is checked as in Lemmas 2.3.4 and 2.3.7. Through the Tannakian formalism of Lemmas 2.3.5 and 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.9 gives Theorem 2.1.3(2).
items.locator: §2.3, the torsor M_p, p. 672; Lemma 2.3.8 and Proposition 2.3.9, pp. 673–674
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2: 'compare its Levi torsor with the de Rham/Hodge torsor'. PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S3: 'pullback identification of the Levi torsor and its associated algebraic automorphic bundles'. Both stages are stated for Hodge type. The graded comparison is Corollary 2.2.4 for i = 1, dualized and extended to tensors. That corollary has its own item and belongs in PadicHodgeTheory P8, which T2 reaches through T1. The tensor matching is Blasius's theorem [Bla94], which has its own item. The printed text differs in one place. The proof on p. 674 says 'The determinant representation GSp(V, ψ) → G_m gives rise geometrically to the Tate motive'. The character meant is the similitude character: the determinant is its g-th power and would give Ô_{𝒮_K}(g), not Ô_{𝒮_K}(1). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 (isocrystals over F̄_p)
items.statement: An isocrystal over F̄_p is a pair (V, φ) consisting of a finite-dimensional vector space V over L = W(F̄_p)[1/p] and a σ-linear automorphism φ of V, where σ is the automorphism of L induced by the p-th power Frobenius of F̄_p. Its height is dim_L V.
items.note: At the pinned commit, Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal p k V` is a module over K(p, k) = FractionRing (𝕎 k) together with a Frobenius-semilinear automorphism `frob : V ≃ᶠˡ[p, k] V`. For k = F̄_p, K(p, k) is W(F̄_p)[1/p] = L and its Frobenius is σ. The class imposes no finiteness condition, so Definition 3.1.1 is `[Isocrystal p k V] [FiniteDimensional K(p, k) V]`, and the height is `Module.finrank K(p, k) V`. Morphisms and isomorphisms are `WittVector.IsocrystalHom` and `WittVector.IsocrystalEquiv`. The height-one classification `WittVector.isocrystal_classification` belongs to the Dieudonné–Manin item. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, library citations.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification
items.statement: Every isocrystal (V, φ) over F̄_p is isomorphic to a unique isocrystal of the form ⊕_{λ ∈ Q} V_λ^{⊕n_λ}. Here λ = s/r runs over the rational numbers written in lowest terms with r > 0, and the n_λ are nonnegative integers, almost all zero. Also V_λ = (L^r, A_λσ), where A_λ is the r × r matrix with entries 1 in positions (i, i + 1) for 1 ≤ i < r, p^s in position (r, 1) and 0 elsewhere; thus (A_λσ)^r = p^sσ^r. The subspaces V_λ^{⊕n_λ} ⊂ V (the part of slope λ) are uniquely determined. Consequently B(GL_n) is in bijection with the Newton polygons of height n, via the slope decomposition.
items.note: VB0: 'Prove the Dieudonné–Manin classification after the stipulated algebraically closed residue base, including simple objects of rational slope, multiplicities'. VB0 pins the convention 'by the standard rank-r block with Frobenius r-th power pi^s sigma^r', which here is (A_λσ)^r = p^sσ^r. Mathlib has the height-one case. `WittVector.isocrystal_classification` (k algebraically closed, `finrank K(p, k) V = 1`) gives an isomorphism with `WittVector.StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k m`, which is the isocrystal (K(p, k), p^mσ) = V_m in the paper's normalisation. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Isocrystals with G-structure and the set B(G)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, and let L and σ be as in Definition 3.1.1. B(G) is the set of σ-conjugacy classes of elements b ∈ G(L), where b ~ hbσ(h)^{-1} for h ∈ G(L). By Kottwitz, B(G) does not change if F̄_p is replaced by any algebraically closed field of characteristic p. An isocrystal with G-structure is an exact tensor functor Rep_{Q_p}G → {isocrystals over F̄_p}. B(G) is in bijection with the isomorphism classes of isocrystals with G-structure; for G = GL_n the bijection is b ↦ (L^n, bσ), onto isocrystals of height n. The Galois cohomology H^1(Q_p, G) is identified with the isomorphism classes of exact tensor functors Rep_{Q_p}G → {Q_p-vector spaces}. These embed fully faithfully into isocrystals with G-structure through W ↦ W ⊗_{Q_p} L with the Frobenius of L. The induced injection H^1(Q_p, G) ↪ B(G) has image exactly the classes b with trivial Newton point ν_b [Kot85].
items.note: BG0: 'Define B(G) as sigma-conjugacy classes in G(E-breve), with relation b' = g b sigma(g)^(-1), and compare with isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals.' The characterisation of H^1(Q_p, G) as the classes with trivial ν is covered at most by BG1: 'Prove the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) used in FS III, including basic classes, the centralizer Levi and the comparison with the torsor kernel.' No stage names H^1(Q_p, G) explicitly. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: The Newton map, the Kottwitz map and B(G, µ) (Definition 3.1.2)
items.statement: Fix a splitting of G_{Q̄_p}, a maximal torus T ⊂ G_{Q̄_p}, and X_*(G) = X_*(T) with its dominant chamber. Let Γ = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) and π_1(G) = π_1(G_{Q̄_p}). Kottwitz attaches to b ∈ G(L) a slope homomorphism ν_b ∈ Hom(D_L, G_L), where D is the pro-torus with character group Q. For GL_n this is the slope decomposition; in general it comes from the Tannakian formalism. The conjugacy class of ν_b is σ-invariant and depends only on the σ-conjugacy class of b. This gives the Newton map ν : B(G) → (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom, where (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)_dom is identified with the conjugacy classes in Hom(D_{Q̄_p}, G_{Q̄_p}). The Kottwitz map κ : B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ is the unique natural transformation B(·) → π_1(·)_Γ of set-valued functors on connected reductive groups over Q_p with κ(b) = val_p(det b) for GL_n. By [RR96, Thm 1.15], the image of ν_b in π_1(G)^Γ ⊗ Q equals the Galois average of κ(b). Kottwitz proves that (ν, κ) : B(G) → (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom × π_1(G)_Γ is injective. On (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom, ν ⪯ ν' means that ν' − ν is a nonnegative rational linear combination of positive coroots. On B(G), b ⪯ b' means ν_b ⪯ ν_{b'} and κ(b) = κ(b'). Identify a conjugacy class µ of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} with an element of X_*(G)_dom. Let µ̄ = [E' : Q_p]^{-1} Σ_{γ ∈ Gal(E'/Q_p)} γ(µ) ∈ (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom, for E' large enough, and let µ♭ be the image of µ in π_1(G)_Γ. Definition 3.1.2: the set of µ-admissible elements is B(G, µ) = {b ∈ B(G) : ν_b ⪯ µ̄ and κ(b) = µ♭}. The paper works with B(G, µ^{-1}), where µ^{-1} denotes a dominant representative of the inverse of µ.
items.note: BG1: 'Construct pi_1(G), its Galois coinvariants, the Kottwitz map kappa and rational dominant Newton cocharacter nu … Define the partial order with equal kappa and the dominance comparison of Newton points, pinning its orientation.' The injectivity of (ν, κ) falls under BG1's 'classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G)'. BG1 does not name the Galois average µ̄, the class µ♭ or the set B(G, µ). These are one-line definitions from BG1's data, and BG1's blueprint should state them, because B(G, µ^{-1}) indexes the strata of Theorem 1.11. IG.0 uses B(G_{Q_p}, µ^{-1}) only for the split datum of the non-compact sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 (the rational annuli Y_I are preperfectoid affinoids)
items.statement: Let F be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p, and ϖ ∈ F with 0 < |ϖ| < 1. Let Y_(0,∞) = Spa(W(O_F), W(O_F)) ∖ {p[ϖ] = 0}, with W(O_F) given the (p, [ϖ])-adic topology. The map α : Y_(0,∞) → (0, ∞), α(x) = log|[ϖ](x̃)| / log|p(x̃)|, where x̃ is the maximal generalization of x, is continuous. For an interval I, Y_I is the interior of α^{-1}(I). For every closed interval I = [s, r] ⊂ (0, ∞) with r, s ∈ Q, the space Y_I = Spa(R^{[s,r]}_F, R^{[s,r],+}_F) is a sheafy affinoid adic space. Here R^{[s,r],+}_F is the p-adic completion of the integral closure of W(O_F)[p/[ϖ^{1/r}], [ϖ^{1/s}]/p] in W(O_F)[p/[ϖ^{1/r}], [ϖ^{1/s}]/p][1/p], and R^{[s,r]}_F = R^{[s,r],+}_F[1/p]. More precisely, R^{[s,r]}_F is preperfectoid: R^{[s,r]}_F ⊗̂_{Q_p} K is a perfectoid K-algebra for every perfectoid field K/Q_p. In particular, Y_(0,∞) is an honest adic space.
items.note: Layer 6 of the Tau Ceti adic-spaces roadmap constructs 𝒴 = D(p) ∩ D([ϖ]) for any complete rank-one perfect nonarchimedean field F of characteristic p, not necessarily algebraically closed. It gives the radius inequalities order-theoretically, without a real-valued α at higher-rank points. It also constructs Kedlaya's interval rings B^I, whose plus ring 'agrees with the integral closure of the image of the appropriate localised A_inf plus ring', and these are sheafy by its Layer 4. RF0:annuli: 'construct Y_S = 𝒴_S \ V(pi), the open where pi[varpi] is nonzero, and the annulus rings with their explicit plus subrings. Prove complete separated sheafiness'. RF0:integral-Y proves the charts perfectoid only 'after the specified completed extension O_E→O_(E∞)', where E∞ is the completion of E(π^{1/p^∞}). No stage states that R^{[s,r]}_F ⊗̂_{Q_p} K is perfectoid for every perfectoid field K/Q_p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Definition 3.2.2 (the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve) and the point ∞
items.statement: Let F be as in Proposition 3.2.1. The Witt-vector lift ϕ of the Frobenius of O_F acts on Y_(0,∞). The map α is ϕ-equivariant when ϕ acts on (0, ∞) by multiplication by p, so the action is properly discontinuous. The adic Fargues–Fontaine curve is 𝒳_F = Y_(0,∞)/ϕ^Z (Definition 3.2.2). Now let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extension of Q_p and F = C♭. Fontaine's map θ : W(O_F) → O_C defines a (C, O_C)-point of Y_(0,∞), hence a point ∞ ∈ 𝒳_F(C, O_C) with inclusion i_∞ : Spa(C, O_C) → 𝒳_F. The point ∞ is closed with residue field C. The completed local ring of 𝒳_F at ∞ is B^+_dR,C, the ker θ-adic completion of W(O_F)[1/p], which is a complete discrete valuation ring.
items.note: Layer 6 of the Tau Ceti adic-spaces roadmap: 'Define the quotient topological space 𝒳 = 𝒴 / φ^ℤ', with its structure sheaf. RF1: 'the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z'. RF2:untilts: 'Construct marked untilts over E, the primitive kernel of theta, and its divisor on Y_S and X_S … Construct completion along a divisor, B_dR^+ … At a geometric untilt identify the complete discrete valuation ring and its residue field.' Mathlib has the ring itself. `BDeRhamPlus` is the ker θ-adic completion of W(R♭)[1/p] for a p-adically complete ring R, built with `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, and for R = O_C it is B^+_dR,C. That it is a discrete valuation ring is not proved there. The printed Definition 3.2.2 reads 'The adic Fargues-Fontaine curve is y 𝒳_F = Y_(0,∞)/ϕ^Z' with a stray 'y'; arXiv v1 reads 'is given by' (p. 679). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.3 (Fargues–Fontaine: classification of vector bundles)
items.statement: Let F be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p, with a chosen embedding F̄_p → O_F. This gives a structure map Y_(0,∞) → Spa(L, O_L). Pull an isocrystal (V, φ_V) back to a vector bundle on Y_(0,∞) with a ϕ-linear automorphism, and descend it to a vector bundle E(V) on 𝒳_F. Then V ↦ E(V) induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of isocrystals over F̄_p and isomorphism classes of vector bundles on 𝒳_F [FF14] (Theorem 3.2.3). Fargues–Fontaine prove this for the schematic curve, and the adic statement follows by GAGA ([KL15], [Far15b]) (Remark 3.2.4). The functor is not an equivalence of categories: in general there are nonzero maps between bundles of different slopes.
items.note: VB2:classification: 'The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes; it is not asserted fully faithful onto all bundle morphisms.' VB1: 'Construct the isocrystal-to-bundle functor'. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Definition 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6 (O(d), degree and slopes)
items.statement: For d ∈ Z, O_{𝒳_F}(d) is the line bundle attached to the isocrystal (L, p^{-d}σ) (Definition 3.2.5). By Theorem 3.2.3, d ↦ O(d) is an isomorphism Z ≅ Pic 𝒳_F. The degree of a vector bundle is the degree of its determinant; this gives slopes and Harder–Narasimhan filtrations. The slopes of an isocrystal V and of the bundle E(V) differ by a sign (Remark 3.2.6).
items.note: RF3: 'Define O(1) by Frobenius descent with the chosen pi-normalization; construct O(n) … Prove the sign conversion between Frobenius eigenvalue and degree.' VB1: 'Build degree, rank, slope, saturated subbundles and semistability.' VB2:classification: 'every bundle at a geometric point is a direct sum of the stable O(lambda)', which gives Pic 𝒳_F ≅ Z, together with 'Hom/Ext vanishing … needed for HN filtrations'. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.7 (Fargues–Fontaine: the schematic curve)
items.statement: Let X_F = Proj(⊕_{d≥0} H^0(𝒳_F, O(d))). There is a natural map of locally ringed spaces 𝒳_F → X_F, and pullback along it is an equivalence between vector bundles on X_F and on 𝒳_F ([KL15], [Far15b]). Theorem 3.2.7 [FF14]: X_F is a regular noetherian scheme of Krull dimension 1 with field of constants Q_p. Its residue fields at closed points are the algebraically closed complete extensions C of Q_p with C♭ ≅ F. For every closed point x, X_F ∖ {x} is the spectrum of a principal ideal domain.
items.note: VB2:ampleness: 'For S a geometric perfectoid point, prove regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve, its local principal-ideal properties and the closed-point description' and 'Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3'. RF3: 'Form the graded algebra of global sections for affinoid S and construct Proj and the analytic-to-schematic map of locally ringed spaces'. VB1 computes the sections of O(n), in particular that the field of constants is Q_p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Definition 3.2.8 and Theorem 3.2.9 (Fargues: G-bundles on the curve)
items.statement: Let F be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p, with a chosen embedding F̄_p → O_F, and let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p. A G-bundle on X_F (or on 𝒳_F) is an exact tensor functor Rep_{Q_p}G → Bun_{X_F} ≅ Bun_{𝒳_F} (Definition 3.2.8). Composing with the functor V ↦ E(V) from isocrystals over F̄_p to vector bundles (Theorem 3.2.3) gives a functor b ↦ E_b from isocrystals with G-structure to G-bundles on X_F. Theorem 3.2.9 [Far15a]: this functor induces a bijection on isomorphism classes; that is, every G-bundle on X_F is isomorphic to E_b for a unique b ∈ B(G).
items.note: BG0: 'Construct G-torsors on the existing sousperfectoid spaces and curve, and prove the comparison between geometric étale torsors, étale sheaf torsors, and exact tensor functors Rep_E(G) → vector bundles', and 'Define B(G) … and compare with isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals'. BG2:uniformization: 'Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence and the kappa/nu formulas … This explicitly includes the non-simply-connected derived-group case.' A point of |Bun_G| is represented by a G-bundle on the curve of an algebraically closed perfectoid field of characteristic p, so this bijection is Theorem 3.2.9 for every connected reductive G over Q_p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: The Robba rings and Kedlaya–Liu's comparison of bundles with ϕ-modules (Theorems 3.2.13 and 3.3.4)
items.statement: Absolute case. Let F be complete algebraically closed of characteristic p. The Robba ring is R̃_F = lim_{→r} R̃^r_F, where R̃^r_F = H^0(Y_(0,r], O) (Definition 3.2.10). The ring R̃^r_F is the inverse limit of the Banach algebras R̃^{[s,r]}_F over s ∈ (0, r]. Equivalently, it is the Fréchet completion of W(O_F)⟨p/[ϖ]^{1/r}⟩[1/p] = {Σ_{n>−∞} [c_n]p^n : c_n ∈ F, c_nϖ^{n/r} → 0} for the norms max_n |c_nϖ^{n/s}|, s ∈ (0, r] [KL15, Def. 4.2.2]. ϕ induces isomorphisms R̃^r_F ≅ R̃^{r/p}_F, hence an automorphism of R̃_F. A ϕ-module over R̃_F is a finite projective R̃_F-module with a ϕ-linear automorphism (Definition 3.2.11). R̃_F is a Bézout domain [KL15, Lemma 4.2.6], so every ϕ-module is finite free (Remark 3.2.12). Vector bundles on 𝒳_F are equivalent to ϕ-modules over R̃_F [KL15, Thm 6.3.12] (Theorem 3.2.13). Relative case. Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid algebra of characteristic p. Let R̃^r_R be the inverse limit of the Banach algebras R̃^{[s,r]}_R over s ∈ (0, r], and let the relative Robba ring be R̃_R = lim_{→r>0} R̃^r_R. Vector bundles on 𝒳(R, R^+) are equivalent to ϕ-modules over R̃_R, that is, finite projective R̃_R-modules with a ϕ-linear automorphism [KL15, Thms 6.3.12, 8.7.7] (Theorem 3.3.4).
items.note: Not planned. No stage constructs the Robba rings R̃_F and R̃_R (direct limits over r of the functions on Y_(0,r]), proves their Bézout property, or proves Kedlaya–Liu's equivalence between vector bundles and ϕ-modules over them. VB1 compares bundles only with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent. The Robba rings the atlas does plan (PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0, and the (ϕ, Γ)-module and p-adic local Langlands stages that import them) are rings of convergent Laurent series over a p-adic field, a different object. The paper uses this item only in the proof of Proposition 3.5.7(1), to apply [KL15, Thm 7.4.5]. There Theorem 3.3.4 is cited as 'Corollary 3.3.4' (misprint E2). VB4 plans that semicontinuity directly for bundles on X_S, so a formalisation can bypass this item. Its natural owner is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator, status, planning stages.

items.name: The relative Fargues–Fontaine curve and relative GAGA (Proposition 3.3.1, Definition 3.3.2, Theorem 3.3.3)
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid algebra of characteristic p with pseudouniformizer ϖ. Let Y_(0,∞)(R, R^+) = Spa(W(R^+), W(R^+)) ∖ {p[ϖ] = 0}, with α and Y_I(R, R^+) defined as in the absolute case. Proposition 3.3.1: for every closed interval I = [s, r] ⊂ (0, ∞) with r, s ∈ Q, Y_I(R, R^+) = Spa(R^{[s,r]}_R, R^{[s,r],+}_{R,R^+}) is a sheafy affinoid adic space. Here R^{[s,r],+}_{R,R^+} is the p-adic completion of the integral closure of W(R^+)[p/[ϖ^{1/r}], [ϖ^{1/s}]/p] in W(R^+)[p/[ϖ^{1/r}], [ϖ^{1/s}]/p][1/p], and R^{[s,r]}_R = R^{[s,r],+}_{R,R^+}[1/p] depends only on R. Moreover R^{[s,r]}_R ⊗̂_{Q_p} K is a perfectoid K-algebra for every perfectoid field K/Q_p, so Y_(0,∞)(R, R^+) = ∪_I Y_I(R, R^+) is an adic space. Definition 3.3.2: Frobenius acts totally discontinuously, and the relative curve is 𝒳(R, R^+) = Y_(0,∞)(R, R^+)/ϕ^Z. With the line bundles O(d), the scheme X(R) = Proj(⊕_{d≥0} H^0(𝒳(R, R^+), O(d))) does not depend on R^+. Theorem 3.3.3 [KL15, Thm 8.7.7]: pullback along 𝒳(R, R^+) → X(R) is an equivalence of categories of vector bundles.
items.note: RF0:annuli: 'the annulus rings with their explicit plus subrings. Prove complete separated sheafiness'. RF0:integral-Y makes the charts perfectoid only after the completed extension to E∞; the statement for every perfectoid K/Q_p is not planned. RF1: 'the adic quotient X_S = Y_S/phi^Z'. RF3: 'Form the graded algebra of global sections for affinoid S and construct Proj and the analytic-to-schematic map'. VB2:ampleness: 'Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3'. Theorem 3.3.4 belongs to the Robba-ring item. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator, planning stages.

items.name: Kedlaya–Liu: semicontinuity of Newton polygons in families
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid algebra of characteristic p, and let M be a ϕ-module over the relative Robba ring R̃_R; by Theorem 3.3.4 this is the same as a vector bundle on 𝒳(R, R^+). The map sending a point β of the Gelfand spectrum M(R) to the slope polygon of M ⊗ R̃_{H(β)} is lower semicontinuous. That is, where the rank of M is constant (which holds locally), for each x ∈ [0, rank M] the y-coordinate at x of the polygon is a lower semicontinuous function of β [KL15, Thm 7.4.5]. In the proof of Proposition 3.5.7(1) the paper applies this, through representations of G, to the tilt (R♭, R♭+) of an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R^+) over E whose map to Fℓ_{G,µ} is a topological quotient map.
items.note: VB4: 'Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity with the source's dominance convention'. VB4 states this for vector bundles on the relative curve X_S over a perfectoid space S of characteristic p. That is the form the proof of Proposition 3.5.7(1) uses: a representation of G gives a vector bundle on 𝒳(R♭, R♭+), to which the semicontinuity is applied (p. 690). [KL15, Thm 7.4.5] phrases the result for ϕ-modules over the relative Robba ring R̃_R, which correspond to vector bundles by Theorem 3.3.4. Theorem 3.3.4 belongs to the Robba-ring item, which no stage plans; a formalisation following VB4 does not need that translation. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Definitions 3.4.1–3.4.2 (the B^+_dR-affine Grassmannian and its Schubert cells)
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid Q_p-algebra [KL15, Def. 3.6.1]. The map θ : W(R^{♭+}) → R^+ is surjective, and its kernel is generated by an element ξ ∈ W(R^{♭+}) that is not a zero-divisor. B^+_dR,R is the ξ-adic completion of W(R^{♭+})[1/p], and B_dR,R = B^+_dR,R[ξ^{-1}]; both are independent of R^+. Definition 3.4.1: Gr^{B^+_dR}_G(R, R^+) is the set of isomorphism classes of G-torsors over Spec B^+_dR,R trivialized over Spec B_dR,R. For a perfectoid field K, B^+_dR,K is a complete discrete valuation ring, abstractly isomorphic to K[[ξ]], and Gr_G(K, K^+) = G(B_dR,K)/G(B^+_dR,K). Let C be algebraically closed with a fixed embedding Q̄_p → C. The Cartan decomposition G(B_dR,C) = ⊔_{µ ∈ X_*(G)_dom} G(B^+_dR,C) µ(ξ)^{-1} G(B^+_dR,C), with a deliberately nonstandard sign (footnote 14), attaches to each x ∈ Gr_G(C, O_C) a relative position µ(x) ∈ X_*(G)_dom. Definition 3.4.2: for a conjugacy class µ defined over E, Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ} ⊂ Gr^{B^+_dR}_G ⊗_{Q_p} E is the subfunctor on perfectoid affinoid E-algebras of the torsors whose relative position is µ at every point of Spa(R, R^+).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'Construct L+G, LG, the étale quotient LG/L+G … prove the torsor interpretation and descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings' and 'Define bounded relative position geometrically using dominant cocharacters … and construct Schubert cells/closures'. The paper's Gr is a functor on perfectoid affinoid (R, R^+), and it normalises relative position by µ(ξ)^{-1} (footnote 14). GS0 works with the v-sheaf over Div^1 and the standard sign, so the source route must record the conversion µ ↔ µ^{-1}. Mathlib's `BDeRhamPlus` is B^+_dR,R for the ring R^+, namely the ker θ-adic completion of W(R^{♭+})[1/p], and `BDeRham` is a localization of it. That ker θ is principal, and hence that B_dR,R = B^+_dR,R[ξ^{-1}], is not proved there. The printed text says the kernel of θ is generated by 'ξ ∈ W(R^+)' (p. 683, also in arXiv v1); ξ lies in W(R^{♭+}). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 3.4.3 (the Bialynicki-Birula map)
items.statement: Fix a conjugacy class µ defined over E, and let Fℓ_{G,µ}/E be the rigid-analytic flag variety of ascending filtrations of type Fil_•(µ) on Rep_{Q̄_p}G. Here Fil_m(µ) is the sum of the subspaces on which µ acts with weights m' ≥ −m, and Fℓ_{G,µ} = G/P_µ with P_µ the stabilizer of Fil_•(µ). Proposition 3.4.3: there is a natural Bialynicki-Birula map π_{G,µ} : Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ} → Fℓ_{G,µ} of functors on perfectoid affinoid E-algebras. For G = GL_n and µ = (k_1 ≥ … ≥ k_n), a B^+_dR,R-lattice Λ ⊂ B^n_dR,R gives the increasing filtration Fil_mR^n = ((B^+_dR,R)^n ∩ ξ^{-m}Λ)/((ξB^+_dR,R)^n ∩ ξ^{-m}Λ). Each R^n/Fil_mR^n is finite projective, by [KL15, Prop. 2.8.4], and Fil_mR^n has rank max{i : k_i ≥ −m}. The general case follows by the Tannakian formalism.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness: 'Identify a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and positive-loop unipotent fibres.' The projectivity of R^n/Fil_mR^n rests on [KL15, Prop. 2.8.4], which is a separate item. Footnote 15 explains the sign in Fil_m(µ) by the global convention that type (p, q) means the character z ↦ z^{-p} z̄^{-q}. The flag variety of a Shimura datum is item 5. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 3.4.4 (the Bialynicki-Birula map on field points)
items.statement: For µ minuscule and (K, K^+) a perfectoid field over E, π_{G,µ} is bijective on (K, K^+)-points.
items.note: The paper's proof: B^+_dR,K is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field K, so B^+_dR,K ≅ K[[ξ]] by the Cohen structure theorem, and π_{G,µ} becomes the Bialynicki-Birula map of the classical affine Grassmannian of G, which is an isomorphism for minuscule µ [NP01, Lemme 6.2]. Neither the libraries nor the atlas has the Cohen structure theorem or [NP01, Lemme 6.2]. The paper uses the lemma only for injectivity in Theorem 3.4.5. No stage states it; its destination is GS0:Schubert-smoothness, as an auxiliary lemma beside Theorem 3.4.5. If that layer proves Theorem 3.4.5 from its stabilizer computation, the lemma is the special case of (K, K^+)-points and needs neither input. The proof prints Gr_{G,µ}(K, K^+) = G(K((ξ)))/G(K[[ξ]]); the right side is Gr_G(K, K^+), of which Gr_{G,µ}(K, K^+) is the Schubert cell of µ (p. 685; the same in arXiv v1).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.6 (lattices are detected pointwise)
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid Q_p-algebra, Λ a finite projective B^+_dR,R-module, and a ∈ Λ ⊗_{B^+_dR,R} B_dR,R. Suppose that a ∈ Λ ⊗_{B^+_dR,R} B^+_dR,K(z) for every z ∈ Spa(R, R^+), where K(z) is the completed residue field at z. Then a ∈ Λ.
items.note: The proof uses only that R is reduced, which holds because a perfectoid algebra is uniform. It finds a nonzero element of the finite projective R-module ξ^{-m}Λ/ξ^{-m+1}Λ that vanishes at every point of Spa(R, R^+). The paper uses the lemma only for injectivity in Theorem 3.4.5. No stage states it; its destination is GS0:Schubert-smoothness, as an auxiliary lemma beside Theorem 3.4.5. It needs nothing beyond that layer's imports: the ξ-adic filtration of B^+_dR and its graded pieces come from RF2:untilts ('residue map, ideal filtration, graded pieces'), which GS0:loop-geometry imports. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 3.4.5 (for minuscule µ the Bialynicki-Birula map is an isomorphism)
items.statement: If µ is minuscule, the Bialynicki-Birula map π_{G,µ} : Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ} → Fℓ_{G,µ} is an isomorphism of functors on perfectoid affinoid E-algebras.
items.note: The paper proves injectivity from Lemmas 3.4.4 and 3.4.6. Surjectivity uses three inputs, each a separate item. First, Gr^{B^+_dR}_G is a pro-étale sheaf (via [KL15, Thm 9.2.15]). Second, for each representation V of G, the filtered bundle with integrable connection (V ⊗ O_{Fℓ_{G,µ}}, id ⊗ ∇, Fil_{−•}) satisfies Griffiths transversality because µ is minuscule ([Del79, Prop. 1.1.14]). Third, [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9] gives a B^+_dR-local system M_V ⊂ V ⊗ B_dR, compatible with tensor products and short exact sequences, whose pullbacks give the required preimages (p. 686). GS0:Schubert-smoothness plans to 'Identify a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and positive-loop unipotent fibres' and to 'prove VI.2.8's explicit congruence bound from weights of μ on Lie G', but it does not state the minuscule isomorphism. The item is therefore missing, and that stage is its destination. The layer should prove it from its stabilizer computation (FS VI.2.4) rather than by the paper's argument, whose input [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9] belongs to PadicHodgeTheory P8, which the layer does not import. For minuscule µ the weights of µ on Lie G are −1, 0 and 1, so the first congruence subgroup of L^+G fixes the base point, the unipotent fibres are points, and the Schubert cell maps isomorphically onto the flag variety. FS Remark VI.2.5 identifies this map with the Bialynicki-Birula map. The Galois-orbit descent that the layer plans covers µ defined only over E. Signs: FS normalise the cell by µ(ξ) and use P^−_µ, with Lie algebra (Lie G)_{µ≤0}. With the paper's µ(ξ)^{-1} (footnote 14), the paper's cell of µ is FS's cell of µ^{-1}, whose flag base G/P^−_{µ^{-1}} is G/P_µ = Fℓ_{G,µ} (p. 684). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1 (Kedlaya–Liu: Beauville–Laszlo gluing on the curve)
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid Q_p-algebra, and let X(R♭) be the schematic relative curve. Let Z be the image of the canonical closed immersion i_∞ : Spec R → X(R♭). Then Spec B^+_dR,R is the completion of X(R♭) along Z, and Spec B_dR,R = Spec B^+_dR,R ×_{X(R♭)} (X(R♭) ∖ Z). Theorem 3.5.1 [KL15, Thm 8.9.6]: vector bundles on X(R♭), or equivalently on 𝒳(R♭, R♭+), are equivalent to triples (M_1, M_2, ι). Here M_1 is a vector bundle on X(R♭) ∖ Z, M_2 is a vector bundle on Spec B^+_dR,R, and ι : M_1|_{Spec B_dR,R} ≅ M_2|_{Spec B_dR,R}. The equivalence is compatible with tensor products and short exact sequences. In particular, gluing a B^+_dR,R-lattice in B^n_dR,R to the trivial bundle on X(R♭) ∖ Z gives a vector bundle.
items.note: RF4:vector-bundles: 'Prove Beauville–Laszlo gluing for finite locally free modules along the Cartier divisors just constructed: a bundle off D, a bundle on its formal neighborhood, and an isomorphism on the punctured neighborhood determine a bundle … Prove compatibility with tensor, dual, base change'. RF4 does not name compatibility with short exact sequences. VB2:ampleness: 'Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve'. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Corollary 3.5.2 (the G-bundle of a point of the Grassmannian)
items.statement: For every perfectoid affinoid Q_p-algebra (R, R^+) there is a natural map E : Gr^{B^+_dR}_G(R, R^+) → {G-bundles on 𝒳(R♭, R♭+)}. For G = GL_n it glues a B^+_dR,R-lattice in B^n_dR,R to the trivial bundle on X(R♭) ∖ Z, by Theorem 3.5.1; in general it comes from the Tannakian formalism. Now let (R, R^+) = (C, O_C), with C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed and a fixed embedding Q̄_p ↪ C. Composing with Theorem 3.2.9 gives b(·) : Gr^{B^+_dR}_G(C, O_C) → B(G), x ↦ b(E(x)), the class of the G-bundle E(x).
items.note: RF4:G-torsors: 'Transfer the preceding gluing to G-torsors via the exact tensor-functor comparison supplied in BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0 … only then export the modification interpretation to GS0/BG2.' BG2:uniformization: 'Construct the Hecke modification uniformization around an untilt divisor through RF4 patching' and 'Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G)'. On (C, O_C)-points the composite of these two is b(·). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 (Newton above Hodge for modifications)
items.statement: Let C/Q_p be complete and algebraically closed, and let E be a vector bundle of rank n on the schematic curve X_{C♭} with a trivialization outside ∞. Let µ(E) ∈ X_*(GL_n)_dom be its relative position with respect to the trivial bundle. In the normalization of §3.4, a line bundle whose completion at ∞ is the lattice ξ^{-d}B^+_dR,C has µ = d. Let ν_E ∈ (X_*(GL_n) ⊗ Q)_dom be its Newton polygon, whose slopes are the λ_i with E ≅ ⊕_i O_{X_{C♭}}(λ_i). Then ν_E ⪯ µ(E): the Newton polygon of E lies above its Hodge polygon. The correspondence between isocrystals and bundles reverses slopes, so this says b(E)^{-1} ∈ B(GL_n, µ(E)), equivalently b(E) ∈ B(GL_n, µ(E)^{-1}) (footnote 17).
items.note: The proof follows Katz [Kat79]. Using exterior powers, it suffices to check two things. (1) The Newton and Hodge slopes agree for the top exterior power: a line bundle whose completion at ∞ is ξ^{-d}B^+_dR,C is O(d), of slope d. (2) The first Newton slope lies above the first Hodge slope: after twisting, all Hodge slopes are ≥ 0, so O^n ↪ E, while there is no nonzero map O → O(λ) for λ < 0 [FF14]. No stage states Newton-above-Hodge for modifications of the trivial bundle. On p. 688 the proof prints the lattice as ξ^{-d}B_dR,C where ξ^{-d}B^+_dR,C is meant. It also writes 𝒳_{FF,C}, O_{X^♭} and O_{X^♭}(d) for the lemma's X_{C♭}, O_{X_{C♭}} and O_{X_{C♭}}(d). Both slips are already in arXiv v1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.5 (the Kottwitz invariant of a modification)
items.statement: Let µ be any conjugacy class of cocharacters (not necessarily minuscule), and let C/Q_p be complete and algebraically closed with a fixed embedding Q̄_p ↪ C. The composite Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ}(C, O_C) → B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ, x ↦ κ(b(E(x))), is constant with value −µ♭.
items.note: BG2:uniformization: 'Prove the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G), geometric-base independence and the kappa/nu formulas. Prove kappa locally constant using the source z-extension route and its v-surjectivity lemma … This explicitly includes the non-simply-connected derived-group case.' The lemma is Fargues–Scholze Proposition III.3.6(ii). For split G, the composite of the Beauville–Laszlo map |Gr_G| → |Bun_G| with κ is the opposite of the locally constant map |Gr_G| → π_1(G) characterised by Gr_{G,µ} ⊂ Gr_G^{µ♯}. For general G the same holds with values in π_1(G)_Γ, as stated after the proof there. Fargues–Scholze prove it by the paper's reduction: a z-extension, then a torus, an induced torus and G_m. Before the two statements are identified, the blueprint must match the paper's normalisation of relative position with that of Fargues–Scholze. In the paper the cell is G(B^+_dR,C)µ(ξ)^{-1}G(B^+_dR,C) (footnote 14), and for G = G_m the lattice ξ^{-d}B^+_dR,C has µ = d and gives O(d) (p. 688). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.3 (modifications of type µ land in B(G, µ^{-1}))
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, µ any conjugacy class of cocharacters (not necessarily minuscule), and C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed with a fixed embedding Q̄_p ↪ C. For every x ∈ Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ}(C, O_C), the class b = b(E(x)) lies in B(G, µ^{-1}). That is, ν_b ⪯ \overline{µ^{-1}}, by Lemma 3.5.4 and [RR96, Lemma 2.2], and κ(b) = −µ♭, by Lemma 3.5.5.
items.note: Proof: the bound ν_b ⪯ \overline{µ^{-1}} reduces to G = GL_n by [RR96, Lemma 2.2], which is a separate item, and is then Lemma 3.5.4. The equality κ(b) = −µ♭ is Lemma 3.5.5, which BG2:uniformization plans. No stage states which classes modifications of type µ reach. BG2:uniformization plans 'the Hecke modification uniformization around an untilt divisor through RF4 patching' and 'the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G) … and the kappa/nu formulas', but not the bound on ν_b. That stage is its destination. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Definition 3.5.6 (the Newton stratification of the flag variety)
items.statement: Let µ be minuscule and defined over E. For a perfectoid affinoid E-algebra (R, R^+), the inverse of the isomorphism π_{G,µ} of Theorem 3.4.5, followed by Corollary 3.5.2, gives E : Fℓ_{G,µ}(R, R^+) ≅ Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ}(R, R^+) → {G-bundles on 𝒳(R♭, R♭+)}. The map |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) is defined as follows. Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of E and C^+ ⊂ C an open and bounded valuation subring. The map sends x ∈ Fℓ_{G,µ}(C, C^+) to the class of E(x) given by Theorem 3.2.9. It does not depend on the choice of C. A higher-rank point has the same image as its rank-one generalization, so the map factors through the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |Fℓ_{G,µ}|, the Berkovich space Fℓ^Berk_{G,µ}. For b ∈ B(G), Fℓ^b_{G,µ} ⊂ Fℓ_{G,µ} is the set of points with image b.
items.note: A higher-rank point has the image of its rank-one generalization. BG3 plans the strata of Bun_G ('Construct Bun_G^b as the locally closed substack for each b'), and Fℓ^b_{G,µ} is their pullback along Fℓ_{G,µ} ≅ Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ} → Bun_G, the inverse of Theorem 3.4.5 followed by the Beauville–Laszlo map. No stage states the stratification of the flag variety, so the item is missing, with BG3 as its destination.
