BG3 must then import GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:Schubert-smoothness, which receives Theorem 3.4.5. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.7 (semicontinuity and admissibility)
items.statement: Let µ be minuscule and defined over E, and let b(·) : |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) be the map of Definition 3.5.6. (1) b(·) is upper semicontinuous for the order ⪯ on B(G) (the paper prints "lower", E35): for every b ∈ B(G), the set of x ∈ |Fℓ_{G,µ}| with b(x) ⪰ b is closed. (2) The image of b(·) is contained in the set B(G, µ^{-1}) of µ^{-1}-admissible elements.
items.note: Part (2) is Proposition 3.5.3. For part (1): κ is constant by (2), so only the Newton map matters. The proof pulls back to an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R^+) → Fℓ_{G,µ} that is a topological quotient map (a pro-étale cover), reduces to representations of G by [RR96, Lemma 2.2], and applies [KL15, Thm 7.4.5] through Theorem 3.3.4, which is printed as 'Corollary 3.3.4' (recorded misprint E2, confirmed on the page image, p. 690). 'Lower semicontinuous' is meant in the sense Corollary 3.5.9 uses: for every b ∈ B(G), the set of x with b(x) ⪰ b is closed. BG2:uniformization plans the semicontinuity of ν on |Bun_G| ('prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory'). Part (1) would follow by pulling back along Fℓ_{G,µ} ≅ Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ} → Bun_G, but no stage plans the flag-variety statement itself. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Remark 3.5.8 (Rapoport: every µ^{-1}-admissible class occurs)
items.statement: Let µ be minuscule and defined over E. Then the map b(·) : |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G, µ^{-1}) of Definition 3.5.6 and Proposition 3.5.7(2) is surjective: every µ^{-1}-admissible class occurs [Rap15, Prop. A.9].
items.note: Rapoport's appendix to Scholze's paper on the p-adic cohomology of the Lubin–Tate tower proves this, based on this section. It is the converse of Proposition 3.5.3 on (C, O_C)-points, where Fℓ_{G,µ}(C, O_C) = Gr^{B^+_dR}_{G,µ}(C, O_C). No stage states which classes modifications of type µ reach, so the item is missing. Its destination is BG2:uniformization, which also receives Proposition 3.5.3. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 1.11 = Corollary 3.5.9 (the strata are locally closed)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, µ a conjugacy class of minuscule cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} with field of definition E, and Fℓ_{G,µ} the adic flag variety over E of filtrations of type Fil_•(µ). Send x ∈ Fℓ_{G,µ}(C, C^+) to the class in B(G) of the G-bundle E(x) on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (Definition 3.5.6). This gives a decomposition Fℓ_{G,µ} = ⊔_{b∈B(G,µ^{-1})} Fℓ^b_{G,µ} into locally closed subsets. For every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}), the union Fℓ^{⪰b}_{G,µ} := ⊔_{b⪯b'} Fℓ^{b'}_{G,µ} is closed; in particular, the stratum of the basic element is open. So the closure relations are opposite to those of the Newton stratification of Shimura varieties, and the µ-ordinary stratum is closed (Remark 1.17; §3, p. 674).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.11 and footnote 6, p. 655 (examples pp. 655–656); Remark 1.17, p. 658; §3, p. 674; §3.5, Corollary 3.5.9, p. 690
items.note: Proof: Proposition 3.5.7 (item 46), with Definition 3.5.6 (item 45), via Theorem 3.4.5. The closedness uses Kedlaya–Liu's semicontinuity of the Newton polygon [KL15] (p. 656). Footnote 6: the closure of a stratum is not shown to be a union of strata, so 'closure relations' is meant loosely. The §1 examples are given without proof. For the modular curve, Fℓ = P^1 = P^1(Q_p) ⊔ Ω^2. For basic b, Fℓ^b is the admissible locus of [RZ96], whose classical points form the weakly admissible locus. For a nonsplit inner form of GL_5 with µ = (1,1,0,0,0), all classical points are basic although other strata are nonempty. On points, Fℓ^b_{G,µ} is the preimage of the stratum Bun^b_G under x ↦ E(x), the map Fℓ_{G,µ} ≅ Gr_{G,µ} → Bun_G mentioned in Remark 1.18. The paper itself works only with points and does not construct Bun_G. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2:uniformization plans to 'prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory'. BG3 plans to 'Construct Bun_G^b as the locally closed substack for each b' and to 'prove that the union of basic strata is open'. No stage states the result on the flag variety. It belongs in BG3 together with Definition 3.5.6 and Proposition 3.5.7, as the pullback of BG3's strata along Fℓ_{G,µ} ≅ Gr_{G,µ} → Bun_G. For this, BG3 must import Theorem 3.4.5 from GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Schubert-smoothness. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Tate modules and universal covers of p-divisible groups (Definition 4.1.1)
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete Z_p-algebra, and let Nilp^op_R be the opposite of the category of R-algebras on which p is nilpotent. View a p-divisible group G over R as the fpqc sheaf S ↦ colim_n G[p^n](S) on Nilp^op_R. (1) The (integral) Tate module is the fpqc sheaf T_p(G)(S) = lim_n G[p^n](S), a sheaf of Z_p-modules. (2) The universal cover is the fpqc sheaf G̃(S) = lim_{p : G → G} G(S), a sheaf of Q_p-vector spaces with G̃ = T_p(G)[1/p]. Canonically, T_pG = Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G) and G̃ = Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G)[1/p], with sheaf Homs. There is a short exact sequence 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0 of sheaves on Nilp^op_R, which for connected G restates [SW13, Prop. 3.3.1].
items.locator: §4.1, Definition 4.1.1, pp. 690–691; proof of Proposition 4.1.2, p. 691
items.note: Follows [SW13, §3]. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 plans the Tate module of a p-divisible group ('Construct its Tate module'), and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 extends it to 'generic-fibre Tate modules'. Neither states the Tate module as the fpqc sheaf S ↦ lim_n G[p^n](S) on Nilp^op_R. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3:positive-basic-examples plans only the universal cover of a Lubin–Tate formal group ('Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculations'). No stage plans the universal cover G̃ of a general p-divisible group or the identifications with Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G), so the item is missing. Its destination is R07.1, beside the Tate module. The universal cover is the same inverse limit with p inverted, and R07.1 lies upstream of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 and of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0, where the universal cover of X_b and its automorphism group are used (Lemma 4.2.10, p. 704). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2 (Messing, Scholze–Weinstein: representability of universal covers)
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete Z_p-algebra and G a p-divisible group over R, regarded as the fpqc sheaf S ↦ colim_n G[p^n](S) on Nilp^op_R, with Tate module T_pG and universal cover G̃ as in Definition 4.1.1. (1) If G is connected, it is representable by an affine formal scheme with finitely generated ideal of definition; if moreover Lie G is free of rank r, then G ≅ Spf R[[x_1, …, x_r]]. (2) If ρ : G_1 → G_2 is an isogeny, the induced map ρ̃ : G̃_1 → G̃_2 is an isomorphism. (3) If R is perfect of characteristic p, G is connected and Lie G is free of rank r, then G̃ ≅ Spf R[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]]. (4) Under the hypotheses of (3), T_pG ≅ Spec R[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]]/(x_1, …, x_r).
items.note: Part (1) is [Mes72]; parts (2) and (3) are [SW13, Prop. 3.1.3]; part (4) follows from (1), (3) and the exact sequence 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0 of sheaves on Nilp^op_R ([SW13, Prop. 3.3.1] for connected G). FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 plans the Tate module ('Define a p-divisible group as compatible finite locally free levels … Construct its Tate module') but neither the universal cover nor these representability statements. A source route adds them to R07.1, beside Definition 4.1.1. R07.1 is upstream of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0, which uses the proposition for Aut_G(X̃_b) (Lemma 4.2.10, p. 704). VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3:positive-basic-examples plans the Lubin–Tate universal cover of Fargues–Scholze §II.2.1. For E = Q_p that is the one-dimensional case of (3), so the two should be built once. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory: M(G) and D(G)
items.statement: For a p-divisible group G over R, the universal vector extension EG is a crystal on the nilpotent crystalline site of R [Mes72], and its Lie algebra extends to a crystal 𝕄(G) on the crystalline site of R [BBM82]. The theory is covariant. It is normalised as the literal dual of contravariant Dieudonné theory, without a Tate twist (footnote 18). For G over F̄_p, D(G) = 𝕄(G)(W(F̄_p) → F̄_p), and D(G)[1/p] is an isocrystal over L = W(F̄_p)[1/p]. Its Frobenius ϕ_G satisfies D(G) ⊂ ϕ_G(D(G)) ⊂ p^{-1}D(G), and pϕ_G is the usual Frobenius. G is isoclinic if D(G)[1/p] has a single slope, and isoclinic of slope λ if that slope is −λ (so µ_{p^∞} is isoclinic of slope 1). For every complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field F ⊃ F̄_p, the isocrystal D(G)[1/p] defines a vector bundle 𝓔(G) on the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve 𝒳_F. By Example 4.1.3, 𝓔(Q_p/Z_p) = O_{𝒳_F} and 𝓔(µ_{p^∞}) = O_{𝒳_F}(1).
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans to 'Construct Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields and prove the classification in the covariant or contravariant convention chosen above', with 'Frobenius/Verschiebung, dimensions, heights, slopes', and to 'Supply the deformation results needed for p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings'. CrystallineCohomology CR.7 will 'Export PD bases, crystals, connections, filtrations, Frobenius and log monodromy to R07's Dieudonne crystal and Grothendieck–Messing construction' and 'Verify its covariance/contravariance and Tate twists on the constant and multiplicative p-divisible groups'; this is Example 4.1.3 and footnote 18. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1 will 'Construct the isocrystal-to-bundle functor', which gives 𝓔(G). AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 imports 'Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory from R07.6', but R07.6's own description does not mention it. The evaluation of 𝕄(G) on A_cris(O_C/p) belongs to Theorem 4.1.4. The text calls D(G)[1/p] an isocrystal 'as defined in Section 4', meaning Definition 3.1.1 (sourceIssues E3). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.4 (Scholze–Weinstein: p-divisible groups over O_C/p and bundles)
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_C. Let A_cris be the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of W(O_{C♭}) → O_C/p, let B^+_cris = A_cris[1/p], and let X_{C♭} = Proj(⊕_{d≥0}(B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^d}) be the schematic Fargues–Fontaine curve. For a p-divisible group G over the semiperfect ring O_C/p, M(G) = 𝕄(G)(A_cris → O_C/p) is a finite projective A_cris-module, and M(G)[1/p] carries a Frobenius-semilinear map ϕ_G. E(G) is the vector bundle on X_{C♭} attached to the graded module ⊕_{d≥0}(M(G)[1/p])^{ϕ=p^d}. (1) For every p-divisible group G over O_C/p there are a p-divisible group H over F̄_p and a quasi-isogeny ρ : H ×_{F̄_p} O_C/p → G. (2) G ↦ E(G) is a fully faithful functor from p-divisible groups over O_C/p up to isogeny to vector bundles on X_{C♭}. Its essential image consists of the bundles all of whose slopes lie between 0 and 1. (3) For a p-divisible group G over F̄_p, GAGA for the curve identifies the bundle 𝓔(G) on the adic curve 𝒳_{C♭} attached to D(G)[1/p] with E(G ×_{F̄_p} O_C/p).
items.note: Parts (1) and (2) are [SW13, Thm 5.1.4]. That theorem rests on Dieudonné theory up to isogeny over the f-semiperfect ring O_C/p ([SW13, Thm A], a separate item). Part (3) is GAGA for the Fargues–Fontaine curve. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2 plans to 'Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site' but does not plan this theorem. A source route adds it to T2, together with the classification of p-divisible groups over O_C by pairs (T, W). T2 must then import VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1 ('Construct the isocrystal-to-bundle functor'), VB2:ampleness (the schematic curve and its comparison with the adic one) and VB2:classification (slopes). Lemma 4.2.18 uses the theorem to produce the quasi-isogeny ρ (p. 711). The text says C has 'ring of integers O_C/p' (sourceIssues E4). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: classification of p-divisible groups over O_C, and the quasi-logarithm
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p. The functor G ↦ (T_pG, Lie G ⊗_{O_C} C) is an equivalence between p-divisible groups over O_C and pairs (T, W), with T a finite free Z_p-module and W ⊂ T ⊗_{Z_p} C(−1) a C-subspace. W is embedded through the Hodge–Tate sequence 0 → Lie G ⊗ C(1) → T_pG ⊗ C → (Lie G^∨)^∨ ⊗ C → 0 [SW13, Thm B = Thm 5.2.1]. The paper writes W ⊂ T ⊗_{Z_p} C and calls it the Hodge–Tate filtration; it suppresses the twist by its fixed choice of p-power roots of unity. For a p-divisible group X_b over F̄_p, the quasi-logarithm [SW13, §3] is a map of sheaves qlog_{X_b} : (X̃_b)^ad_η(R, R^+) → D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗_L R on complete affinoid (Ĕ, O_Ĕ)-algebras. At a geometric point (C, C^+), for a deformation G of X_b, the image of T_pG^ad_η(C, C^+) ⊗_{Z_p} C under qlog_{X_b} is identified with (Lie G^∨)^∨ ⊗ C.
items.locator: §1, p. 654; §4.2, pp. 699–700 and 711 (proofs of Theorem 4.2.4, Proposition 4.2.14 and Lemma 4.2.18); §4.3, p. 725 (proof of Lemma 4.3.20)
items.note: Input to Theorem 4.2.4, Proposition 4.2.14, Lemma 4.2.18 and Lemma 4.3.20 (with [SW13, Props 3.4.2, 7.1.1]). No stage plans it. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 plans only the finite-level map ('Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters'). T2 plans to 'Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site', but not the classification. AInfCohomology:AI.2 plans Fargues' classification of finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules over O_C by pairs (T, Ξ), with Ξ a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗ B_dR. This is the nearest planned statement, but it is a different one. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6 and ET.6a cite Scholze–Weinstein §§6–7 for the infinite-level Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers, which rest on this classification, but they do not plan it. The item belongs in T2, where the Hodge–Tate filtration W is built. It uses the universal cover of Definition 4.1.1 and Proposition 4.1.2. That cover sits beside the Tate module of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 and reaches T2 through T1, T0 and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3–A4. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator.

items.name: Lemmas 4.1.5–4.1.6 (Chai–Oort: the internal Hom p-divisible group)
items.statement: Let G, G' be isoclinic p-divisible groups over a perfect field k. For n ≥ 1, H_n = 𝓗om(G[p^n], G'[p^n]) is a commutative group scheme of finite type over k. For m ≥ n, the restriction map r_{m,n} : H_m → H_n has closed kernel, and H_n^{(m)} = H_m/ker r_{m,n} is a subgroup scheme of H_n; as m grows these form a descending chain. (Lemma 4.1.5) H_n^{(m)} is constant for m ≫ 0, equal to a finite group scheme H'_n over k. (Lemma 4.1.6) The maps ι_n : H_n → H_{n+1}, given by precomposition with multiplication by p : G[p^{n+1}] → G[p^n] followed by composition with the inclusion G'[p^n] ↪ G'[p^{n+1}], send H'_n into H'_{n+1}, and H_{G,G'} = colim_n H'_n is a p-divisible group over k with H_{G,G'}[p^n] = H'_n.
items.note: The construction is due to Chai and Oort; the authors learnt of it in a talk of C.-L. Chai at the Faltings conference in 2014 (p. 693). No stage plans the internal Hom. It goes to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0 as the tool for 'the automorphism group scheme. Construct the connected/formal and profinite parts of Aut(X)'. IG.0 plans that only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum'). This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemmas 4.1.7–4.1.8 (Tate module and Dieudonné module of H_{G,G'})
items.statement: Let G, G' be isoclinic p-divisible groups over a perfect field k. (Lemma 4.1.7) The Tate module T_pH_{G,G'} is identified with the sheaf 𝓗om(G, G'). (Lemma 4.1.8) D(H_{G,G'})[1/p] = Hom(D(G)[1/p], D(G')[1/p])^{≤0}, the slope ≤ 0 part of the internal Hom of Dieudonné modules. (Remark 4.1.9) The statement depends only on G and G' up to quasi-isogeny. Chai and Oort prove Lemma 4.1.8 by computing the relative Frobenius of H_{G,G'} in terms of those of conveniently chosen G and G'. They also give an integral version of it. (O_F-linear version, p. 706) Let F/Q_p be unramified of degree d. The construction extends to an internal Hom in the category of p-divisible groups with O_F-action. For such G over F̄_p, the rational Dieudonné module decomposes as D(G)[1/p] = ⊕_{τ : O_F ↪ W(F̄_p)} D(G)[1/p]_τ. Fix τ_0 and put D_F(G) = D(G)[1/p]_{τ_0}, an isocrystal for ϕ^d. The analogue of Lemma 4.1.8 holds for D_F and O_F-linear homomorphisms, with the same proof after replacing ϕ by ϕ^d and embedding F into B^+_cris via τ_0.
items.locator: §4.1, Lemmas 4.1.7–4.1.8, Remark 4.1.9, pp. 695–696; §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.2.11 and footnote 19, p. 706 (the O_F-linear version)
items.note: The paper's proof differs from Chai and Oort's. It evaluates on f-semiperfect rings R [SW13, Def. 4.1.2]. There Dieudonné theory up to isogeny ([SW13, Thm A], a separate item) gives H̃_{G,G'}(R) = (Hom(D(G)[1/p], D(G')[1/p]) ⊗ B^+_cris(R))^{ϕ=1}. By the Dieudonné–Manin classification it then suffices that there is no nonzero x ∈ A_cris(R) with p^aϕ^b(x) = x for integers a, b > 0; the printed text omits 'nonzero' (p. 696). By footnote 19, p-divisible groups with O_F-action behave up to quasi-isogeny like p-divisible O_F-modules. No stage plans these statements. They go to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0 with Lemmas 4.1.5–4.1.6. IG.0 plans 'the automorphism group scheme' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel, and this paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Corollaries 4.1.10–4.1.11 (slopes of H_{G,G'})
items.statement: Let G, G' be isoclinic p-divisible groups over a perfect field k. (Corollary 4.1.10) (1) If the slope of G is strictly greater than the slope of G', then H_{G,G'} = 0. (2) If the slopes are equal, H_{G,G'} is an étale p-divisible group. (3) If the slope of G is strictly less than the slope of G', H_{G,G'} is a connected p-divisible group. (Corollary 4.1.11) In case (3), if H_{G,G'} has dimension r, the sheaf 𝓗om(G, G') is representable by the scheme Spec k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]]/(x_1, …, x_r).
items.note: Corollary 4.1.10 has no printed proof. It is read off from the slopes in Lemma 4.1.8: H_{G,G'} is isoclinic of slope λ' − λ when G, G' have slopes λ, λ'. Corollary 4.1.11 follows from Proposition 4.1.2(4) and Corollary 4.1.10(3). Proposition 4.2.11 uses both to put Aut(X̃_b) in lower triangular form and to identify its fibres over J_b(Q_p) (p. 705). No stage plans them. They go to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0, whose 'Construct the connected/formal and profinite parts of Aut(X)' is planned only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Unramified local PEL data and the p-divisible group X_b
items.statement: B is a finite-dimensional semisimple Q_p-algebra with anti-involution *, and V a finite left B-module with an alternating form (·,·) : V ⊗_{Q_p} V → Q_p such that (bv, w) = (v, b*w); G(R) = {(g, c) ∈ GL_{B⊗R}(V ⊗ R) × R^× : (gv, gw) = c(v, w)}, with multiplier c, is assumed connected (type D excluded). Unramified: B is a product of matrix algebras over unramified extensions of Q_p with a fixed *-stable maximal Z_p-order O_B, and Λ ⊂ V is a fixed O_B-stable lattice, self-dual for (·,·), defining a reductive group G_{Z_p}. µ : G_m → G_{Q̄_p} is a conjugacy class of cocharacters with only weights 0 and 1 on V, V_{Q̄_p} = V_0 ⊕ V_1 (both totally isotropic), and with multiplier ∘ µ = id; E is its field of definition, b ∈ G(L) has class in B(G, µ^{-1}), and Ĕ = E·L. The slopes of b on V lie in [−1, 0], so there is a p-divisible group X_b over F̄_p, unique up to isogeny, with rational Dieudonné module (V ⊗_{Q_p} L, b(id ⊗ σ)); its universal cover X̃_b is unique and carries ι : B → End(X̃_b) and a symmetric polarization whose Rosati involution is compatible with *. D = (B, *, V, (·,·), b, µ) and D^int = (O_B, *, Λ, (·,·), b, µ).
items.note: IG.0 plans 'local deformation data' (its title) and to 'Develop the Serre–Tate deformation and quasi-isogeny comparisons' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum'). This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified local PEL data of type (A) or (C), with no compactness assumed (pp. 696–697). The global data of §4.3 give such local data at every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) (p. 714). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Definition 4.2.1 and Theorem 4.2.2 (Rapoport–Zink spaces of PEL type)
items.statement: (Definition 4.2.1) 𝔐_{D^int} is the functor on Nilp^op_{O_Ĕ} sending R to the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (G, ρ), where G is a p-divisible group over R with an O_B-action and a principal polarization whose Rosati involution is compatible with * on O_B, the O_B-action satisfying the determinant condition [RZ96, 3.23], and ρ : X_b ×_{F̄_p} R/p → G ×_R R/p is a quasi-isogeny compatible with the O_B-action and with the polarizations up to an automorphism of µ̃_{p^∞,R/p}. (Theorem 4.2.2, combining [RZ96, Thm 3.25, §3.82]; in this unramified situation without type D, p = 2 is allowed) 𝔐_{D^int} is representable by a formal scheme that locally admits a finitely generated ideal of definition, and it is formally smooth.
items.note: Definition 4.2.1 writes O_{Ĕ_0} for O_Ĕ (sourceIssues E5). Representability rests on Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory (a separate item, planned in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2). No stage plans Rapoport–Zink spaces of PEL type. IG.0's 'Develop the Serre–Tate deformation and quasi-isogeny comparisons' is planned only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel, and HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2 says 'do not restrict general local shtukas to classical Rapoport–Zink spaces'. This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). IG.0 must then import formal schemes from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Generic fibre, finite level and infinite level (Definition 4.2.3)
items.statement: M_{D^int} = (𝔐_{D^int})^ad_η := 𝔐^ad ×_{Spa(O_Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} Spa(Ĕ, O_Ĕ). Here 𝔐 ↦ 𝔐^ad is the fully faithful functor of [SW13, §2, Prop. 2.2.1] on formal schemes over O_Ĕ that locally admit a finitely generated ideal of definition. M_{D^int} agrees with the rigid-analytic generic fibre. Let K_0 = {g ∈ G(Q_p) : gΛ = Λ} and K_n = {g ∈ K_0 : g ≡ 1 mod p^n}. Then M_{D^int,n} is the functor on complete affinoid (Ĕ(ζ_{p^n}), O_{Ĕ(ζ_{p^n})})-algebras parametrizing O_B-linear maps Λ/p^n → G[p^n]^ad_η(R, R^+) that match (·,·) on Λ with the pairing on G[p^n] induced by the polarization. That pairing takes values in µ_{p^n}, which is identified with Z/p^n by the fixed ζ_{p^n} ∈ E(ζ_{p^n}). These are finite étale covers of M_{D^int} [RZ96, L 5.33]. (Definition 4.2.3) M_{D^int,∞} sends a complete affinoid (Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O_{Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞})})-algebra (R, R^+) to the triples (G, ρ, α) with (G, ρ) ∈ M_{D^int}(R, R^+) and α : Λ → T_pG^ad_η(R, R^+) O_B-linear, such that: (1) α matches (·,·) on Λ with the polarization pairing via Z_p → (T_pµ_{p^∞})^ad_η(R, R^+), 1 ↦ (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …); and (2) Λ → T_pG^ad_η(C, C^+) is an isomorphism for every geometric point Spa(C, C^+) of Spa(R, R^+).
items.note: 𝔐 ↦ 𝔐^ad is [SW13, Prop. 2.2.1]. No stage plans these spaces. IG.3 ('For a geometric flag point x=Spa(C,O_C)→Fl, identify its polarized p-divisible group over O_C and special fiber X') is written for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel and names no Rapoport–Zink space. This paper's source route adds the Rapoport–Zink spaces at finite and infinite level to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C), as the compact-case proof of the fibre theorem. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.4 (infinite-level RZ spaces of PEL type)
items.statement: M_{D^int,∞} is representable by an adic space over Spa(Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O_{Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞})}); it is preperfectoid and M_{D^int,∞} ~ lim_n M_{D^int,n}. It depends only on D: it is the sheafification of the functor sending (R, R^+) to the B-linear maps V → (X̃_b)^ad_η(R, R^+) that match (·,·) on V with the polarization (up to the fixed p-power roots of unity) and such that, for the induced map V ⊗_{Q_p} R → D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗_L R (through the quasi-logarithm qlog_{X_b}), (1) the image of V ⊗ R is totally isotropic for the pairing induced by D(X_b)[1/p] ≅ V ⊗_{Q_p} L; (2) the quotient W of D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗_L R by this image is a finite projective R-module, locally isomorphic to V_1 ⊗ R as a B ⊗_{Q_p} R-module; (3) for every point Spa(C, C^+) of Spa(R, R^+), the sequence 0 → V → (X̃_b)^ad_η(C, C^+) → W ⊗_R C → 0 is exact. Thereafter M_{D^int,∞} is identified with M_{D,∞}.
items.note: The proof follows [SW13, §6], whose Theorem 6.5.4 is the EL case. M_{D^int,∞} is a closed subfunctor of Scholze–Weinstein's M_∞ (a separate item). The O_B-action and polarization conditions are closed by Grothendieck–Messing theory, and being a genuine isogeny on the generic fibre is open and closed as in [SW13, Prop. 3.3.3]. Preperfectoidness follows from [SW13, Thm 6.3.4, Prop. 2.3.7], and the rational description from [SW13, Lemma 6.3.6, Prop. 3.4.2(v)]. The identification X̃_b ≅ G̃ uses rigidity of universal covers. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a plans only the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers ('Prove the infinite-level moduli description and duality isomorphism'), and no stage plans infinite-level Rapoport–Zink spaces of EL or PEL type. IG.3 names no Rapoport–Zink space and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum. This paper's source route adds the theorem to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Scholze–Weinstein's EL theorem should have a single owner, imported by both IG.3 and ET.6a. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Propositions 4.2.5–4.2.6 (the local Hodge–Tate period map lands in the b-stratum)
items.statement: For the PEL data, Fℓ_{G,µ} parametrizes the B-equivariant quotients V ⊗_{Q_p} R → W' that are finite projective R-modules with totally isotropic kernel and W' locally isomorphic to V_0 ⊗ R as B ⊗_{Q_p} R-modules. (Proposition 4.2.5) There is a G(Q_p)-equivariant local Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : M_{D,∞} → Fℓ_{G,µ}, sending a point given by V → (X̃_b)^ad_η(R, R^+) to the quotient of V ⊗_{Q_p} R given by the image of V ⊗_{Q_p} R → D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗_L R. (Proposition 4.2.6) π_HT factors through π^b_HT : M_{D,∞} → Fℓ^b_{G,µ}. (Remark 4.2.7) The same proof shows that the local Hodge–Tate period map of Rapoport–Zink spaces of EL type [SW13, Prop. 7.1.1] factors through Fℓ^b_{G,µ}.
items.note: [SW13, Prop. 7.1.1]. The bundle E_V is the modification of V ⊗ O at ∞ by the lattice with Ξ/(V ⊗ B^+_dR) = Lie G ⊗ C. By the proof of [SW13, Prop. 5.1.6] (a separate item), it equals the bundle of G ×_{O_C} O_C/p. The text refers to 'Theorem 3.5.9' for Corollary 3.5.9 (sourceIssues E6). No stage plans the local Hodge–Tate period map. IG.3's 'compatibility with … flag Newton strata' is written for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel and names no local period map. This paper's source route adds it to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). IG.3 must import the flag Newton strata from BunGAndNewtonStrata BG3. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Remark 4.2.8 (local and global Hodge–Tate maps agree)
items.statement: For A/O_C and G = A[p^∞], the Hodge–Tate filtration on T_pG ⊗ C agrees with the one of §2 [Sch13d, Prop. 4.15], so local and global Hodge–Tate period maps are compatible.
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1 plans to 'Apply them to degree-one proper smooth abelian families with connection, filtration and tensor compatibility, and identify the resulting maps with T0', where T0 will 'Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters'. For an abelian variety A over O_C, this identifies the Hodge–Tate filtration of T_pA ⊗ C coming from the relative comparison theorem (Corollary 2.2.4) with the one coming from the p-divisible group A[p^∞] [Sch13d, Prop. 4.15]. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: status, planning stages.

items.name: Definition 4.2.9 and Lemma 4.2.10 (the automorphism group of X̃_b)
items.statement: (Definition 4.2.9) Aut_G(X̃_b) is the sheaf on Nilp^op_{W(F̄_p)} with Aut_G(X̃_b)(R) = {(α, β) : α ∈ Aut_B(X̃_{b,R}), β ∈ Aut(µ̃_{p^∞,R}), α respects the polarization up to β}. (Lemma 4.2.10) It is representable by a formal scheme over Spf W(F̄_p), locally of the form Spf W(R) for a perfect ring R.
items.note: Proof (p. 704): forgetting the extra structures is a closed embedding. For a completely slope divisible X_b = ⊕ X_i (Oort–Zink, a separate item), Aut(X̃_b) is a closed subfunctor of a product of copies of 𝓗om(X_i, X_j)[1/p], i ≥ j. Each factor is the universal cover of H_{X_i,X_j} (Lemma 4.1.7), hence representable by Proposition 4.1.2. The perfect-ring description follows from rigidity of universal covers [SW13, Prop. 3.1.3] (a separate item). IG.0 plans 'the automorphism group scheme' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum'). This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corollary 4.3.5, in IG.1, lets Aut_G(X̃_b) act on the Igusa variety, so the group must sit in IG.0. IG.0 must import formal schemes (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.4) and universal covers (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.11 (structure of Aut_G(X̃_b))
items.statement: Let ρ be the half-sum of the positive roots, and regard the locally profinite set J_b(Q_p) as a formal scheme over W(F̄_p), whose sections over an open U ⊂ J_b(Q_p) are the continuous maps U → W(F̄_p). For unramified PEL data of type (A)/(C) as above, there is a natural map Aut_G(X̃_b) → J_b(Q_p) all of whose fibres are isomorphic to Spf W(F̄_p)[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]], with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Reduction to EL and simple PEL data ([Ham15, §4.1, Cor. 4.5]): Res_{F/Q_p}GL_n, GSp_n/O_F and GU_n/O_{F^+} (the last left as an exercise). For a general unramified F/Q_p the proof uses the O_F-linear internal Hom and the O_F-linear version of Lemma 4.1.8 (p. 706). The dimensions d_{i,j} = m_im_j(λ_j − λ_i) add up to ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ ([Ham15, App. A]). Remark 4.2.12 treats µ_{p^∞} × Q_p/Z_p. Remark 4.2.13 says d is the dimension of central leaves [Ham15, Cor. 7.8]. IG.0 plans to 'Construct the connected/formal and profinite parts of Aut(X)' and the 'functorial action of the self-quasi-isogeny group J_b(Q_p)' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.14 (fibres of the local period map are Aut_G(X̃_b)-torsors)
items.statement: Aut_G(X̃_b) acts on 𝔐_{D^int}; the action of its adic generic fibre Aut_G(X̃_b)^ad_η over Spa(L, O_L) on M_{D^int} extends to M_{D,∞}, and π^b_HT is equivariant for the trivial action on Fℓ^b_{G,µ}. Let M̂_{D,∞} be the perfectoid space attached to the preperfectoid space M_{D,∞} [SW13, Prop. 2.3.6], and (M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞})^∧ the one attached to the preperfectoid closed subspace M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞} ⊂ M_{D,∞} ×_{Spa(Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} M_{D,∞} [SW13, Prop. 2.3.7]. (Proposition 4.2.14) The action map M̂_{D,∞} ×_{Spa(L,O_L)} Aut_G(X̃_b)^ad_η → (M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞})^∧ is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces.
items.locator: §4.2, discussion before Proposition 4.2.14 and Proposition 4.2.14, pp. 708–711
items.note: The proof goes through Lemma 4.2.15 and [SW13, Thm B]; the paper does not show that the target is a torsor in any topology. The perfectoid spaces M̂_{D,∞} and (M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞})^∧ are strong completions of preperfectoid spaces (a separate item). No stage plans this. IG.3 names no Rapoport–Zink space or local period map and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum. This paper's source route adds the proposition to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C), as an input of the product formula. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.15 (non-noetherian Berthelot: extending maps over R^+)
items.statement: Let R^+ be a Z_p-algebra that is integrally closed in R = R^+[1/p], and let G, H be p-divisible groups over R^+ such that the Newton polygon of G_s, and that of H_s, is independent of s ∈ Spec(R^+/p). A morphism f_R : G_R → H_R of p-divisible groups over R extends, necessarily uniquely, to a morphism f : G → H over R^+ if and only if, for every geometric rank-one point Spa(C, O_C) of Spa(R, R^+), the base change f_C : G_C → H_C extends to f_{O_C} : G_{O_C} → H_{O_C}.
items.note: The proof reduces to a valuation ring using R^+ = {f ∈ R : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ Spa(R, R^+)}. It then reduces to Lemma 4.2.16 over the valuation ring C^+/𝔪_{O_C} of characteristic p (p. 710). No stage plans the lemma. It goes to IG.3 with Propositions 4.2.14 and 4.2.22, which use it. IG.3 names no Rapoport–Zink space and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum; this paper's source route adds this geometry there. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.16 and Remark 4.2.17 (homomorphisms over valuation rings of characteristic p)
items.statement: (Lemma 4.2.16) Let V be a valuation ring of characteristic p with fraction field K, and G, H p-divisible groups over V with constant Newton polygon. Then Hom(G, H) → Hom(G_K, H_K) is a bijection. (Remark 4.2.17) Consequently the noetherian hypothesis can be removed from the main result of [Ber80]: the same bijection holds for p-divisible groups G, H with constant Newton polygon over an integral domain R of characteristic p that is integrally closed in its fraction field K. Indeed, whether a homomorphism over K extends to R is the question whether certain matrices over K have entries in R. Since R is integrally closed, this can be checked on the valuation rings of K containing R.
items.note: The proof of Lemma 4.2.16 first enlarges K to be algebraically closed, so that V is perfect. It then reduces to completely slope divisible groups ([OZ02, Props 1.3, 2.3], a separate item), which are base changed from F̄_p. Berthelot's full faithfulness of the Dieudonné functor over perfect valuation rings (a separate item) then reduces the claim to W(V)[1/p]^{ϕ^r=p^s} = W(K)[1/p]^{ϕ^r=p^s} (pp. 710–711). The main result of [Ber80], Theorem 4.7.2, is stated for connected normal schemes of characteristic p. Its reduction to discrete valuation rings uses the noetherian hypothesis. The printed Remark 4.2.17 says 'for any integral domain R', which is false without integral closedness. Example: let R = {f ∈ F̄_p[t] : f(0) = f(1)}, and let G be the étale p-divisible group over R whose Tate module is the rank-one Z_p-local system obtained from the trivial one on the normalization A^1 by gluing the fibres over 0 and 1 via multiplication by a ∈ Z_p^×, a ≠ 1. Then G_K ≅ Q_p/Z_p, so Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G_K) = Z_p, while Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G) = ker(a − 1) = 0. Lemma 4.2.15 already assumes R^+ integrally closed, so nothing else in the paper is affected. IG.0 plans 'isomorphism-versus-isogeny distinctions' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. This paper's source route places the lemma in IG.0. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.18 (surjectivity onto the b-stratum)
items.statement: Let C/Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}) be a complete algebraically closed extension with ring of integers O_C. Then π^b_HT : M_{D,∞}(C, O_C) → Fℓ^b_{G,µ}(C, O_C) is surjective.
items.note: Proof (p. 711): [SW13, Thm B] gives a p-divisible group over O_C with trivialized Tate module, an O_B-action and a principal polarization. The identification of G-bundles from the proof of Proposition 4.2.6 (the bundle from the proof of [SW13, Prop. 5.1.6], a separate item) and Theorem 4.1.4 then give the quasi-isogeny ρ. No stage plans the lemma. IG.3 names no local period map and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum. This paper's source route adds it to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Propositions 4.2.19–4.2.21 (dimension of partially proper adic spaces)
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with ring of integers O_K and residue field k; dimension means Krull dimension, the length of the longest chain of specializations. (Remark 4.2.20) A map f : X → Y of analytic adic spaces is partially proper if, for every complete nonarchimedean field K' with ring of integers O_{K'} and every open and bounded valuation subring K'^+ ⊂ O_{K'}, the map X(K', K'^+) → X(K', O_{K'}) ×_{Y(K', O_{K'})} Y(K', K'^+) is bijective. (Proposition 4.2.19) If X is partially proper over Spa(K, O_K), its dimension is the maximal transcendence degree, over k, of k(x) for x ∈ X, where k(x) is the residue field of the ring of integers O_{K(x)} of the completed residue field K(x). (Proposition 4.2.21) If f : X → Y is a map of partially proper adic spaces over Spa(K, O_K), x ∈ X a rank-one point with image y, and X_y = X ×_Y {y}, then dim cl_X{x} = dim cl_Y{y} + dim cl_{X_y}{x}.
items.note: Proofs: by partial properness, closures of rank-one points are Zariski–Riemann spaces of k(x)/k, and transcendence degree is additive in k(x)/k(y)/k. Partial properness of maps of analytic adic spaces is planned by AdicEtaleGeometry A2 ('Build diagonals, separated morphisms, proper and partially proper morphisms, valuative criteria') and, for small v-stacks, by DiamondEtaleCohomology C4. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3 only uses it for proper support. DiamondEtaleCohomology C8 plans the dimension theory of diamonds ('topological dimension, topological transcendence degree of complete fields', 'the local, base-change, composition and analytic dimension comparisons actually stated in the section'). It does not plan these statements about the Krull dimension of partially proper adic spaces. They are general dimension theory of analytic adic spaces, not Igusa geometry, so a separate source route adds them to C8. IG.3 already reaches C8 through its imports, which Propositions 4.2.22–4.2.23 need. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.22 (dimension of the automorphism group)
items.statement: For every complete nonarchimedean field K over O_Ĕ, the space Aut_G(X̃_b)^ad ×_{Spa(O_Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} Spa(K, O_K) is partially proper over Spa(K, O_K), of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Partial properness comes from Lemmas 4.2.15–4.2.16: a quasi-self-isogeny over Spa(C, O_C) that extends to Spa(C, C^+) respects the extra structures there. The dimension comes from Proposition 4.2.11. Each connected component is Spa(O_Ĕ[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]]) ×_{Spa(O_Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} Spa(K, O_K), which after tilting is topologically the d-dimensional open unit disc over K (pp. 712–713). No stage plans the proposition. IG.3 names no Rapoport–Zink geometry and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum. This paper's source route adds it to IG.3, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C), as an input of Proposition 4.2.23. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.23 (dimension of the Newton strata of the flag variety)
items.statement: dim Fℓ^b_{G,µ} = ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Fℓ_{G,µ} and M_{D,∞} are partially proper of dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩; the proof uses Lemma 4.2.18 and Propositions 4.2.14 and 4.2.21–4.2.22. The converse inequality picks 'y ∈ Fℓ_{G,µ}' where y ∈ Fℓ^b_{G,µ} is needed (sourceIssues E7). IG.4 uses the formula as its 'flag-stratum dimensions'. IG.0's 'dimension formulas in this PEL setting' are planned only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. The proof runs through the Rapoport–Zink geometry, so this paper's source route makes IG.3 the single owner of the formula, for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C). Theorem 2.7.3 of the non-compact sequel states the same dimension formula. It should import the formula from IG.3 and leave only the stratification to BunGAndNewtonStrata BG2–BG3.

items.name: Global unramified PEL data and their moduli spaces
items.statement: Global PEL data [Kot92b, §5]: B a finite-dimensional simple Q-algebra with centre F, V a faithful finitely generated B-module, * a positive involution on B with F^+ = F^{*=1}, and (·,·) a nondegenerate Q-valued alternating form on V with (bv, w) = (v, b*w); G(R) = {x ∈ End_{B⊗R}(V ⊗ R) : xx* ∈ R^×}, assumed connected (type D excluded); h : C → End_{B⊗R}(V ⊗ R) a *-homomorphism with (v, h(i)w) symmetric and positive definite on V ⊗ R, giving a Shimura datum. Unramified at p: B_{Q_p} is a product of matrix algebras over unramified extensions of Q_p, O_B ⊂ B is a *-stable maximal Z_(p)-order, and Λ ⊂ V is an O_B-stable Z_(p)-lattice self-dual for (·,·), defining a connected reductive G_{Z_(p)} with G_{Z_(p)}(R) = {x ∈ End_{O_B⊗R}(Λ ⊗ R) : xx* ∈ R^×}; K_p = G_{Z_(p)}(Z_p) is hyperspecial. For compact open K^p ⊂ G(A^p_f) and a place 𝔭 | p of E, Kottwitz's moduli space S_{K_pK^p} of abelian varieties with extra structures is defined over O_{E,𝔭}; its generic fibre is in most cases the Shimura variety of (G, {h}), and in general |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of it.
items.note: PELModuli M0 plans to 'Define integral, rational, and p-integral PEL data separately' and to 'Construct the similitude group'. M1 plans to 'Define the fibre categories of polarized abelian schemes with endomorphisms, Rosati compatibility, determinant condition, and level structure', allowing 'only the prime-to-p quasi-isogenies specified by the source' over a p-integral base. M2, 'For a good rational prime', requires 'the unramified order condition … and no nontrivial level at p' and will 'Prove the smoothness theorem'. M3 will 'Describe these forms by the relevant pointed-set obstruction ker¹(Q,G)' and 'Prove the actual indexing/comparison theorem'. These stages treat PEL data of types A, C and D, so they cover the paper's generality. §5.1 (p. 730) writes S_K for the PEL moduli problem, the disjoint union of |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety. The printed text there first writes |ker^1(G, Q)|. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: The Newton stratification of the special fibre and the local data at b
items.statement: Let F_q be the residue field of O_{E,𝔭}. The special fibre S_{K_pK^p} ×_{O_{E,𝔭}} F_q has a Newton stratification by locally closed strata S^b_{K_pK^p}, b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}). A point gives a p-divisible group with extra structures, hence an isocrystal with G-structure classified by some b ∈ B(G), and this b lies in B(G, µ^{-1}) [RR96]. For each b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}), choose as in [Man05, §3] a completely slope divisible p-divisible group X_b over F̄_q with extra structures giving rise to the σ-conjugacy class b. Let D_{int,b} be the integral data given by the base change of B, V, O_B, Λ to Z_p together with (µ, b). It is an unramified local PEL datum in the sense of §4.2, and 𝔐^b := 𝔐_{D_{int,b}} is its Rapoport–Zink space. 𝔐^b lives over O_Ĕ, where Ĕ now denotes the completion of the maximal unramified extension of E_𝔭.
items.note: IG.0 builds the Newton map and admissibility ('Build the Newton map into B(G_Qp,mu^(-1)) … Prove admissible Newton points, slope decompositions and dimension formulas in this PEL setting') only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum'). No other stage plans Newton strata of PEL special fibres. This paper's source route widens IG.0 to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C), next to the central leaves and Igusa varieties. The general statement needs Grothendieck's specialization theorem for the isocrystal with G-structure and the admissibility b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) [RR96]. The local data D_{int,b} and 𝔐^b are used in Mantovan's product formula and throughout the rest of §4.3 and §4.4. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, status, planning stages.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 and Proposition 4.3.3 (the perfect Igusa variety Ig^b)
items.statement: Let X_b be the completely slope divisible p-divisible group over F̄_q with extra structures (O_B-action and polarization) fixed for b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}). Ig^b is the functor on F̄_q-algebras R sending R to the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (A, ρ), where A ∈ 𝒮_{K_pK^p}(R) is an abelian variety with extra structures satisfying the determinant condition and ρ : A[p^∞] ≅ X_b ×_{F̄_p} R is an isomorphism compatible with the extra structures, required to preserve the polarization only up to a scalar, i.e. up to an automorphism of µ_{p^∞,R}. (Remark 4.3.2: this differs from Mantovan's Igusa varieties.) Proposition 4.3.3: Ig^b is representable by a scheme. Indeed Ig^b → 𝒮_{K_pK^p} ×_{O_{E,𝔭}} F̄_q is relatively representable: it is the inverse limit over n of the schemes parametrizing isomorphisms 𝒜[p^n] ≅ X_b[p^n] compatible with the extra structures, 𝒜 the universal abelian variety.
items.note: Remark 4.3.2: Ig^b differs from Mantovan's Igusa varieties; Proposition 4.3.8 identifies it with the perfection of I^b_Mant. The item is missing. IG.1 plans to 'Construct Ig^X by trivializing the PEL p-divisible group over the leaf', but 'with the same fixed PEL datum' as IG.0, which instantiates the moduli objects 'for this split datum' of the non-compact sequel. This paper constructs Ig^b for every PEL datum of type (A) or (C) that is unramified at p, with hyperspecial K_p, and assumes no compactness (pp. 713–715). The item belongs to IG.1 once that layer is blueprinted in this generality. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.4 and Corollary 4.3.5 (Aut_G(X̃_b) acts; Ig^b is perfect)
items.statement: For an F̄_q-algebra R, Ig^b(R) is identified with the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (A, ρ̃). Here A ∈ 𝒮_{K_pK^p}(R) is an abelian variety considered up to p-power isogeny respecting the extra structures, and ρ̃ : A[p^∞] → X_b ×_{F̄_p} R is a quasi-isogeny respecting the extra structures. Given such a pair, there is a unique A' with extra structures and a p-power isogeny A' → A for which the induced quasi-isogeny A'[p^∞] → X_b ×_{F̄_p} R is an isomorphism. Corollary 4.3.5: the formal group scheme Aut_G(X̃_b) of Definition 4.2.9 acts canonically on Ig^b by acting on ρ̃ (quasi-isogenies of X_b are the automorphisms of X̃_b). This extends the evident action of the automorphisms of X_b respecting the extra structures. Moreover Ig^b is perfect: its Frobenius is an automorphism, because pullback along Frobenius is an equivalence on abelian varieties up to p-power isogeny (Verschiebung is an inverse up to multiplication by p) and on p-divisible groups up to quasi-isogeny.
items.note: Perfectness: pullback along Frobenius is an equivalence on abelian varieties up to p-power isogeny, since Verschiebung is an inverse up to multiplication by p, and on p-divisible groups up to quasi-isogeny. The item is missing. IG.1 plans to 'Prove its perfectness' and to 'construct the J_b(Q_p) action'. IG.0 plans 'the automorphism group scheme' and the 'functorial action of the self-quasi-isogeny group J_b(Q_p)'. All of these are for the fixed split datum of the non-compact sequel, and neither stage names the action of the formal group scheme Aut_G(X̃_b) of Definition 4.2.9. That group scheme is to be built in IG.0 for PEL data of type (A) or (C) unramified at p. The item belongs to IG.1 once that layer is widened to these data. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Central leaves and Mantovan's Igusa varieties (Definition 4.3.6)
items.statement: The central leaf C^b ⊂ 𝒮^b_{K_pK^p} ×_{F_q} F̄_q is the set of points x with 𝒜_x[p^∞] ×_{κ(x)} κ(x)‾ ≅ X_b ×_{F̄_p} κ(x)‾. By [Man05, Prop. 1] it is closed and, with its reduced structure, a smooth subscheme. Unlike Ig^b, it depends on the choice of X_b within its isogeny class. Write X_b = ⊕_{i=1}^r X_i with X_i isoclinic of strictly decreasing slopes λ_i ∈ [0, 1]. The p-divisible group 𝒢_b of 𝒜 over C^b is completely slope divisible. Its slope filtration 0 ⊂ 𝒢_{b,1} ⊂ … ⊂ 𝒢_{b,r} = 𝒢_b has graded pieces 𝒢^i_b = 𝒢_{b,i}/𝒢_{b,i−1}, isoclinic of slope λ_i. The O_B-action and the polarization respect the filtration, so each 𝒢^i_b has an O_B-action, and there are induced polarizations 𝒢^i_b → (𝒢^j_b)^∨ whenever λ_i + λ_j = 1. Definition 4.3.6: the (pro-)Igusa variety I^b_Mant → C^b parametrizes, over a C^b-scheme S, tuples (ρ_i)_{i=1}^r of isomorphisms ρ_i : 𝒢^i_b ×_{C^b} S ≅ X_i ×_{F̄_p} S that are compatible with the O_B-actions and commute with the polarizations up to an automorphism of µ_{p^∞,S}. Remark 4.3.7: I^b_{Mant,m} parametrizes isomorphisms ρ_{i,m} : 𝒢^i_b[p^m] ≅ X_i[p^m] ×_{F̄_p} S that respect the extra structures and fppf-locally lift to every level m' ≥ m. By [Man05, Prop. 4], its reduced subscheme is a finite étale Galois cover of C^b. By Lemma 4.1.5, the images of Aut(X_i[p^{m+k}]) in Aut(X_i[p^m]) stabilize to an open and closed subscheme of H_{X_i,X_i}[p^m], so I^b_{Mant,m} → C^b is a quasi-torsor under an étale group scheme. By [Man05, Prop. 4] it is then a torsor, and in particular I^b_{Mant,m} is reduced. Finally, I^b_Mant = lim_m I^b_{Mant,m} is a pro-étale cover of C^b.
items.note: C^b depends on X_b within its isogeny class, unlike Ig^b. IG.0 plans the central leaf 'for a p-divisible group X over algebraically closed k of characteristic p with its O_F and polarization structures' in the split datum of the non-compact sequel. IG.1 plans the finite-level models 'for completely slope-divisible X' with 'the same fixed PEL datum'. Neither covers O_B-actions of general PEL type (A)/(C), so the item stays missing. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 1.12 = Proposition 4.3.8 (Ig^b is the perfection of Mantovan's Igusa variety)
items.statement: Work in the setting of §4.3: global PEL data of type (A) or (C), unramified at p, with K_p hyperspecial; b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}); X_b completely slope divisible with extra structures. The natural map Ig^b → I^b_Mant = lim_m I^b_{Mant,m} to Mantovan's Igusa variety over the leaf C^b identifies the perfect scheme Ig^b with the perfection of I^b_Mant. Consequently H^i(Ig^b, Z/ℓ^nZ) = colim_m H^i(I^b_{Mant,m}, Z/ℓ^nZ). The group J_b(Q_p) ⊂ Aut_G(X̃_b) acts on Ig^b, whereas only a submonoid of J_b(Q_p) acts on I^b_Mant. The paper leaves to the reader the check that the resulting J_b(Q_p)-action on cohomology is the one constructed by Mantovan.
items.note: Proof: over the perfection, the slope filtration of G_b splits canonically, using the isomorphisms F^s/p^{t_i} with λ_i = t_i/s. The first half of Proposition 1.12 (Ig^b is a perfect scheme representing the moduli problem) is items 74–75. IG.1 plans the same identification ('identify their perfected limit with Ig^X') only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Corollary 4.3.9 (Ig^b → C^b is faithfully flat)
items.statement: The map Ig^b → C^b is faithfully flat. Proof: I^b_Mant is a cofiltered limit of smooth schemes along affine transition maps, so its Frobenius is faithfully flat. Hence Ig^b → I^b_Mant is faithfully flat, since it identifies Ig^b with the perfection of I^b_Mant (Proposition 4.3.8). Also I^b_Mant → C^b is faithfully flat. The paper adds a sketched remark that is not part of the corollary. The map Ig^b → C^b is evidently a quasi-torsor under the group scheme of automorphisms of X_b respecting the extra structures, so, being faithfully flat, it is a torsor under that group. C^b is smooth, the group is highly nonreduced (like Spec F̄_p[[X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_d^{1/p^∞}]]/(X_1, …, X_d)), and the torsor Ig^b is perfect. From this one can deduce, for example via the transitivity triangle of cotangent complexes, that dim C^b = d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: The later arguments do not depend on the dimension statement. Corollary 6.1.4 uses dim Fℓ^b_{G,µ} = ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ (Proposition 4.2.23) instead. The proof of Theorem 6.3.1(1), which passes to compactly supported Igusa cohomology by Poincaré duality, needs only that the cohomology is concentrated in one degree. Remark 4.2.13 attributes the dimension of central leaves to [Ham15, Cor. 7.8]. IG.1 plans 'the Γ_X=Aut(X)(k)-torsor over (C^X)_perf' and its distinction 'from the original generally nonreduced Aut(X)-torsor', but only for the sequel's split datum. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemmas 4.3.10 and 4.3.12 (the canonical lift of Ig^b and the isomorphism 𝔛^b_{O_K} ≅ Ig^b_{O_K} ×_{O_Ĕ} 𝔐^b)
items.statement: Since Ig^b is perfect, it lifts uniquely to a flat p-adic formal scheme Ig^b_{O_Ĕ} over W(F̄_q) = O_Ĕ. On Nilp_{O_Ĕ} it parametrizes abelian varieties in 𝒮_{K_pK^p} up to p-power isogeny, with an isomorphism between the universal cover of A[p^∞] and (the canonical lift of) X̃_b respecting all extra structures. Fix (X_b)_{O_K} ∈ 𝔐^b(O_K), a lift of X_b up to quasi-isogeny, with extra structures, to the ring of integers of a complete nonarchimedean field K/Ĕ. Such a lift exists with K = Ĕ because 𝔐^b is formally smooth. Lemma 4.3.10: for R ∈ Nilp_{O_K}, Ig^b_{O_K}(R) = (Ig^b_{O_Ĕ} ×_{O_Ĕ} O_K)(R) is the set of pairs (A, ρ) with A ∈ 𝒮_{K_pK^p}(R) an abelian variety with extra structure and ρ : A[p^∞] ≅ (X_b)_{O_K} ×_{O_K} R an isomorphism compatible with the extra structure. Definition 4.3.11: 𝔛^b sends R ∈ Nilp_{O_Ĕ} to the set of pairs (A, ρ) with A ∈ 𝒮_{K_pK^p}(R) and ρ : A[p^∞] ×_R R/p → X_b ×_{F̄_q} R/p a quasi-isogeny compatible with the O_B-action, and with the polarization up to an automorphism of µ̃_{p^∞,R/p}. Lemma 4.3.12: for R ∈ Nilp_{O_K}, define a map on pairs ((A, ρ), (𝒢, ρ')) as follows. Lift ρ' uniquely to a quasi-isogeny 𝒢 → (X_b)_{O_K} ×_{O_K} R, and take the unique quasi-isogeny A' → A of p-power order under which A'[p^∞] → A[p^∞] becomes the composite quasi-isogeny 𝒢 → A[p^∞]. The map sends the pair to (A', ρ'). This gives an isomorphism Ig^b_{O_K} ×_{O_Ĕ} 𝔐^b ≅ 𝔛^b_{O_K} compatible with the projections to 𝔐^b, where 𝔛^b → 𝔐^b is (A, ρ) ↦ (A[p^∞], ρ). In particular, taking K = Ĕ, 𝔛^b is representable by a formal scheme.
items.note: The paper would like 𝔛^b to be an Aut_G(X̃_b)-torsor over the completion of 𝒮_{K_pK^p} along 𝒮^b_{K_pK^p}, but only the quasi-torsor property is clear; the J_b(Q_p)-torsor of Proposition 4.3.13 is offered instead (p. 720). The printed Definition 4.3.11 has the base Nilp_{O_{E,𝔭}}; Nilp_{O_Ĕ} is meant, because ρ takes values in X_b ×_{F̄_q} R/p and Lemma 4.3.12 treats 𝔛^b over O_Ĕ. arXiv v1 prints the same. The item is missing. IG.3 plans to 'Construct the canonical formal lift of the perfect Igusa schemes to O_C and its perfectoid generic fibers', but only for the split datum of the non-compact sequel, and it names no Rapoport–Zink space. The decomposition 𝔛^b_{O_K} ≅ Ig^b_{O_K} ×_{O_Ĕ} 𝔐^b over the formal Rapoport–Zink space 𝔐^b of Definition 4.2.1 has to be added to IG.3 when that layer is widened to PEL data of type (A) or (C) unramified at p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name.

items.name: Proposition 1.13 = Proposition 4.3.13 (the J_b(Q_p)-torsor over a Newton stratum)
items.statement: Let S be a scheme over F̄_p and X a p-divisible group over S with extra structures (O_B-action and polarization, in the PEL setting of §4.3). Suppose that for some b ∈ B(G) all fibres of X are quasi-isogenous to X_b compatibly with the extra structures. Then there is a natural J_b(Q_p)-torsor over S: a torsor on S_proét under the sheaf of groups attached to the topological group J_b(Q_p), in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze [BS15]. Its fibre at any geometric point x̄ is the set of quasi-isogenies between X_x̄ and X_b compatible with the extra structures, and it depends only on X up to isogeny. If S is connected and locally topologically noetherian and x̄ is a geometric point, the torsor corresponds to a homomorphism π_1^proét(S, x̄) → J_b(Q_p). Proposition 1.13 is the case X = A[p^∞] over a Newton stratum 𝒮^b_K ⊂ 𝒮_K ⊗ F̄_p of the integral model at hyperspecial level. This stratum is of finite type over F̄_p, hence noetherian, so the homomorphism is π_1^proét(S, x̄) → J_b(Q_p) with S the connected component of 𝒮^b_K containing x̄.
items.locator: §1, Proposition 1.13, Remark 1.14, pp. 656–657; §4.3, Proposition 4.3.13, Remark 4.3.14, pp. 720–724
items.note: Remarks 1.14 and 4.3.14 add the following, without proof. The image of π_1^proét may be noncompact. It is compact if X admits a slope decomposition (or is isogenous to such an X); this explains [OZ02, Ex. 4.2], a p-divisible group over a nonnormal base that is not isogenous to one with a slope filtration. For the basic stratum the image is a discrete cocompact subgroup of J_b(Q_p), related to p-adic uniformization. On the leaf 𝒞_b ⊂ 𝒮^b_K the map π_1(𝒞_b, x̄) → J_b(Q_p) takes values in a compact open subgroup and corresponds to Mantovan's tower I^b_{Mant,m} → 𝒞_b (p. 657). The printed text differs: Proposition 1.13 writes π_1^proét(𝒮^b_K, x̄) without assuming 𝒮^b_K connected, whereas Remark 4.3.14 defines the homomorphism only for connected S. The statement above therefore uses the connected component containing x̄. Proof (pp. 721–724): reduce to S perfect, where the quasi-isogenies with X_b form a J_b(Q_p)-quasitorsor on S_proét. Over a strictly henselian perfect base a quasi-isogeny exists by Lemma 4.3.15. In general, étale locally and after replacing X by a quasi-isogenous group, X[p^n] ≅ X_b[p^n]. For n large, the K_b-quasitorsor of isomorphisms with X_b is then a torsor, hence a pro-étale cover over which a quasi-isogeny exists. This uses [Sch13a, Lemma 4.4], Lemma 4.3.15 with Remark 4.3.16, and Lemma 4.1.5. The paper does not use the proposition later. The pro-étale fundamental group and torsors under J_b(Q_p) on S_proét are defined in a separate item. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 plans to 'Supply descent, isomorphism-versus-isogeny distinctions and the automorphism group scheme', and the 'functorial action of the self-quasi-isogeny group J_b(Q_p)', only for the split unitary datum of Caraiani–Scholze's non-compact sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.15 and Remark 4.3.16 (constant Newton polygon over strictly henselian perfect rings)
items.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian perfect ring with residue field k. Then G ↦ G_k is an equivalence from the category of p-divisible groups over R with constant Newton polygon, up to isogeny, to the category of p-divisible groups over k up to isogeny. The proof shows that every such G is isogenous to G_0 ×_{F̄_p} R for a (completely slope divisible) p-divisible group G_0 over F̄_p. Remark 4.3.16: let G and H be p-divisible groups over R with constant Newton polygon. There is a constant c, depending only on the heights of G and H, such that for every homomorphism ψ_k : G_k → H_k over k, p^cψ_k lifts to a homomorphism G → H, necessarily unique (cf. [OZ02, Cor. 3.4]).
items.note: Inputs: full faithfulness of the Dieudonné functor over perfect rings (Gabber, from [Ber80]; cf. [Lau13, Thm D]); Lemma 4.2.16 for domains; minimal primes and the v-cover R → R̃ [BS17, Thm 4.1(i)]; cf. [OZ02, Cor. 3.4, 3.6]. The lemma is used only in the proof of Proposition 4.3.13, which the paper says 'will not be used in the sequel'. It is therefore not on the path to Theorem 1.15. The item is missing. IG.0 plans to 'Supply descent, isomorphism-versus-isogeny distinctions' only 'For a p-divisible group X over algebraically closed k of characteristic p with its O_F and polarization structures', in the split datum of the non-compact sequel. The lemma concerns p-divisible groups without extra structure over strictly henselian perfect rings. It belongs to IG.0, together with Proposition 4.3.13. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Definition 4.3.17, Remark 4.3.18 and Corollary 4.3.19 (the infinite-level space X^b_∞)
items.statement: Let X^b = (𝔛^b)^ad_η. Definition 4.3.17: X^b_∞ sends a complete affinoid (Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O_{Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞})})-algebra (R, R^+) to the set of triples (𝒜, ρ, α) with (𝒜, ρ) ∈ X^b(R, R^+) and α : Λ → T_p𝒜 a morphism of O_B-modules such that (1) the pairing on Λ matches the pairing on T_p𝒜 induced by the polarization and the fixed choice of p-power roots of unity; and (2) the induced maps Λ → T_p𝒜^ad_η(C, C^+) are isomorphisms at all geometric points Spa(C, C^+) of Spa(R, R^+). Remark 4.3.18: sending an abelian variety to its p-divisible group gives maps 𝔛^b → 𝔐^b and X^b_∞ → M^b_∞, and X^b_∞ = X^b ×_{M^b} M^b_∞; so X^b_∞ is representable by an adic space. Corollary 4.3.19: (Ig^b_{O_K})^ad_η ×_{Spa(Ĕ, O_Ĕ)} M^b_∞ ≅ X^b_{∞,K}. In particular X^b_∞ is preperfectoid, because M^b_∞ is preperfectoid and Ig^b_{O_K} is locally W(R) ⊗_{O_Ĕ} O_K with R perfect, so its generic fibre is perfectoid when K is perfectoid.
items.note: M^b_∞ is preperfectoid by Theorem 4.2.4. Preperfectoid spaces and their strong completions [SW13, Def. 2.3.4, Prop. 2.3.6] are planned by no layer and form a separate item. The item is missing. IG.3 plans 'the canonical formal lift of the perfect Igusa schemes to O_C and its perfectoid generic fibers', but only for the split datum of the non-compact sequel, and it names no Rapoport–Zink space. The space X^b_∞ and its decomposition over M^b_∞ have to be added to IG.3 when that layer is widened to PEL data of type (A) or (C) unramified at p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.20 (the product formula)
items.statement: Let X̂^b_∞ be the perfectoid space associated with the preperfectoid space X^b_∞ [SW13, Prop. 2.3.6], and let 𝒮_{K^p} be the perfectoid Shimura variety of infinite level at p over E_𝔭. Let 𝒮^b_{K^p} ⊂ 𝒮_{K^p} be the locus of points Spa(K, K^+) over which the universal abelian variety extends to K^+ and defines a point of 𝒮^b_{K_pK^p} over the residue field of K^+. This is the preimage, under the continuous specialization map, of the locally closed subset 𝒮^b_{K_pK^p} ⊂ 𝒮_{K_pK^p} ×_{O_{E,𝔭}} F_q, so it is locally closed. Lemma 4.3.20: X̂^b_∞ maps to 𝒮^b_{K^p} by forgetting ρ, and to M^b_∞ by (𝒜, ρ, α) ↦ (𝒜[p^∞], ρ, α). These maps are compatible with π_HT and π^b_HT (Remark 4.2.8), and the induced map X̂^b_∞ → (M^b_∞ ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} 𝒮^b_{K^p})^∧ is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces. Equivalently, the square formed by X^b_∞ → M^b_∞, X^b_∞ → 𝒮^b_{K^p}, π^b_HT and π_HT is Cartesian on points with values in perfectoid spaces.
items.note: The square commutes by Remark 4.2.8. The proof uses [SW13, Thm B] on (C, O_C)-points and Lemma 4.2.15 for general perfectoid (R, R^+). The printed statement says 'The perfectoid space X̂^b maps to 𝒮^b_{K^p}', where X̂^b_∞ is meant: the display and the diagram use X̂^b_∞, and X^b carries no trivialization α. It also describes the map to M^b_∞ as (𝒜, ρ) ↦ (𝒜[p^∞], ρ), leaving out the trivialization α that has to be carried along. arXiv v1 prints the same. The item is missing. IG.3 plans to 'Construct the actual maps from Ig_C^(X,tor) and Ig_C^(X,*) to the corresponding period-map fibers' by the direct construction of the non-compact sequel and for its split datum. It names neither Rapoport–Zink spaces nor the product formula. The product formula has to be added to IG.3 as the compact-case proof of the fibre theorem (Theorem 4.4.4), for PEL data of type (A) or (C) unramified at p. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.1 (stalks of pushforwards are cohomology of fibres)
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a quasicompact quasiseparated map of analytic adic spaces, where X is either a locally strongly noetherian adic space or a perfectoid space over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), and Y is perfectoid. (Footnote 24: it suffices that X, Y and all fibres of f over geometric points have well-defined étale sites; for example, X and Y both perfectoid.) Let x ∈ X have residue field K(x) with open bounded valuation subring K(x)^+. Let C(x̄) be a completed algebraic closure of K(x) with an open bounded valuation subring C(x̄)^+ lifting K(x)^+, giving a geometric point x̄ = Spa(C(x̄), C(x̄)^+) → X. Let Y_x̄ = (Y ×_X Spa(C(x̄), C(x̄)^+))^∧, a perfectoid space over C(x̄). Then for every sheaf 𝒢 of abelian groups on Y_ét and every i ≥ 0, the natural map (R^if_*𝒢)_x̄ → H^i(Y_x̄, 𝒢) is an isomorphism. The same holds for sheaves of groups with i = 0, 1 and for sheaves of sets with i = 0.
items.note: Proof in the paper: Y_x̄ ~ lim_j Y ×_X U_j over the étale neighbourhoods U_j of x̄ [SW13, Prop. 2.4.3], followed by [Sch12, Cor. 7.18], which by footnote 25 is also valid when all terms are perfectoid. DiamondEtaleCohomology C0 plans to 'Prove 14.4–14.11: the limit-preservation assertions, … continuity of étale cohomology', and ECD Proposition 14.9, which it covers, has exactly the three cases of the lemma: sheaves of sets for i = 0, sheaves of groups for i = 0, 1, and abelian sheaves for all i. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 plans the 'geometric stalks', 'the stalk formula over strict localization' and 'continuity under the cofiltered limits used in the classical proofs'. The passage between analytic adic spaces and their diamonds is DiamondsAndVStacks D6 ('Prove ECD Lemma 15.6 in full: … the étale and finite étale site comparisons'). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.2 (cohomology is determined by rank-one points)
items.statement: Let X be a quasicompact quasiseparated analytic adic space; for definiteness, X is perfectoid (footnote 26: the lemma also holds for X strongly noetherian, or whenever X has a well-behaved étale site). Let U ⊂ X be a quasicompact open subset containing all rank-one points of X. Then for every locally constant sheaf 𝒢 of abelian groups on X_ét and every i ≥ 0, the natural map H^i(X, 𝒢) → H^i(U, 𝒢) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: it suffices that 𝒢 → Rj_*𝒢 is an isomorphism. By Lemma 4.4.1 this can be checked at a geometric point Spa(C, C^+), where U = Spa(C, D^+) and both spaces are strictly local. No layer states the lemma. The only atlas mention of rank-one points in this sense is IG.3 ('open immersions with the same rank-one points'), for the sequel's datum. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3 (étale cohomology of a perfect scheme, of its lift over O_C and of its perfectoid generic fibre)
items.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p. Let X be a perfect scheme over F̄_p, and C a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field whose residue field contains F̄_p. Let 𝔛_{O_C} be the flat formal scheme over Spf O_C that is the unique lifting of X ×_{F̄_p} O_C/p, and 𝒳_C = (𝔛_{O_C})^ad_η its generic fibre, which is a perfectoid space. Then for all i the canonical maps H^i(X, Z/ℓ^nZ) ← H^i(𝔛_{O_C}, Z/ℓ^nZ) → H^i(𝒳_C, Z/ℓ^nZ) are isomorphisms.
items.note: Proof outline: reduce to the perfection of an affine X_0 of finite type over F̄_p. The formal scheme has the étale site of its special fibre, and invariance under change of algebraically closed field gives the first isomorphism. Tilting reduces to C of characteristic p, where 𝒳_C ~ lim_Frob X_{0,C}. Then [Hub96, Cor. 3.5.17], [DK73, XIII 2.1.4] and the universal local acyclicity of X_0 → Spec F̄_p [Del77, Th. finitude, Th. 2.13] show that the nearby cycles are Z/ℓ^n. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:formal-adic-comparison plans Huber 3.5.13–3.5.16, with 3.5.16 over microbial valuation rings that need not be discrete. It identifies 3.5.17 with the nearby cycles only 'for a strictly henselian rank-one DVR'. H1:valuation-nearby-cycles plans nearby cycles over arbitrary valuation bases, which covers O_C, and H1:valuation-exports makes them compatible with the formal–adic comparison. IG.3 plans 'the canonical formal lift of the perfect Igusa schemes to O_C and its perfectoid generic fibers', for the sequel's datum. No layer states the lemma for an arbitrary perfect scheme. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name.

items.name: Theorem 1.15 = Theorem 4.4.4 (stalks of Rπ_HT* Z/ℓ^n are the cohomology of Igusa varieties)
items.statement: Assume the global PEL data of §4.3 (type (A) or (C), unramified at p, K_p hyperspecial), and that S_{K^pK_p} is proper over O_{E,𝔭}; this is equivalent to G being anisotropic over Q [Lan11]. Let ℓ ≠ p, K^p sufficiently small, π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} the Hodge–Tate period map, and b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}). For every geometric point x̄ of Fℓ_{G,µ} lying in Fℓ^b_{G,µ} and all i there are isomorphisms (R^iπ_HT* Z/ℓ^nZ)_x̄ ≅ H^i(Ig^b, Z/ℓ^nZ) ≅ colim_m H^i(I^b_{Mant,m}, Z/ℓ^nZ). They depend only on the choice of a lift of x̄ to M^b_∞, and they are compatible with the Hecke action of G(A^p_f). Theorem 1.15 states this as (Rπ_HT* Z/ℓ^nZ)_x̄ ≅ RΓ(Ig^b, Z/ℓ^nZ).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 4.4.1 (a stalk is the cohomology of the fibre); Lemma 4.4.2 (reduction to a rank-one point); the argument of Lemma 4.2.18 (every rank-one point of the fibre lies in S^b_{K^p}); Lemma 4.2.18 itself (lifting x̄ to M^b_∞); Lemma 4.3.20 and Corollary 4.3.19 (the fibre is (Ig^b_{O_C})^ad_η); Lemma 4.4.3 (passage to the special fibre); and Proposition 4.3.8. Here S_{K^p} is built from the PEL moduli space, which is |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety. The paper adds that a version with the local system of an algebraic representation ξ can be formulated, but it does not carry this out. IG.3 plans the compactified analogue only for the non-compact datum of the sequel (its Theorem 4.1.1 and Corollary 4.1.2). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator.

items.name: The unitary setup of §5.1
items.statement: F = F^+·K is the compositum of a totally real field F^+ and an imaginary quadratic field K, c is the nontrivial element of Gal(F/F^+), and Spl_{F/F^+} is the set of rational primes v such that every prime of F^+ above v splits in F. G/Q is the unitary similitude group of an alternating hermitian form ⟨ , ⟩ on an F-vector space V with dim_F V = n, subject to (1) F^+ ≠ Q; (2) every rational prime ramified in F lies in Spl_{F/F^+}; (3) G is quasi-split at all finite places (footnote 27: (2) implies (1)). An R-algebra homomorphism h : C → End_F(V)_R with h(z^c) = h(z)^c for all z ∈ C and with (v, w) ↦ ⟨v, h(i)w⟩ symmetric and positive definite makes (F, c, V, ⟨ , ⟩, h) a PEL datum. Because c is an involution of the second kind, this datum is of type (A) in Kottwitz's classification [Kot92b]. (G, {h}) is a Shimura datum with Hodge cocharacter µ and reflex field E, and S_K denotes the PEL moduli space, the disjoint union of |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety. The prime p is unramified in F and split in K (so p ∈ Spl_{F/F^+}); 𝔭 | p is a prime of E, and K = K^pK_p ⊂ G(A_f) is sufficiently small with K_p ⊂ G(Q_p) hyperspecial, so that S_K has a good integral model 𝒮_K over O_{E_𝔭}. Write p_1, …, p_m for the primes of F^+ above p, write p = uu^c in K, and write p_i also for the place of F above p_i and u. Then G_{Q_p} = ∏_i Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} GL_n × G_m, where the G_m-factor is the similitude factor and the GL-factors come from V ⊗_Q Q_p → ⊕_i V ⊗_F F_{p_i}. Accordingly b = ((b_i)_i, b_0) ∈ ∏_i B(Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} GL_n) × B(G_m) and J_b = ∏_i J_{b_i} × G_m; every irreducible π_p of G(Q_p) is ⊗_i π_{p_i} ⊗ π_0 with π_0 a character of Q_p^×; and G_n⃗(Q_p) = ∏_i GL_n⃗(F_{p_i}) × Q_p^×.
items.note: Footnote 27: (2) implies (1). The paper cites the classification into types (A), (C) and (D) as 'page 375 of [Kot85]'; [Kot85] occupies pp. 201–220, and page 375 lies in [Kot92b] (pp. 373–444). No stage describes this datum. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration fixes the non-compact sequel's datum ('Instantiate PELModuli M0–M3's actual integral-model objects for this split datum'; 'These geometric constructions do not assert results for every Hodge-type or arbitrary Shimura datum'), and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison says that 'The global CS specialization assumes its CM field F=F^+F_0, [F^+:Q]>1, splitting at the auxiliary p'. Here n and the signature at each infinite place are arbitrary (G is quasi-split at the finite places but not necessarily at ∞), and p need only split in K, so the setup belongs to the Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Endoscopic data, transfer factors and the fundamental lemma
items.statement: Let F be a local or global field of characteristic 0 and G a connected reductive group over F. An endoscopic triple (H, s, η) for G consists of a quasi-split connected reductive group H over F, an element s ∈ Z(Ĥ) and an embedding of complex Lie groups η : Ĥ → Ĝ satisfying the conditions of [Kot84, 7.4]; it is elliptic if (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° ⊂ Z(Ĝ), Γ = Gal(F̄/F), and E^ell(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of elliptic endoscopic triples, isomorphism being taken in the sense of [Shi10, §2.1], which is stronger than that of [Kot84]. If G^der is simply connected, then, with L-groups formed using Weil groups, η extends to an L-morphism η̃ : ^LH → ^LG [Lan79, Prop. 1]. For F local, η̃ determines the Langlands–Shelstad transfer factor Δ : H(F)_{ss,(G,H)-reg} × G(F)_ss → C, canonical up to a nonzero constant [LS87]. Transfer and the fundamental lemma (Ngô, Waldspurger): for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) there is φ^H ∈ C_c^∞(H(F)) with SO^{H(F)}_{γ_H}(φ^H) = Σ_{γ ∈ G(F)_ss/∼} Δ(γ_H, γ) e(G_γ) O^{G(F)}_γ(φ); if H, G and η̃ are unramified and φ ∈ H^ur(G(F)), then Δ can be normalised so that φ^H = η̃^*(φ), where η̃^* : H^ur(G(F)) → H^ur(H(F)) is induced by η̃ via the Satake isomorphism; in particular the idempotent of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of G(F) may be transferred to the idempotent of a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of H(F).
items.note: ET.0: 'Define endoscopic triples and equivalence, ellipticity, relevant embeddings, z-extensions and endoscopic groups of Levi subgroups', with 'Shin stable Igusa §§2–4' (where the notion of isomorphism used here is defined) among its sources; the L-morphism η̃ of [Lan79, Prop. 1] belongs with these endoscopic data. ET.1: 'Construct the factors from a-data, chi-data, splittings and the cohomological pairings, including discriminants and the absolute normalization'. ET.3: 'Prove characteristic-zero local smooth transfer through Waldspurger's fundamental-lemma-implies-transfer argument … State exactly which standard unramified Hecke functions match'. All three are stated for general reductive groups over local or global fields of characteristic 0; ET.3 keeps the residue-characteristic bounds of its proof and notes that 'The global application may enlarge S'. The paper prints ellipticity as (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° ⊂ Z(G) (sourceIssues E8) and sets Γ := Gal(Q̄/Q), although F is an arbitrary local or global field. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Acceptable functions and Shin's test functions (Definition 5.2.2)
items.statement: A function φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) is acceptable if it satisfies the conditions of [Shi09, Def. 6.2], the main one being that φ is a linear combination of functions φ^p × φ_p with φ_p supported on ν_b-acceptable elements of J_b(Q_p), i.e. on δ = (δ_i) ∈ ∏_{i=1}^r Aut^0(X_i) such that v_p(e_i) < v_p(e_j) for all eigenvalues e_i of δ_i and e_j of δ_j whenever λ_i > λ_j [Shi09, Def. 6.1], the λ_i being the slopes of X_b. By Remark 5.2.1 this separates the components of J_b(Q_p) of different slopes by p-adic valuation, which is what allows functions to be transferred from J_b(Q_p) to G(Q_p) ([Shi10, L. 3.9], [HT01, L. V.5.2]); by [Shi09, L. 6.3] the twist of any φ by a sufficiently high power of Frobenius is acceptable. Definition 5.2.2: for acceptable φ = ∏_{v≠∞} φ_v with φ_v ∈ C_c^∞(G(Q_v)) for v ≠ p and φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)), and (H, s, η) ∈ E^ell(G), φ^H := φ^{H,p}φ^H_pφ^H_∞ ∈ C_c^∞(H(A)), where φ^{H,p} is the Langlands–Shelstad transfer of φ^p, φ^H_∞ is Kottwitz's function [Kot90, §7] with the trivial algebraic representation of G as input (the local system on I^b_Mant being Q̄_ℓ), and φ^H_p is Shin's function [Shi10, §6].
items.note: ET.5 plans these constructions: 'Construct acceptable elements/functions in J_b(Q_p), Frobenius-Hecke correspondences and their fixed points', 'Stabilize away from p by ET.1/3 and at infinity by the explicit pseudocoefficients', and 'At p construct the relation between endoscopy of J_b and endoscopy of G via its Levi data; … construct the matching p-test function'. It does so only for the Igusa varieties it takes from IG.0–IG.1 ('Consume only IG.0–IG.1's finite-level Igusa varieties'), which belong to the non-compact sequel's split unitary datum of rank 2n. Here conditions (ii)–(iii) of [Shi09, Def. 6.2], and [Shi09, L. 6.3], concern fixed points of Hecke–Frobenius correspondences on the Igusa varieties of the compact data of §§5.1 and 5.6, and J_b = ∏_i J_{b_i} × G_m involves inner forms of Levi subgroups of Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p}GL_n for arbitrary unramified F_{p_i}. ET.5 must be widened to these data, together with IG.0–IG.1. The archimedean function for an inner form G_R of arbitrary signature is a separate item. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.3 (Shin: stable trace formula for Igusa varieties)
items.statement: Let φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) be an acceptable function of the form ∏_{v≠∞} φ_v, and let φ^H be as in Definition 5.2.2 for (H, s, η) ∈ E^ell(G) (the PEL datum being unramified at p, with K_p hyperspecial). Then tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| Σ_{(H,s,η) ∈ E^ell(G)} ι(G, H) ST^H_e(φ^H) [Shi10, Thm 7.2], where ker^1(Q, G) = ker(H^1(Q, G) → ∏_v H^1(Q_v, G)), ι(G, H) = τ(G)τ(H)^{-1}|Out(H, s, η)|^{-1}, and ST^H_e(φ^H) is a sum of stable orbital integrals over representatives of the Q-elliptic semisimple stable conjugacy classes in H(Q). By Remark 5.2.4 the formula holds for every PEL Shimura variety of type (A) or (C).
items.note: [Shi10, Thm 7.2].
