ET.5 plans the same identity ('prove the stable Igusa identity, including ker^1 and iota(G,H) factors') only for the Igusa varieties of IG.0–IG.1, which belong to the non-compact sequel's split datum; Mantovan's Igusa varieties for compact PEL data are item 76. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Corollary 5.2.5 and Remark 5.2.6 (Shin's formula for the unitary group)
items.statement: For the group G of §5.1, E^ell(G) depends only on the quasi-split inner form G_n, and an isomorphism G ×_Q A_f ≅ G_n ×_Q A_f is fixed (G being quasi-split at all finite places). For n⃗ = (n_i)_{i=1}^s with positive entries, G_n⃗ is the quasi-split group over Q sending a Q-algebra R to {(λ, g) ∈ R^× × GL_n⃗(F ⊗_Q R) : g·Φ_n⃗·ᵗg^c = λΦ_n⃗}, where GL_n⃗ = ∏_i GL_{n_i}, i_n⃗ : GL_n⃗ → GL_{Σ n_i} is the natural map, Φ_n⃗ = i_n⃗(Φ_{n_1}, …, Φ_{n_s}) and (Φ_m)_{ij} = (−1)^{i+1}δ_{i,m+1−j} ([Shi11, §3.1]). Representatives of E^ell(G_n) are (G_n, 1, id) and (G_{n_1,n_2}, (1, (I_{n_1}, −I_{n_2})), η_{n_1,n_2}) with n_1 + n_2 = n and n_1 ≥ n_2 > 0; a pair (n_1, n_2) with n_1 and n_2 both odd may have to be excluded [Kot84, 7.4.3], and η_{n_1,n_2} is induced by GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2} ↪ GL_n. Let ϖ : A_K^×/K^× → C^× be a Hecke character whose restriction to A^×/Q^× corresponds to the quadratic character of K/Q, chosen ramified only at primes of Spl_{F/F^+} ([Shi11, Lemma 7.1]); it extends η_{n_1,n_2} to η̃_{n_1,n_2} : ^LG_{n_1,n_2} → ^LG_n. Away from p and ∞ the explicit transfer factors of [Shi11, §3.4] are used, with η̃^*_{n_1,n_2} on H^ur at unramified places. The function φ^n⃗_∞ is an explicit linear combination of the Euler–Poincaré functions φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} over the discrete L-parameters φ_{G_n⃗} with η̃∘φ_{G_n⃗} corresponding to the trivial algebraic representation of G_C ([Shi11, (5.11)]). Corollary 5.2.5: if φ^p·φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) is acceptable, then tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| Σ_{G_n⃗} ι(G, G_n⃗) ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ^n⃗), where G_n⃗ runs over these representatives and φ^n⃗ is obtained from φ as in Definition 5.2.2. Remark 5.2.6: ι(G, G_n⃗) = ½τ(G)τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} if n⃗ = (n/2, n/2), and ι(G, G_n⃗) = τ(G)τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} otherwise.
items.note: Corollary 5.2.5 is Theorem 5.2.3 for G, with E^ell(G) = E^ell(G_n) described as in [Shi11, §§3.1–3.5]. G_R is an inner form of G_n of arbitrary signature, so q(G) = ½dim(G(R)/K_∞A°_∞) (p. 738), whereas [Shi11] treats a group of Harris–Taylor type; the archimedean functions for arbitrary signature are a separate item. The layers that own the corollary plan it only for the non-compact sequel's group of rank 2n: ET.0 'For the groups G_(n_i) of CSnc §5.2 compute the finite list of elliptic endoscopic data and their explicit L-morphisms'; ET.1 'explicit discrete-series/Euler–Poincaré pseudocoefficient formulas in the unitary cases used below'; ET.5 'prove the stable Igusa identity, including ker^1 and iota(G,H) factors' for the Igusa varieties of IG.0–IG.1. They must be widened to arbitrary n, odd n included, and arbitrary signature. The paper prints the range as n_1 ≥ n_2 ≥ 0 (n_2 = 0 would list (G_n, 1, id) twice; [Shi11, §3.2] has n_1 ≥ n_2 > 0) and cites the choice of ϖ as '[Shi11, Prop. 7.1]'; the result is [Shi11, Lemma 7.1]. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Base change, the twisted group and Lefschetz functions
items.statement: Let 𝒢_n⃗ := Res_{K/Q}(G_n⃗ ×_Q K). There are L-morphisms BC_n⃗ : ^LG_n⃗ → ^L𝒢_n⃗ and ζ̃_{n_1,n_2} : ^L𝒢_{n_1,n_2} → ^L𝒢_n with BC_n∘η̃_{n_1,n_2} = ζ̃_{n_1,n_2}∘BC_{n_1,n_2} (5.3.1). Let S be a finite set of primes containing ∞, p and the primes where F or ϖ ramifies, arranged so that S_fin ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+}. For a finite place v ∉ S, BC_n⃗ induces BC^*_n⃗ : H^ur(𝒢_n⃗(Q_v)) → H^ur(G_n⃗(Q_v)); for v ∈ S_fin a BC-transfer φ_v ∈ C_c^∞(G_n⃗(Q_v)) of f_v ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(Q_v)) is defined as in [Shi11, §4.2]; BC^*_n⃗ is surjective when v splits in K (for example v = p), and a transfer ζ̃^*_n⃗ is defined compatibly. At ∞, for an irreducible algebraic representation ξ of (G_n⃗)_C and Ξ := ξ ⊗ ξ, Labesse's twisted Lefschetz function f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ} [Lab91] and the Euler–Poincaré function φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} are BC-matching. Let 𝒢^+_n⃗ := (Res_{K/Q}GL_1 × Res_{F/Q}GL_n⃗) ⋊ {1, θ} with θ(λ, g)θ^{-1} = (λ^c, λ^c g^♯) and g^♯ = Φ_n⃗ ᵗg^{−c} Φ_n⃗^{−1}; then 𝒢_n⃗ ⋊ Gal(K/Q) ≅ 𝒢^+_n⃗ with c ↦ θ, and the two cosets are written 𝒢_n⃗ and 𝒢_n⃗θ. For f ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n⃗(A)) (with trivial character on A°_{𝒢_n⃗,∞}) and fθ its translate by θ, the invariant twisted trace formula gives I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_geom(fθ) = I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(fθ) (5.3.2) ([Art88a], [Art88b]).
items.note: ET.4 plans the twisted space in general ('Construct the cyclic-restriction-of-scalars twisted space and its invariant twisted trace identity'), but the transfers and the functions at ∞ only for the non-compact sequel's groups: 'For CSnc's G_(n_i), build the finite-place transfer maps and infinity pseudocoefficients and prove all commuting diagrams of L-morphisms, spherical Hecke transfers and traces', with its bad places handled by 'the small bad-place level N_0'. Here Σ_i n_i = n is arbitrary (ζ̃_n⃗ depends on the parity of n − n_i, p. 745) and the bad places satisfy S_fin ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+}, so ET.4 must be widened. The paper prints g^♯ = Φ_n⃗ ᵗg^c Φ_n⃗^{-1}, which reverses products; θ is an automorphism only with ᵗg^{−c}, as in [Shi11, (4.2)]. It names the Hecke character ψ once (sourceIssues E9). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.1 (Shin: geometric side as stable orbital integrals)
items.statement: For BC-matching φ = φ^Sφ_{S_fin}φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} and f = f^Sf_{S_fin}f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ}, I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_geom(fθ) = τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ).
items.note: [Shi11, Cor. 4.7]. Proof: [Lab99, Thm 4.3.4] rewrites the stable orbital integrals as the elliptic part of the twisted trace formula; f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ} is cuspidal, so only θ-elliptic elements contribute, and [F^+ : Q] ≥ 2 leaves only 𝒢_n⃗θ itself. ET.4 plans this ('Prove that [F^+:Q]>1 rules out the proper cuspidal twisted subsets in the source argument … Deduce the specific equality of stable elliptic terms with the discrete twisted trace') only 'For CSnc's G_(n_i)', the endoscopic groups of the non-compact sequel's group of rank 2n. Here Σ_i n_i = n is arbitrary, so ET.4 must be widened. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: status, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.2 (the Igusa trace as twisted spectral sides)
items.statement: Let (f^n)^S ∈ H^ur(𝒢_n(A^S)) and f^n_{S_fin∖{p}} ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n(A_{S_fin∖{p}})) be arbitrary, φ^S and φ_{S_fin∖{p}} their BC-transfers, φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)) acceptable and φ := φ^S·φ_{S_fin∖{p}}·φ_p. For each G_n⃗ let φ^n⃗ be as in Definition 5.2.2 and f^n⃗ := (f^n⃗)^S·(f^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}}·f^n⃗_p·f^n⃗_∞, where (f^n⃗)^S and (f^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}} are the transfers of (f^n)^S and f^n_{S_fin∖{p}} along ζ̃, BC^*_n⃗(f^n⃗_p) = φ^n⃗_p (BC^*_n⃗ is surjective at p), and f^n⃗_∞ is the linear combination of Lefschetz functions for the representations Ξ(φ_n⃗) of 𝒢_n⃗ with η̃∘φ_n⃗ corresponding to the trivial representation of G ([Shi11, (6.7)], formed here for the inner form G_R of arbitrary signature, with q(G) = ½dim(G(R)/K_∞A°_∞)). Then tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]) = |ker^1(Q, G)|τ(G) Σ_{G_n⃗} ε_n⃗ I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ), where ε_n⃗ = ½ if n⃗ = (n/2, n/2) and ε_n⃗ = 1 otherwise.
items.note: Proof: Corollary 5.2.5, Remark 5.2.6, Proposition 5.3.1 and (5.3.2). G_R has arbitrary signature, and q(G) = ½dim(G(R)/K_∞A°_∞) (p. 738). The non-compact sequel's identical first clause of its Theorem 5.6.1 is planned at ET.4 and ET.7b, but these layers are written for its datum: ET.4 'For CSnc's G_(n_i)', ET.5 for 'IG.0–IG.1's finite-level Igusa varieties', and ET.7b 'Combine ET.5 with ET.4 and the explicit CSnc §5.6 test functions'. They must be widened to arbitrary n, arbitrary signature and the compact data of §5.1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.3 (Shin: the twisted spectral side)
items.statement: I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ) = Σ_M |W_M||W_G|^{-1} |det(Φ_n⃗^{-1}θ − 1)_{a^{𝒢θ}_M}|^{-1} Σ_{Π_M} tr(n-Ind^{𝒢_n⃗}_Q(Π_M)_ξ(f^n⃗) ∘ A'), Π_M running over Φ_n⃗^{-1}θ-stable subrepresentations of R_{M,disc}.
items.note: [Shi11, Prop. 4.8, Cor. 4.14]; Remark 5.3.4 explains the twist by ξ, the normalized intertwiner A' and the θ-stability of n-Ind^{𝒢_n⃗}_Q(Π_M)_ξ. ET.4 plans the spectral simplification ('Deduce the specific equality of stable elliptic terms with the discrete twisted trace and its factors of two/signs. Prove every discarded parabolic term vanishes under these test-function hypotheses') only 'For CSnc's G_(n_i)'; here Σ_i n_i = n is arbitrary, so ET.4 must be widened. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: status, planning stages.

items.name: Decent elements and J_b as an inner form of the Levi M_b
items.statement: b admits a decent representative b̃ ((b̃σ)^s = sν_b̃(p)σ^s, [RZ96, Def. 1.8], [Kot85, §4.3]) with ν defined over Q_p (G quasi-split); M_b = Cent_G(ν) is a Q_p-rational Levi, b is basic in M_b and J_b is an inner form of M_b.
items.note: BG0: 'Construct J_b as its algebraic sigma-centralizer and prove representability and its inner-Levi description'; BG1: 'Prove the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) used in FS III, including basic classes, the centralizer Levi'. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: planning stages.

items.name: Shin's transfer at p and the map Red^b_n⃗
items.statement: For an elliptic endoscopic group G_n⃗ of G, E^eff_p(J_b, G, G_n⃗) is the set of certain isomorphism classes of G_n⃗-endoscopic triples (M_{G_n⃗}, s_n⃗, η_n⃗) for J_b(Q_p) defined in [Shi10, §6.2]. From an acceptable φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)), Shin's φ^n⃗_p is obtained by transfer from J_b(Q_p) to M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p) followed by a nonstandard transfer from M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p) to G_n⃗(Q_p), which uses the acceptability of φ_p [Shi10, L. 3.9]. Dually, Red^b_n⃗ : Groth(G_n⃗(Q_p)) → Groth(J_b(Q_p)) is the composite of (1) Groth(G_n⃗(Q_p)) → ⊕_{(M_{G_n⃗}, s_n⃗, η_n⃗) ∈ E^eff_p(J_b, G, G_n⃗)} Groth(M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p)), on each summand a linear combination of normalized Jacquet functors indexed by a finite set of allowed Levi embeddings M_{G_n⃗} ↪ G_n⃗; (2) Groth(M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p)) → Groth(M_b(Q_p)), the functorial transfer along η̃_n⃗, which is a normalized parabolic induction since both groups are restrictions of scalars of products of general linear groups; (3) the Langlands–Jacquet map Groth(M_b(Q_p)) → Groth(J_b(Q_p)) of [Bad07] (see [Shi11, §5.5] for the precise definitions). For n⃗ = (n), E^eff_p(J_b, G, G_n) = {(M_b, 1, id)} and Red^b_n is a normalized Jacquet functor followed by the Langlands–Jacquet map (Remark 5.4.1).
items.note: [Shi11, §5.5]; the paper remarks that its case is slightly more general but the formulas are exact analogues (p. 739). It says that E^eff_p is 'defined in Section 6.2 of [Shi09]'; the set is defined in [Shi10, §6.2]. ET.6 plans step (3) in general ('Prove the Grothendieck-group extension and compatibility with Jacquet/induction operations used for J_b'). The rest is planned only for the non-compact sequel's datum: ET.5 'At p construct the relation between endoscopy of J_b and endoscopy of G via its Levi data; prove Shin's Kottwitz-invariant/transfer-factor identity and construct the matching p-test function', for 'IG.0–IG.1's finite-level Igusa varieties', and ET.7b 'Jacquet functors and inner-form transfer' with 'the explicit CSnc §5.6 test functions'. Here G_n⃗(Q_p) = ∏_i GL_n⃗(F_{p_i}) × Q_p^× with Σ_i n_i = n arbitrary and each F_{p_i} an arbitrary unramified extension of Q_p, so ET.5 and ET.7b must be widened. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.2 (Red^b_n⃗ is dual to φ ↦ φ^n⃗_p)
items.statement: For π_p ∈ Groth(G_n⃗(Q_p)), tr π_p(φ^n⃗_p) = tr(Red^b_n⃗(π_p))(φ_p).
items.note: Proof as for [Shi11, L. 5.10] (see also [Car12, L. 6.3–6.4] for a unitary group of slightly different signature): both constructions break into three mutually dual steps; the transfer from J_b(Q_p) to M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p) factors through the quasi-split M_b(Q_p); and the nonstandard transfer between M_{G_n⃗} and G_n⃗ is compatible by [Shi10, L. 3.9]. ET.5 ('construct the matching p-test function') and ET.7b ('Jacquet functors and inner-form transfer') plan this only for the non-compact sequel's datum; here Σ_i n_i = n is arbitrary and each F_{p_i} is an arbitrary unramified extension of Q_p, so both must be widened. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: status, planning stages.

items.name: Lemma 5.4.3 (generic principal series die under Red^b)
items.statement: Let π^n⃗_p ∈ Irr(G_n⃗(Q_p)) decompose as π^n⃗_p = ⊗_{i=1}^m π^n⃗_{p_i} ⊗ π^n⃗_0 according to G_n⃗(Q_p) = ∏_{i=1}^m GL_n⃗(F_{p_i}) × Q_p^×. If for some i the component π^n⃗_{p_i} transfers to a generic principal series representation of GL_n(F_{p_i}) and J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form of M_{b_i}, then Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p) = 0.
items.note: Proof: by [Shi10, §2] the L-morphism ^LM_{G_n⃗} → ^LM_b restricts η̃_{n_1,n_2}, so the image of π^n⃗_p in Groth(M_b(Q_p)) has only generic principal series as M_{b_i}(F_{p_i})-components, and such an element lies in the kernel of the Langlands–Jacquet map when J_{b_i} is not quasi-split ([Bad07, Thm 3.1, Prop. 3.3]). The paper prints the conclusion as Red^b_n⃗(π_p) = 0. ET.6 plans the local input in general ('Derive the source's nontransfer obstruction for generic principal-series parameters to a nontrivial inner form'). The lemma is a statement about Red^b_n⃗, which ET.7b plans only for the non-compact sequel's datum ('Jacquet functors and inner-form transfer', with 'the explicit CSnc §5.6 test functions'), and IG.5 uses its analogue only 'for p totally split'. ET.7b must be widened to arbitrary n and arbitrary unramified F_{p_i}. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.1 (the Igusa trace through θ-stable automorphic representations)
items.statement: Fix f^S ∈ H^ur(𝒢_n(A^S)) and f_{S_fin∖{p}} ∈ C_c^∞(𝒢_n(A_{S_fin∖{p}})), and let φ^S and φ_{S_fin∖{p}} be their base-change transfers to G_n(A^S) and G_n(A_{S_fin∖{p}}). Let φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)) be any function, not necessarily acceptable, and set φ := φ^S φ_{S_fin∖{p}} φ_p. Then tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]) is a finite linear combination of terms tr((Π^n⃗)^S((f^n⃗)^S) ∘ A^S) · tr((Π^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}}((f^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}}) ∘ A_{S_fin∖{p}}) · tr(Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p)(φ_p)), each attached to some G_n⃗ ∈ E^ell(G). Here (f^n⃗)^S and (f^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}} are the transfers of f^S and f_{S_fin∖{p}} along ζ̃_n⃗ (§5.3), and A^S and A_{S_fin∖{p}} are components of a normalized intertwiner. Π^n⃗ is a θ-stable isobaric irreducible automorphic representation of 𝒢_n⃗ of the form (n-Ind^{𝒢_n⃗}_Q Π_M)_ξ, with Π_M in the (relatively) discrete automorphic spectrum of the Levi M of a parabolic Q ⊂ 𝒢_n⃗, and Π^n⃗_∞ is cohomological for the trivial algebraic representation. Finally, π^n⃗_p ∈ Rep(G_n⃗(Q_p)) base changes to the component Π^n⃗_p.
items.note: After the proof of [Shi11, Thm 6.1] (printed 'Proposition 6.1 of [Shi11]'; p. 737 cites it correctly as Theorem 6.1): Theorem 5.3.2, Proposition 5.3.3, Moeglin–Waldspurger [MW89], Jacquet–Shalika [JS81], injectivity of base change at the split prime p, Lemma 5.4.2, and the argument of [Shi09, proof of L. 6.4] to remove acceptability. In that last step the paper speaks of twisting 'φ^p' by a high power of Frobenius (p. 743); it is φ_p that is twisted, by a central Frobenius element of J_b(Q_p). ET.4 and ET.7b plan the non-compact sequel's version (its Theorem 5.6.1 and Lemma 5.6.2; ET.7b: 'express the rational alternating Igusa representation by the specified automorphic representations, Jacquet functors and inner-form transfer') only for its split datum of rank 2n. They must be widened to arbitrary n and the compact data of §5.1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Corollary 5.5.2 and Remark 5.5.3 (Hecke eigensystems occurring in Igusa cohomology)
items.statement: Fix φ_{S_fin∖{p}} and φ_p. If Π^n⃗ is a θ-stable automorphic representation of 𝒢_n⃗ as in Lemma 5.5.1 that contributes to tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]), then the transfer ζ̃_n⃗,*((Π^n⃗)^S) of (Π^n⃗)^S to 𝒢 = 𝒢_n occurs in BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur}); conversely, every 𝒢(A^S)-subrepresentation of BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur}) is of the form Π^S with Π = ζ̃_n⃗,*(Π^n⃗). Remark 5.5.3: the same Π^S may come from Π^n⃗ for several G_n⃗ ∈ E^ell(G); in Case ST of [Shi11, §6] it comes both from an endoscopic group 𝒢_{n_1,n_2} and from a Levi subgroup M of 𝒢.
items.note: Proof: linear independence of unramified Hecke characters, applied to the finitely many terms of Lemma 5.5.1 (the sign of the normalized intertwiner A^S being ignored). Remark 5.5.3 refers to Case ST of [Shi11, §6]. ET.7b plans 'the finite local factorization and separation of Hecke eigencharacters with virtual multiplicities retained' only for the non-compact sequel's datum; it must be widened to arbitrary n and the compact data of §5.1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: L-algebraic and C-algebraic automorphic representations
items.statement: The notions of L-algebraic and C-algebraic automorphic representations of [BG14]; for general linear groups they differ by a character twist. If Π^n⃗_∞ is cohomological (Lemma 5.5.1), then Π^n⃗ is C-algebraic; writing Π^n⃗ = ψ ⊗ Π_1 ⊗ Π_2 on 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(A) = A_K^× × GL_{n_1}(A_F) × GL_{n_2}(A_F), each Π_i is a regular C-algebraic, θ-stable, isobaric automorphic representation of GL_{n_i}(A_F), and Π_i|det|^{(1−n_i)/2} is regular L-algebraic.
items.note: AF.4: 'distinguish C-algebraic and L-algebraic normalizations and record the half-root twist when definable'; AG2.0: 'Define regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized cases separately'. Both are stated for general groups. The decomposition of 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(A) is printed with A^×_{F_0} for A_K^× (sourceIssues E11). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Galois representations of regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations
items.statement: For a regular L-algebraic, conjugate self-dual, cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_m(A_F), m ≥ 1, there is a Galois representation r_Π : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_m(Q̄_ℓ) with WD(r_Π|Gal(F̄_q/F_q))^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{-1}rec(Π_q) at every finite place q of F not above ℓ, rec being normalized as in [HT01] ([Shi11], [CH13], [Car12]); by footnote 28, compatibility up to semisimplification suffices for the paper.
items.locator: §5.5, p. 744 and proof of Theorem 5.5.4, pp. 744–745
items.note: AG2.2 (the geometric construction, with its parity and Shin-regularity restrictions), AG2.3 (Chenevier–Harris: 'the arbitrary regular polarized branch') and AG2.5 (local–global comparison: 'Prove the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades under their stated assumptions'). Footnote 28: compatibility up to semisimplification suffices. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.4 (Galois representations for the pieces Π_i)
items.statement: Let Π^n⃗ be a θ-stable isobaric automorphic representation of 𝒢_{n_1,n_2} as in Lemma 5.5.1 (Π^n⃗_∞ cohomological for the trivial representation), written Π^n⃗ = ψ ⊗ Π_1 ⊗ Π_2 on 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(A) = A_K^× × GL_{n_1}(A_F) × GL_{n_2}(A_F), so that each Π_i is a regular C-algebraic, θ-stable, isobaric automorphic representation of GL_{n_i}(A_F) and Π_i|det|^{(1−n_i)/2} is regular L-algebraic. Then there is a Galois representation r_i : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{n_i}(Q̄_ℓ) such that WD(r_i|Gal(F̄_q/F_q))^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{-1}rec(Π_{i,q}|det|^{(1−n_i)/2}) for every place q of F, rec denoting the local Langlands correspondence normalized as in [HT01].
items.note: Proof: Π_i = n-Ind^{GL_{n_i}}_{Q_i}(Π_{M_i}) with Π_{M_i} Φ_{n_i}^{-1}θ-stable in the discrete spectrum of M_i, so by [MW89] Π_i is built from regular L-algebraic, conjugate self-dual, cuspidal representations, to which [Shi11], [CH13] and [Car12] apply. The theorem concerns GL_{n_i} over F for arbitrary n_i and is planned in that generality: AG2.0 'Define regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, essentially conjugate self-dual and polarized cases separately' and its agreement 'with rec(π_v ⊗ |det|^((1−n)/2)) in AG2.5'; AG2.2 'keep cuspidal parameters distinct from discrete isobaric parameters. Construct the representation for each discrete constituent with its explicit algebraic twists'; AG2.3 'the arbitrary regular polarized branch'; AG2.5 'Compare restrictions to Weil groups through the actual arbitrary-rank local Langlands construction ET.6'; ET.7a 'the required GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification'. The non-compact sequel's identical Theorem 5.7.1 is planned at AG2.0, AG2.2 and AG2.5. The cited sources give the compatibility at finite places not above ℓ, which is all the paper uses (unramified places and the auxiliary prime p ≠ ℓ); at places above ℓ the printed 'any place q' needs AG2.6 ('use the generalized log-crystalline weight spectral sequence for the full monodromy comparison where the source proves it'). The statement prints GL_n for GL_{n_i} and A^×_{F_0} for A_K^× (sourceIssues E10, E11). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Corollary 5.5.5 (Galois representations for Igusa Hecke eigensystems)
items.statement: Let Π^S be an irreducible admissible 𝒢(A^S)-subrepresentation of BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur}). Then there is a Galois representation r_{Π^S,ℓ} : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, whose Frobenius eigenvalues at every finite place v above a prime q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) match the Satake parameters of Π^S at v: the characteristic polynomial of r_{Π^S,ℓ}(Frob_v) is the image of X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} + ⋯ + (−1)^iq_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i} + ⋯ + (−1)^nq_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{n,v} under the Satake parameter map of Π^S and ι_ℓ^{-1}, where q_v is the order of the residue field of v and T_{i,v} ∈ Z[𝒢(Q_q)//𝒢(Z_q)] is the characteristic function of GL_n(O_{F_v}) diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) GL_n(O_{F_v}) × ∏_{w≠v} GL_n(O_{F_w}) × Z_q^× × Z_q^× (i entries ϖ_v) in 𝒢(Q_q) = ∏_{w|q} GL_n(F_w) × Q_q^× × Q_q^×.
items.note: Proof: choose Π^n⃗ = ψ ⊗ Π_1 ⊗ Π_2 as in Corollary 5.5.2 and r_i as in Theorem 5.5.4; then r_{Π^S,ℓ} = ⊕_{i=1}^2 r_i ⊗ ε_i, where ε_i corresponds to the L-algebraic character |det|^{(n_i−n)/2}ϖ(N_{F/K}∘det)^{ε(n−n_i)} of GL_{n_i}(A_F), ε(m) ∈ {0, 1} is the parity of m, and ϖ_∞(z) = (z/z̄)^{δ/2} with δ odd; Π^0|det|^{(1−n)/2} = n-Ind(Π^0_1 ⊗ Π^0_2), and normalized induction is compatible with rec. The paper writes Spl_{F_0/Q} for Spl_{K/Q} and prints T_{i,v} with Z_p^×, Q_p^× in place of Z_q^×, Q_q^× (sourceIssues E11, E12). AG2.0's 'normalization dictionary among algebraic weights, geometric/arithmetic Frobenius, cyclotomic twists, normalized Satake and the integral Hecke polynomial' is general. But AG2.2 plans the direct sum only 'with the required degree-2n Hecke polynomial' of the non-compact sequel's group, and ET.7b plans Corollary 5.5.2 only for that datum; the sequel's analogue, its Theorem 5.1.2, is planned there. Both must be widened to arbitrary n, including the twists by ϖ when n − n_i is odd. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Remark 5.5.6 (local–global compatibility at p)
items.statement: With Π := ζ̃_n⃗,*(Π^n⃗) for Π^n⃗ as in Corollary 5.5.2 and Π_p = (⊗_{i=1}^m Π_{p_i}) ⊗ Π_{p,0}, where p_1, …, p_m are the places of F above u fixed in §5.4, Π_{p_i} and r_{Π^S,ℓ}|Gal(F̄_{p_i}/F_{p_i}) correspond under the geometric normalization of the local Langlands correspondence for every i, by the local–global compatibility at p_i in Theorem 5.5.4. In particular, if r_{Π^S,ℓ}|Gal(F̄_{p_i}/F_{p_i}) = χ_{i,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{i,n} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{-1} not the cyclotomic character for all a ≠ b, then Π_{p_i} is a generic principal series representation of GL_n(F_{p_i}).
items.note: From the local–global compatibility at p_i in Theorem 5.5.4, the formula r_{Π^S,ℓ} = ⊕_i r_i ⊗ ε_i of the proof of Corollary 5.5.5, and the compatibility of rec with normalized parabolic induction and twists. Since pO_F = ∏_i p_ip_i^c, the p_i are the places of F above u fixed on p. 740; the remark prints them as 'the decomposition p = ∏_{i=1}^m p_i of p into prime ideals of F'. ET.6 plans the criterion for generic principal series in general ('prove the classification and induction compatibilities'). AG2.5 ('Compare restrictions to Weil groups through the actual arbitrary-rank local Langlands construction ET.6') plans the comparison only for the systems that AG2.2 builds, whose unitary direct sums have degree 2n. AG2.5 must be widened to the degree-n representations r_{Π^S,ℓ} of Corollary 5.5.5. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.7 (genericity forces the µ-ordinary stratum)
items.statement: Fix the prime 𝔭 | p of E and an isomorphism ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C compatible with E ↪ C and E ↪ E_𝔭 ↪ Q̄_p. Fix also a Galois representation r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ}; BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur})_r denotes the summand coming from the Π^S of Corollary 5.5.5 with r_{Π^S,ℓ} ≅ r. For each place p_i of F above u, let S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p^{-1}∘τ induces p_i}, and let G have signature (p_τ, q_τ) at τ. Assume that each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0. Assume also that for each i for which S_i contains such a τ, r|Gal(F̄_{p_i}/F_{p_i}) = χ_{i,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{i,n} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{-1} not the cyclotomic character for all a ≠ b. Then BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur})_r = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) that is not µ-ordinary (footnote 29: more accurately, µ^{-1}-ordinary).
items.note: Proof (pp. 747–748): if the summand is nonzero, some θ-stable Π^n⃗ with r_{Π,ℓ} ≅ r contributes; by Remark 5.5.6, π^n⃗_{p_i} transfers to a generic principal series for every i such that some τ ∈ S_i has p_τq_τ ≠ 0, so by Lemmas 5.4.3 and 5.5.1 there is no contribution unless all those J_{b_i} are quasi-split. Then B(G, µ^{-1}) = ∏_i B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}) with G_i = Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p}GL_n; B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}) is a single point when µ_i is central, and otherwise equals B(GL_n/F_{p_i}, µ_{i,τ}^{-1}) by the identification B(H/L) = B(L, H) stated in the proof on p. 748 (footnote 30 only remarks that the case L = Q_p was used before); Lemma 5.5.8 concludes. The paper defines S_i with 'ι_p ∘ τ'; since ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C, the embedding into Q̄_p is ι_p^{-1}∘τ. For p totally split and the non-compact sequel's datum, IG.5 plans the analogue ('Prove CSnc Corollary 5.1.3's obstruction: for p totally split … force b ordinary'); no stage covers a prime that is only split in K under the hypothesis on the sets S_i, so the theorem belongs to the Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.8 (only the µ-ordinary class has quasi-split J_b)
items.statement: For L p-adic and µ : t ↦ diag(t, …, t, 1, …, 1) (n − q entries t), exactly one b ∈ B(GL_n/L, µ^{-1}) has J_b quasi-split: the µ-ordinary element diag(ϖ^{-1}, …, ϖ^{-1}, 1, …, 1) (n − q entries ϖ^{-1}), with J_b ≅ GL_{n−q} × GL_q.
items.note: Proof: the slopes of b ∈ B(GL_n/L, µ^{-1}) lie in [−1, 0]; a nonintegral slope λ gives a factor of J_b that is a general linear group over the division algebra of invariant λ mod 1, so J_b quasi-split forces all slopes to be 0 or −1, and κ(b) = −µ in π_1(GL_n) = Z fixes their multiplicities. BG1 plans 'the classification/uniqueness assertions for B(G) used in FS III, including basic classes, the centralizer Levi' and BG0 J_b 'and its inner-Levi description', but neither says which classes of B(G, µ^{-1}) have quasi-split J_b, and no stage names the µ-ordinary element. The lemma belongs in BG1, importing BG0; the totally split case used by IG.5 then rests on the same lemma.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.1 (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties: no endoscopy)
items.statement: Let F = F^+·K and let (B, *, V, ⟨ , ⟩, h) be a PEL datum with B a division algebra with centre F, V a simple B-module and * an involution of the second kind (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties [Kot92a]); then S_K is proper and G has no endoscopy. Assume that B is split at all places above p (so that the constructions and results of §5.4 apply), let G_n be a quasi-split inner form of G over Q and fix G_n ≅ G over Q_p. If φ = φ^pφ_p ∈ C_c^∞(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) with φ_p acceptable, then tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| ι(G, G_n) ST^{G_n}_e(φ^{G_n}).
items.note: Proof: the other terms of the stable trace formula vanish by [Shi10, L. 7.1]. The paper follows [Shi12, §6], which assumes p inert in F^+; that assumption is not needed. No stage covers the Igusa varieties of Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties: ET.5 plans Shin's formula only for 'IG.0–IG.1's finite-level Igusa varieties' of the non-compact sequel's datum. The proposition belongs to the Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties, with the rest of §5.6. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Corollary 5.6.2 (Igusa cohomology of simple Shimura varieties)
items.statement: In Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)), [ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] = (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_{π_f} c(π_f)[π_f^p][Red^b_n(π_p)], the sum running over the admissible representations π_f of G(A_f) such that π_fπ_∞ is an automorphic representation of G for some representation π_∞ of G(R) cohomological for the trivial algebraic representation, with coefficients c(π_f) related to the automorphic multiplicity of π_fπ_∞ (an analogue of [Shi12, Cor. 6.12]).
items.note: From Proposition 5.6.1, the identity Red^b_n([H(S_K, Q̄_ℓ)]) = ε_G·d(G_R)·[H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] (the stable trace formula for S_K, [Art89, Thm 6.1] simplified as in [Shi12, Prop. 6.3], and Lemma 5.4.2 for G_n(Q_p) ≅ G(Q_p)), extended from acceptable to all φ_p by [Shi09, L. 6.4] (printed 'Lemma 6.4 of [Shi11]'; [Shi11] has no such lemma, and p. 743 cites [Shi09] for the same step), and Matsushima's formula. The corollary belongs to the Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties, which imports Matsushima's formula from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.4–AS.5 and ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.5, and the compact-quotient trace formula with Euler–Poincaré functions from AS.4–AS.6 and ET.1. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Corollary 5.6.3 (Theorem 5.5.7 for simple Shimura varieties)
items.statement: Let G be the group of a PEL datum (B, *, V, ⟨ , ⟩, h) in which B is a division algebra with centre F = F^+·K, V is a simple B-module and * is an involution of the second kind (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties). Assume B is split at all places above p, with p as in §5.1, and fix the prime 𝔭 | p of the reflex field E and ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C compatible with E. For a Galois representation r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), let [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]_r be the summand of [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] coming from the representations π of Corollary 5.6.2 with r_{π,ℓ} ≅ r. Here r_{π,ℓ} is attached to π through Shin's stable base change to GL_n. For each prime 𝔭_i of F above p, let S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p^{-1}∘τ induces 𝔭_i}, and let (p_τ, q_τ) be the signature of G at τ. Assume that each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0. Assume also that, for each i for which S_i contains such a τ, r|Gal(F̄_{𝔭_i}/F_{𝔭_i}) = χ_{i,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{i,n} is a direct sum of characters with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{-1} not the cyclotomic character for all a ≠ b. Then [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]_r = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) that is not µ-ordinary.
items.locator: §5.6, Corollary 5.6.3, p. 750; the summand [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]_r is defined on pp. 749–750
items.note: Proved 'in the same way' as Theorem 5.5.7 (p. 750). Corollary 5.6.2 supplies the expression of [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] through Red^b_n. B is split above p, so G(Q_p) ≅ ∏_i GL_n(F_{𝔭_i}) × Q_p^× as in §5.4, and the local argument through Lemmas 5.4.3 and 5.5.8 is unchanged. §5.6 treats Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties [Kot92a]. These include Shimura varieties with q-adic uniformisation for a prime q ≠ p, ℓ, where the result is related to level raising [Tho14] (p. 748). The representations r_{π,ℓ} are attached through Shin's stable base change to GL_n, in the appendix to [Gol14] (p. 749). The Part II imports that construction from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.2 ('Apply stable unitary base change … Construct the representation for each discrete constituent with its explicit algebraic twists'). The paper prints S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p∘τ induces 𝔭_i}, here and in Theorem 5.5.7 (p. 747), also in arXiv v1. Since ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C, that composite is undefined. The composite ι_p^{-1}∘τ : F ↪ Q̄_p is meant, as the identification τ : F → Q̄_p ≅ C on p. 748 shows, and the statement uses it. No stage covers this item. The Igusa cohomology of Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties has no owner, and IG.5 and IG.7 are fixed to the non-compact datum of the sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.1 (Illusie: nearby cycles preserve perversity)
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued non-archimedean field with ring of integers O_K, let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of K, and let ℓ be a prime invertible in O_K. Let X be a scheme of finite type over O_K and X_{O_C} = X ⊗_{O_K} O_C. Write j : X_η̄ = X ⊗_{O_K} C ↪ X_{O_C} for the geometric generic fibre and i : X_s̄ ↪ X_{O_C} for the geometric special fibre. If F is a perverse F_ℓ-sheaf on X_η = X ⊗_{O_K} K, then the nearby-cycle complex RψF = i^*Rj_*(F|_{X_η̄}) is a perverse sheaf on X_s̄ [Ill94, Cor. 4.5].
items.note: LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.6 plans this result: 'Prove the nearby-cycle t-exactness theorem in the trait setting with the source's excellent/constructibility hypotheses. State the convention explicitly: RΨ between fiberwise perverse categories is t-exact'. Its source is 'Illusie's monodromy/nearby-cycle exposition and SGA 7 XIII'. The paper uses the fibrewise convention: F is perverse on X_η and there is no shift. The passage from the strict henselisation to O_C is planned in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:formal-adic-comparison ('identify 3.5.17 for a strictly henselian rank-one DVR and a completed algebraic closure with the LPV.0 trait RΨ'). arXiv v1 assumed only that K is complete non-archimedean; 'discretely valued' was added in revision. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, planning stages.

items.name: Theorem 6.1.2 (Huber: algebraic and formal nearby cycles agree)
items.statement: Keep the situation of Theorem 6.1.1. Let 𝒳_η be the rigid-analytic variety over K associated with X, regarded as an adic space; as the definition of λ requires, this is the generic fibre of the formal completion of X. Let 𝒳_η̄ be its base change to C. Lift an étale map Y → X_s̄ to an étale map of formal schemes over O_C and take its generic fibre. This defines a morphism of sites λ : 𝒳_η̄,ét → (X_s̄)_ét. Let F^ad be the pullback of F along 𝒳_η → X_η. Then Rλ_*(F^ad|_{𝒳_η̄}) ≅ RψF [Hub96, Thm 3.5.13].
items.note: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:formal-adic-comparison plans this theorem for locally noetherian X with torsion coefficients, which covers X of finite type over O_K. It will 'construct the adjunction comparison i* Rj* K → Rb* a* K, and prove it an isomorphism for K in D⁺ with torsion coefficients (3.5.13)'. It will also 'identify 3.5.17 for a strictly henselian rank-one DVR and a completed algebraic closure with the LPV.0 trait RΨ', which gives the form over O_C used here. The paper prints 'the pullback of F under 𝒳_ét → X_ét' (p. 751; also in arXiv v1). F is a sheaf on X_η, so the pullback along 𝒳_{η,ét} → X_{η,ét} is meant, and the statement uses that form. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Equivariant sites and nearby cycles of K_p-equivariant formal models
items.statement: This item covers Scholze's equivariant étale sites for continuous actions of locally profinite groups, from §2 of the Lubin–Tate tower paper, which the paper cites as [Sch15b]. They are the sites (Fℓ_{G,µ}/G(Q_p))_ét and (S_{K^p}/G(Q_p))_ét, with the morphism π_HT/G(Q_p) between them. R(π_HT/G(Q_p))_*F_ℓ pulls back to Rπ_HT*F_ℓ along (Fℓ_{G,µ})_ét → (Fℓ_{G,µ}/G(Q_p))_ét. To see this, pass to slice categories to replace G(Q_p) by a compact open K_p [Prop. 2.9], then pass to the limit [Prop. 2.8]. For an étale U = Spa(A, A°) → Fℓ_{G,µ}, the action of every sufficiently small compact open K_p ⊂ G(Q_p) extends to a continuous action on U [Cor. 2.5]. Put 𝔘 = Spf(A°) and 𝔘_s = Spec(A°/p). Once K_p is small enough, it acts trivially on 𝔘_s, by continuity of the action and finite generation of A°/p. So every étale map to 𝔘_s̄ lifts to a K_p-equivariant étale map to 𝔘_{O_C}, where C = C_p, and this gives a morphism of sites λ_{U/K_p} : (U_η̄/K_p)_ét → 𝔘_s̄,ét. Finally, for sufficiently small K_p there is an equivalence of sites (S_{K^p,U}/K_p)_ét ≅ (S_{K_pK^p,U})_ét [Prop. 2.12].
items.locator: §6.1, before Proposition 6.1.3, p. 751; proof of Proposition 6.1.3, p. 752
items.note: The paper cites these results as [Sch15b], but its bibliography entry for [Sch15b] duplicates [Sch15a] (recorded misprint E13). arXiv v1 cites the Lubin–Tate tower paper here. No stage description mentions equivariant sites. The item belongs with the widening of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4 to compact Shimura varieties of Hodge type. Its text ('Construct the cofinal formal models of the flag variety', 'Prove the adic/scheme nearby-cycle comparison and filtered-colimit/finite-level compatibilities') is written only for the non-compact datum of the sequel. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, locator.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.3 (nearby cycles of Rπ_HT* F_ℓ are perverse)
items.statement: Let π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} be the Hodge–Tate period map of a compact Shimura variety of Hodge type, for a sufficiently small compact open subgroup K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p), and let x̄ be a geometric point of Fℓ_{G,µ}. Then x̄ has a neighbourhood basis of affinoid étale neighbourhoods U = Spa(A, A°) with the following property. Put 𝔘 = Spf(A°). Then Rλ_{U/K_p*}(R(π_HT/G(Q_p))_*F_ℓ)|_{U_η̄/K_p}[⟨2ρ, µ⟩] is a perverse sheaf on 𝔘_s̄ for every sufficiently small pro-p compact open subgroup K_p ⊂ G(Q_p). Here ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ is the dimension of the Shimura variety.
items.note: Proof (pp. 752–753). By [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1(i)], U can be chosen so that S_{K^p,U} = S_{K^p} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} U is affinoid perfectoid and is the preimage of an affinoid S_{K_pK^p,U} for every sufficiently small K_p. The map π_HT is partially proper. Modulo p, π_{HT,𝔘_s} factors through a map π_{HT,K_p,𝔘_s} : 𝔖_{K_pK^p,U,s} → 𝔘_s of affine schemes of finite type over F_p. This map satisfies the valuative criterion for rank-one valuation rings of algebraically closed fields, and is therefore finite (the separate item on finiteness from the rank-one valuative criterion). By footnote 32, π_{HT,𝔘_s} is ind-finite although π_{HT,U} has fibres of positive dimension. Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2 make the nearby cycles of F_ℓ on the formal model 𝔖_{K_pK^p,U} = Spf(R°_{K_pK^p,U}) perverse up to the shift ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ = dim S_{K_pK^p,U}, and pushforward along a finite map preserves perversity. The proof leaves one step implicit. Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2 concern schemes of finite type over the ring of integers of a complete discretely valued field, but 𝔖_{K_pK^p,U} is a formal scheme over O_C. It must first be related to such a scheme, for instance by descending to a finite extension of Q_p and algebraising with Elkik's theorem (the generic fibre is smooth). Otherwise a formal-scheme version of Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2 is needed. The paper says neither. The item belongs with the widening of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4, which plans only the lower bound of the non-compact case ('prove the exact source assertion Rψ(Rπ_HT,open,* F_ell) ∈ pD^(≥d)(Fl_k,F_ell) (CSnc Theorem 4.6.1)'). Full perversity for compact Shimura varieties of Hodge type has to be stated there as a separate theorem. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Corollary 6.1.4 (concentration for Igusa varieties at a minimal stratum)
items.statement: Suppose the Shimura variety is compact, of PEL type (A) or (C), with good reduction at p, as in Theorem 4.4.4, so that the perfect Igusa varieties Ig^b are defined; let ℓ ≠ p. Let S be a finite set of primes containing p with K^p = K^p_S K^S, where K^S ⊂ G(A_f^S) is a product of hyperspecial maximal compact open subgroups and K^p_S ⊂ G(A^p_S). Let T^S = Z[G(A_f^S)//K^S] be the abstract commutative Hecke algebra of K^S-bi-invariant compactly supported functions on G(A_f^S), acting on H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ). Fix a maximal ideal m ⊂ T^S. Among all b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) for which the m-torsion H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)[m] is nonzero for some i ∈ Z, choose one with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ minimal. Then H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)[m] is nonzero only for i = d.
items.note: Section 6.1 is stated for compact Hodge type, but Ig^b and Theorem 4.4.4 exist only in the compact PEL setting of §§4.3–4.4. The statement makes that implicit hypothesis explicit. The paper also does not say that S contains p, but it must: K^S ⊂ G(A_f^S) has no component at p because K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p). The proof uses only a commutative algebra of Hecke operators away from p acting on Rπ_HT*F_ℓ, so it works for any subalgebra of 𝕋^S. The proof of Theorem 6.3.1 needs that form, because there p ∉ S. It applies the corollary with S ∪ {p} in place of S, to the contraction of m to the operators at the primes of Spl_{K/Q} outside S ∪ {p, ℓ}. Proof: averaging over compact open subgroups of J_b(Q_p) shows that the m-torsion is nonzero exactly when the m-localisation is. (Rπ_HT*F_ℓ)_m is supported on the closed set Fℓ^{≥d}_{G,µ}, of dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − d (Proposition 4.2.23). The localised perverse nearby cycles of Proposition 6.1.3 are supported in that dimension. So their stalks at points whose closure has that dimension are concentrated in degree d (the separate item on stalks of perverse sheaves at generic points of their support). Finally, (Rπ_HT*F_ℓ)_{m,ȳ} = RΓ(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m is a colimit of such stalks. The proof prints 𝕋_S for 𝕋^S (p. 754; also in arXiv v1), and the statement uses 𝕋^S. The item belongs with the widening of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4. That stage plans only the one-sided bound of the non-compact case: 'Using flag-stratum dimensions and a Newton point of minimal d_b with nonzero localized cohomology, prove the lower bound i≥d_b in CSnc Lemma 2.8.4'. Concentration in the single degree d has to be stated there as a separate theorem. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.2 (decomposed generic reductions)
items.statement: Let L be a p-adic field (a finite extension of Q_p) with residue field of cardinality q, and let ℓ ≠ p. Let ρ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) be a continuous representation whose reduction ρ̄ is decomposed generic (Definition 6.2.1). The condition depends only on the semisimplification of ρ̄. Then ρ ≅ χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n is a direct sum of continuous characters, and χ_a/χ_b is not the cyclotomic character for any a ≠ b. In particular, the representation of GL_n(L) that corresponds to ρ under the local Langlands correspondence is a generic principal series representation.
items.note: Proof (p. 756). Conjugate ρ into GL_n(O), where O is the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_ℓ, and then into the matrices that are diagonal modulo a uniformiser ϖ. The obstructions to diagonalising modulo higher powers of ϖ lie in H^1(Gal(L̄/L), χ̄_a/χ̄_b) for a ≠ b. These groups vanish because H^1(Gal(L̄/L), χ̄_λ) = 0 for the unramified character χ̄_λ sending Frob to λ when λ ∉ {1, q}. The paper calls this well known. Since ℓ ≠ p, the local Euler characteristic formula and local Tate duality give dim H^1(χ̄_λ) = dim H^0(χ̄_λ) + dim H^0(χ̄_λ^{-1}ε̄), and both terms vanish because λ ≠ 1 and λ ≠ q. The principal series statement follows because no χ_a/χ_b is the cyclotomic character. No stage states this H^1-vanishing for a general p-adic field, so it stays inside this item. Definition 6.2.1 is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7 ('Compare a stronger decomposed-generic API only as a separate specialization'). The lemma belongs to the Part II, over an arbitrary p-adic field L. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5 plans a related local deformation argument only for L = Q_p at a totally split prime, under the weaker condition α_i ≠ pα_j ('Treat p≡1 mod ell and p≠1 mod ell separately using the local deformation argument'). The Part II should reuse its local Galois cohomology. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: The compact unitary Shimura varieties of §6.3 and the Hecke algebra T^S
items.statement: Fix a compact Shimura variety of PEL type attached to PEL data (B, *, V, (·,·)) of type A. Here F = F^+·K is a CM field with totally real subfield F^+, and K ⊂ F is an imaginary quadratic field. There are two cases. Case 1: B is a central division algebra over F, and V ≅ B is a simple B-module. Case 2: B = F, F^+ ≠ Q, the group G is quasi-split at all finite places, and F/F^+ is split at all places above every rational prime that ramifies in F. Let Spl_{F/F^+} be the set of rational primes q such that every place of F^+ above q splits in F. Fix a finite set S of primes such that F and G are unramified outside S; in Case 2, S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+}. Fix a sufficiently small compact open subgroup K = K_SK^S ⊂ G(A_f) = G(A_S) × G(A_f^S), where K^S is a product of hyperspecial maximal compact open subgroups K_q ⊂ G(Q_q). Fix a rational prime ℓ. The abstract Hecke algebra is T^S = ⊗_{q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ})} Z[G(Q_q)//K_q].
items.note: Case 2 is the setting of §5.1. Case 1 is Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties of §5.6. Compactness is assumed ('We fix a compact Shimura variety of PEL type'). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 6.3.1(1) (Galois representations for torsion Hecke eigensystems)
items.statement: Work in the setting of §6.3, Case 1 or Case 2. Let m ⊂ T^S be a maximal ideal such that H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 for some i ∈ Z. The cohomology is étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field. Then there is a unique semisimple continuous representation ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ), unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, with the following property. For every finite place v of F above a prime q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), the characteristic polynomial of ρ_m(Frob_v) is the image under a fixed embedding T^S/m ↪ F̄_ℓ of X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} + ⋯ + (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{i,v} X^{n−i} + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n−1)/2} T_{n,v}. Here q_v is the cardinality of the residue field at v. T_{i,v} ∈ Z[G(Q_q)//K_q] is the characteristic function of GL_n(O_{F_v}) diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) GL_n(O_{F_v}) × ∏_{w≠v} GL_n(O_{F_w}) × Z_q^×, with i entries ϖ_v, inside G(Q_q) = ∏_w GL_n(F_w) × Q_q^×, where w runs over the places of F above the same place of K as v. (The paper prints Z_p^× and Q_p^×; see recorded misprint E12.)
items.note: The proof (pp. 758–759) is written out in Case 2. In Case 1, Corollary 5.6.2 and the Galois representations of §5.6, attached through Shin's stable base change to GL_n, take the place of Lemma 5.5.1 and Corollary 5.5.5. Fix p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}). From here on, m is contracted to the Hecke operators away from p, which are the only ones acting at infinite level at p. The contraction is again a maximal ideal, and nonvanishing at m implies nonvanishing at it. Hochschild–Serre to infinite level at p, the Leray spectral sequence for π_HT and Theorem 4.4.4 give some b with H^*(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0. Among these b take one with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ minimal. Corollary 6.1.4, with S ∪ {p} for S, concentrates this cohomology in degree d. Taking invariants under a pro-p compact open subgroup of J_b(Q_p) shows the same for the Igusa varieties I^b_{Mant,m} of large enough level. Their localised Z_ℓ-cohomology is therefore flat and concentrated in degree d. Poincaré duality with the dual ideal passes to H_c. The m-part of [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S-ur} is then nonzero in the Grothendieck group, and so is its BC^p. By the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma, some Π^S as in Lemma 5.5.1 then has Hecke eigenvalues lifting m away from p. Corollary 5.5.5 attaches r_{Π^S,ℓ} to it. The semisimplified reduction of r_{Π^S,ℓ} has the required Frobenius polynomials at the places above the primes of Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ, p}). Uniqueness follows from Chebotarev's density theorem and the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem. The prime p was arbitrary, so running the argument for two different choices of p and using uniqueness also gives unramifiedness and the Frobenius polynomials at the places above p. The proof cites 'Theorem 5.5.5' where Corollary 5.5.5 is meant (p. 759). arXiv v1 cites its own Theorem 5.5.3 here, so the slip came with the renumbering in revision. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Theorem 6.3.1(2) (middle-degree concentration)
items.statement: Work in the setting of Theorem 6.3.1, and let m ⊂ T^S (with H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 for some i) and ρ_m be as in part (1). Suppose there are a rational prime p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), split as p = uu^c in K, and a prime 𝔭 | p of the reflex field E with the following property. Fix ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C compatible with E ↪ E_𝔭 ↪ Q̄_p. For each prime 𝔭_i of F above u (i = 1, …, m) let S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p^{-1}∘τ induces 𝔭_i}, as in Theorem 5.5.7, and let (p_τ, q_τ) be the signature of G at τ. The property: each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and whenever S_i contains such a τ, ρ_m is decomposed generic at 𝔭_i. (It is unramified there by part (1), since p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}.) Then H^j(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 only for j = dim S_K.
items.note: Proof (pp. 759–760), written out in Case 2. Throughout, localisation at m means localisation at the contraction of m to the Hecke operators at the primes of Spl_{K/Q} outside S ∪ {p, ℓ}. These are the only operators acting on H^*(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ), on Rπ_HT*F_ℓ and on the cohomology of Igusa varieties, and vanishing at the contraction implies vanishing at m. The dual ideal m^∨ satisfies the same hypothesis (the separate item on m^∨), so by Poincaré duality it suffices to prove H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for i < dim S_K. By the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence it then suffices to prove H^i(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for i < dim S_K. Take b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ minimal such that H^*(Ig^b, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0. As in part (1), this cohomology is concentrated in degree d, and there is a Galois representation r lifting ρ_m with BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S-ur})_r ≠ 0. By Lemma 6.2.2 and the hypotheses on p, 𝔭 and ρ_m, r satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 5.5.7, or of Corollary 5.6.3 in Case 1. So b is µ-ordinary. Hence d = ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ = dim S_K, and Corollary 6.1.4 gives H^i(Ig^{b'}, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for i < dim S_K and every b' ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}). Theorem 4.4.4 then gives (R^iπ_HT*F_ℓ)_m = 0 for i < dim S_K, and the Leray spectral sequence for π_HT concludes. The theorem refers to 'the sets S_i from Theorem 5.5.7', which are printed there as {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p∘τ induces 𝔭_i} (p. 747; also in arXiv v1). Since ι_p : Q̄_p ≅ C, that composite is undefined. The composite ι_p^{-1}∘τ : F ↪ Q̄_p is meant, as the identification τ : F → Q̄_p ≅ C on p. 748 shows, and the statement uses it. Decomposed genericity is Definition 6.2.1, which is planned at AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3 (how to satisfy condition (2))
items.statement: Remark 6.3.2: suppose some prime p is completely decomposed in F and ρ_m is unramified and decomposed generic at all places above p. By Chebotarev there are then many such p, so one may take p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}. Such a p lies in Spl_{K/Q}, and every set S_i in Theorem 6.3.1(2) has exactly one element, so the hypothesis of Theorem 6.3.1(2) holds. Remark 6.3.3: suppose the signature of G is (0, n) at all but one infinite place, and ρ_m is unramified and decomposed generic at some finite place v of F. By Chebotarev there are then many such v that are moreover of degree one over the rational prime p below them, with p ∉ S ∪ {ℓ}; such a p is split in K, and we take u to be the place of K below v. Since (p_{τc}, q_{τc}) = (q_τ, p_τ), there is, up to complex conjugation, just one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and exactly one of τ, τc induces a place above u. By choosing the prime 𝔭 of the reflex field suitably, one can arrange that this τ lies in S_i for 𝔭_i = v. Then the hypothesis of Theorem 6.3.1(2) holds.
items.note: Footnote 33: only places with residue field F_p contribute to the Dirichlet density. Remark 6.3.2 connects Theorem 6.3.1(2) with Theorem 1.1, and Remark 6.3.3 connects it with Remark 1.5. The Chebotarev step, that there are infinitely many such p (respectively v) outside S ∪ {ℓ}, is part (c) of the separate item on reduction, uniqueness and Chebotarev. The rest of the remarks, the analysis of the sets S_i and the choice of 𝔭, is not planned anywhere. The decomposition of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (layer AG2.7) records an analogous Chebotarev statement, Lemma 4.3.2 of the ten-author paper on potential automorphy over CM fields. That lemma is for its weaker genericity condition, which excludes only eigenvalue ratios equal to q. The text of AG2.7 mentions 'a stronger decomposed-generic API only as a separate specialization' without stating it, and its decomposition says that API was not identified. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre between finite and infinite level at p
items.statement: Let p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), so that K = K_pK^p. There is a Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E_2^{a,b} = H^a_cts(K_p, H^b(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S_K, F_ℓ), compatible with the Hecke operators away from p. Here H^b(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ) = lim→_{K'_p} H^b(S_{K^pK'_p}, F_ℓ) is the cohomology of the perfectoid Shimura variety S_{K^p} ~ lim S_{K^pK'_p}. All groups are étale cohomology after base change to an algebraically closed field (footnote 34). Consequently, localising at the contraction of m to the Hecke operators away from p: if H^*(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 then H^*(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0; and if H^b(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for all b < d, then H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m = 0 for all i < d.
items.note: Nearby layers plan only other settings. R02.2 (and D7) plan the group-theoretic spectral sequence. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.6 plans 'the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application' for Betti cohomology of arithmetic quotients. With Artin's comparison and the colimit over K'_p it would give this item, but no layer plans that assembly. CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.6 plans 'the continuous Hochschild–Serre/descent spectral sequence … comparing tower cohomology and fixed-level cohomology'. Its conventions take coefficients O/ϖ^s over a finite extension of Q_p, for the same prime p as the tower, which excludes F_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.7 plans 'Descend from infinite level using the actual group actions and HS' only for the non-compact datum, and that layer stays fixed to it. The compact endgame, this spectral sequence included, belongs to the Part II, which assembles it from R02.2, ALS.6 and DiamondEtaleCohomology C0. The identification H^b(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ) = lim→ H^b(S_{K^pK'_p}, F_ℓ) is planned in C0 ('continuity of étale cohomology'). The paper says only 'There is a Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence relating H^i(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ) and H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)'. It then claims (p. 758) that if i is minimal with H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0, then H^i(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0. That follows from the spectral sequence when H^a_cts(K_p, −) vanishes on F_ℓ-modules for a > 0, for instance when K_p is pro-p. Here K_p is hyperspecial, and in general only H^b(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 for some b ≤ i follows. Only that weaker statement is used, and the statement records what the spectral sequence gives. Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, status, planning stages.

items.name: Poincaré duality for smooth varieties over an algebraically closed field (applied to S_K and to Mantovan's Igusa varieties)
items.statement: Let X be smooth, separated and of finite type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from ℓ, and equidimensional of dimension d (otherwise apply the statement to each connected component). Cup product and the trace map give perfect pairings H^i_c(X, Λ) × H^{2d−i}(X, Λ(d)) → Λ for Λ = F_ℓ or Q̄_ℓ, and H_c = H when X is proper. The paper applies this in four places. First, to the proper smooth Shimura variety S_K with F_ℓ-coefficients, for the vanishing above the middle degree in Theorem 6.3.1(2). Second, to the Igusa varieties I^b_{Mant,m} with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients, to pass from H to H_c in the proof of Theorem 6.3.1(1). Third, at the finite levels I^b_{Mant,m} and in the colimit over m, to reduce the computation in §5 for I^b_Mant to compactly supported cohomology. Fourth, together with Hochschild–Serre, to twisted coefficients in Remark 1.7.1. Its compatibility with the Hecke action, which exchanges 𝔪 and the dual ideal 𝔪^∨, is a separate item.
items.locator: §1, Remark 1.7.1, p. 652; §5, introduction, p. 729; §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 759
items.note: EDC.2:pairings plans this: 'For smooth separated finite-type X/k, deduce the perfect pairing H_c^i(X_bar,E)×H^(2d-i)(X_bar,E(d))→E; for proper X remove compact support'. There E is a finite extension of Q_ℓ, and 'the derived finite/integral form' (coefficients Z/ℓ^n, which covers F_ℓ) is kept as a separate statement. The stage does not plan compatibility with Hecke operators or the dual ideal 𝔪^∨, which is a separate item. IG.5 and IG.7 plan the dual ideal 𝔪^∨ = ι(𝔪) and its use with Poincaré duality, but for the sequel's unitary quotient and its Igusa varieties. The varieties I^b_{Mant,m} are smooth, separated and of finite type, being finite étale over the smooth leaf C^b, which is closed in a stratum of finite type (Remark 4.3.7, [Man05, Prop. 1]). Corrected by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17: statement, name, locator.

items.name: The pro-étale fundamental group and J_b(Q_p)-torsors on S_proét (Bhatt–Scholze)
items.statement: For a scheme S, a topological group such as J_b(Q_p) defines a sheaf of groups on the pro-étale site S_proét of Bhatt–Scholze [BS15], and one considers torsors on S_proét under it. If S is connected and locally topologically noetherian and x̄ is a geometric point of S, such a torsor corresponds to a homomorphism π_1^proét(S, x̄) → J_b(Q_p), where π_1^proét is the pro-étale fundamental group of [BS15]. For normal S, π_1^proét(S, x̄) agrees with the profinite étale fundamental group of SGA1.
items.note: The paper states the correspondence between torsors and homomorphisms without proof, citing [BS15]. It uses it only for Proposition 1.13 = Proposition 4.3.13 (item 80), which it does not use later. The paper stresses that this formalism is crucial, because Newton strata are usually not normal and the image in J_b(Q_p) can be noncompact (pp. 656–657). Mathlib has the pro-étale site of Bhatt–Scholze, defined through weakly étale maps (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleTopology). Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has π_1^proét or torsors on S_proét under a topological group. In the atlas, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 owns the pro-étale site ('pro-etale site comparisons'). InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0 plans only the profinite fundamental group of finite étale covers ('Construct the profinite automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers'). From [BS15], EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2 plans only the replete-topos results of §3. The pro-étale fundamental group is the automorphism group of the fibre functor at x̄ on the category of locally constant sheaves on S_proét [BS15, §7], so it widens InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0, which already imports SF.2. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0, which receives Proposition 4.3.13, then imports that stage. No cycle arises, because that stage depends on no Igusa layer. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The Newton stratifications correspond under π_HT on rank-one points
items.statement: Assume the global PEL data of §4.3, and assume that S_{K^pK_p} is proper over O_{E,𝔭}. Let S^b_{K^p} ⊂ S_{K^p} be the preimage, under the specialization map, of the Newton stratum S^b_{K^pK_p} of the special fibre; it is a locally closed subset (p. 725). Then a rank-one point y of S_{K^p} lies in S^b_{K^p} if and only if π_HT(y) ∈ Fℓ^b_{G,µ}. That is, on rank-one points, S^b_{K^p} = π_HT^{-1}(Fℓ^b_{G,µ}). The paper does not state this as a numbered result. It is property (1) of the stratification sought in §3 (p. 674), which p. 675 says §4.3 establishes for compact Shimura varieties of PEL type. The inclusion π_HT(S^b_{K^p}) ⊂ Fℓ^b_{G,µ} rests on Proposition 4.2.6 and Remark 4.2.8, through the commutative diagram of Lemma 4.3.20. The converse on rank-one points is the argument of Lemma 4.2.18, used on p. 728.
items.locator: §1, p. 655; §3, pp. 674–675 (property (1), and the forward reference to §4.3); §4.2, Proposition 4.2.6 and Remark 4.2.8, pp. 702–703; §4.3, p. 725; §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4.4, p. 728
items.note: The paper proves this without numbering it. If y ∈ S^b_{K^p}, then π_HT(y) is the local Hodge–Tate period of A_y[p^∞] (Remark 4.2.8), which lies in Fℓ^b_{G,µ} by Proposition 4.2.6. This is why the square of Lemma 4.3.20 commutes. Conversely, if π_HT(y) ∈ Fℓ^b_{G,µ}, the argument of Lemma 4.2.18 gives a quasi-isogeny from the special fibre of A_y[p^∞] to X_b: the G-bundle of A_y[p^∞] is E(π_HT(y)) ≅ E_b, and Theorem 4.1.4 applies. Properness makes every rank-one point extend over O_C. This converse is the step of the proof of Theorem 4.4.4 on p. 728, which is also recorded as its own item (every rank-one point of a fibre of π_HT over Fℓ^b_{G,µ} lies in S^b_{K^p}). The present item should be deduced from that one together with the forward inclusion, not proved twice. At higher-rank points the two stratifications do not correspond: the closure relations are opposite (p. 655). The introduction says the stratification of Fℓ_{G,µ} 'corresponds under π_HT to the Newton stratification'. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.3 plans 'compatibility with … flag Newton strata' only for the non-compact datum of Caraiani–Scholze's sequel. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Shimura varieties S_K, their canonical models and the p-adic setup
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (G, X) and a compact open subgroup K ⊂ G(A_f), let S_K(C) := G(Q)\(X × G(A_f)/K). When K is neat (in particular, when K is small enough), S_K(C) has the structure of an algebraic variety over C, by a theorem of Baily–Borel. It has a model S_K over the reflex field E [Mil90]. The S_K for varying K form an inverse system with the natural Hecke action of G(A_f). The paper does not print this; it is used implicitly, for example in Theorems 2.1.2(3) and 2.1.3(2). For a prime p one takes K = K^p × K_p ⊂ G(A_f^p) × G(Q_p), with K^p and K_p compact open. One fixes a place 𝔭 of E above p and considers the adic spaces attached to S_K ⊗_E E_𝔭 (written 𝒮_K) and to Fl_{G,µ} ⊗_E E_𝔭 (written Fℓ_{G,µ}).
items.note: ShimuraData D5: 'Define neatness'. ShimuraVarieties V0: 'Prove existence of neat congruence subgroups'. V1: 'Give the double quotient its topology and complex analytic structure, construct level maps and Hecke translations.' V2: 'Prove the Baily–Borel theorem.' V6 ('For Hodge type, use the canonical-model inheritance theorem for a Shimura subdatum') and V7 (general data, by Milne's conjugation and descent) plan the canonical models. V8: 'Construct level maps and Hecke correspondences over the reflex field.' AdicSpacesPartII R1: 'Construct the adic analytification of a finite-type scheme over the base field.' On p. 661 the model over E is stated for arbitrary data, which V7 covers. §2 uses only Hodge-type data, for which V6 suffices. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: A reductive group is the stabilizer of finitely many tensors ([DMOS82, Prop. 3.1])
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a field of characteristic zero, V a faithful finite-dimensional representation of G, and V^⊗ := ⊕_{r,s∈N} V^{⊗r} ⊗ (V^∨)^{⊗s}. Then there is a finite collection of tensors (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗ such that G is the closed subgroup of GL(V) of elements fixing every s_α. As used: for an embedding of Shimura data (G, X) ↪ (GSp(V, ψ), X̃), G is the pointwise stabilizer of a finite collection (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗.
items.note: Cited from Hodge Cycles, Motives, and Shimura Varieties [DMOS82, Prop. 3.1]. The Hodge-type 'tensor description' of AutomorphicBundles B1 presupposes this theorem but does not plan it. No reductive-groups layer states it either: the Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap has the embedding theorem for affine group schemes and Tannakian reconstruction, but not this description of a reductive subgroup as the stabilizer of finitely many tensors. B1 is its only consumer in this paper. Lemma 2.3.1, the torsors P_dR, P_p and G_p, and the factorization of π_HT through Fℓ_{G,µ} (Theorem 1.10) all rest on it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Deligne: Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolute Hodge
items.statement: Every Hodge cycle on an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero that embeds in C is an absolute Hodge cycle [DMOS82]. The proof of Lemma 2.3.2 uses it as follows. Let x be the generic point of a component of S_K, with function field κ ⊇ E. For the abelian variety A_x, the pair (s_α,dR,x, s_α,p,x) of de Rham and p-adic étale components of the Hodge cycle s_α,B,x is absolute Hodge. Hence s_α,dR,x is defined over κ̄, and a Hodge cycle is determined by either its de Rham component or its étale component.
items.locator: §2.3, p. 668 and proof of Lemma 2.3.2, pp. 668–669
items.note: AutomorphicBundles B1: 'Prove the required absolute-Hodge and comparison statements rather than identifying arbitrary Hodge classes with algebraic cycles.' HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1 imports it from B1 ('The required absolute-Hodge/tensor statement from B1 is a proved dependency'). This theorem is the main external input to Lemma 2.3.2. Through that lemma it is also an input to the independence of P_dR, P_p and π_HT from the symplectic embedding. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze: the relative Poincaré lemma for OB_dR
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space of dimension d over Spa(K, O_K), where K is complete and discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p. Then the sequence 0 → B^+_dR,X → OB^+_dR,X → OB^+_dR,X ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X → ⋯ → OB^+_dR,X ⊗_{O_X} Ω^d_X → 0, with differentials induced by ∇, is exact on X_proét. It is strict for the filtrations when Ω^j_X is placed in degree j, and the same holds after inverting ξ [Sch13c, §6]. The proof of Proposition 2.2.5 uses it to identify M ⊗_{B^+_dR,S} OB^+_dR,S with R^iπ_dR*OB^+_dR,X.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory P8:local-rational: 'Prove rational local acyclicity, filtration strictness and the relative Poincaré lemma.' The lemma is used in the proof of Proposition 2.2.5 and underlies Theorem 2.2.2. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Deligne: flat connections with regular singular points and analytic flat connections ([Del70])
items.statement: Let S be a smooth algebraic variety over C. Analytification is an equivalence between two categories: algebraic vector bundles on S with integrable connection with regular singular points, and analytic vector bundles on S(C) with integrable connection, equivalently local systems of C-vector spaces on S(C) [Del70]. The Gauss–Manin connection on the relative de Rham cohomology of a proper smooth morphism to S has regular singular points [Del70]. As used on p. 668: the relative de Rham comparison V^an_dR,C ≅ V_B ⊗_Q O_{S_K(C)} shows that V_dR,C, with its Gauss–Manin connection, is the algebraic bundle with regular singular connection attached to the local system V_B ⊗_Q C. Hence the horizontal analytic sections s_α,dR of (V^an_dR,C)^⊗ that come from the s_α,B are algebraic, that is, (s_α,dR) ⊂ V^⊗_dR,C.
items.note: Cited from P. Deligne, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers [Del70]. The paper uses implicitly the regularity of the Gauss–Manin connection, which is also proved there. ComplexComparisonPartII C5 plans the regular-singular comparison only 'For the nonproper smooth curves used by modular symbols', as a logarithmic comparison of cohomology. No layer plans the equivalence over bases of higher dimension, and that is what p. 668 needs for S_K. C5 already has the analytification of the algebraic de Rham complex and 'relative Gauss–Manin compatibility for proper smooth families', so it is the layer to widen. C5 does not depend on AutomorphicBundles, whose layer B1 (Lemma 2.3.2) consumes the result, so the new link creates no cycle. When S_K is proper, as in the paper's main theorems, proper GAGA already makes the horizontal sections algebraic (ComplexComparisonPartII C3: 'Extend the projective theorem to proper finite-type complex schemes'). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Minuscule cocharacters
items.statement: A conjugacy class µ of cocharacters G_m → G_{Q̄_p} of a connected reductive group G over Q_p is minuscule if, in the action of G_m on Lie G through Ad ∘ µ, only the weights −1, 0 and 1 occur; equivalently, ⟨α, µ⟩ ∈ {−1, 0, 1} for every root α.
items.note: This is the standing hypothesis of Lemma 3.4.4, Theorem 3.4.5, and §3.5 from Definition 3.5.6 on. The Hodge cocharacter µ_h of a Shimura datum is minuscule (§2.1). The Tau Ceti highest-weight roadmap defines 'minuscule' for dominant weights of a semisimple Lie algebra ('all weights of L(µ) form one Weyl orbit'). No stage states the notion for cocharacters of reductive groups, and neither library has it. It belongs with Theorem 3.4.5 in GS0:Schubert-smoothness, whose congruence bound 'from weights of μ on Lie G' (FS VI.2.8) is where the condition is used. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Kedlaya–Liu: projectivity from locally constant fibre rank over uniform Banach rings
items.statement: Let A be a uniform Banach ring and M a finitely generated A-module. Then M is projective if and only if the rank function β ↦ dim_{H(β)}(M ⊗_A H(β)) on the Gelfand spectrum M(A) is continuous [KL15, Prop. 2.8.4]. The proof of Proposition 3.4.3 uses it in this form: a finitely generated R-module M whose fibre dimension dim_{C(x)} M ⊗_R C(x) is the same at all points x = Spa(C(x), O_C(x)) → Spa(R, R^+) is finite projective.
items.note: This shows that the filtration Fil_•R^n attached to a lattice has finite projective graded pieces, so that π_{G,µ} lands in Fℓ_{G,µ}. Mathlib has only the converse direction, on Spec (`Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` for finitely presented flat modules), and nothing over the Berkovich spectrum. No stage plans it. Its destination is GS0:Schubert-smoothness, with Proposition 3.4.3. If that layer constructs π_{G,µ} from its stabilizer computation (FS VI.2.4 with Remark VI.2.5), it does not need this input. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The B^+_dR-affine Grassmannian is a pro-étale sheaf
items.statement: On perfectoid affinoid Q_p-algebras, Gr^{B^+_dR}_G is a sheaf for the pro-étale topology of [KL15, §9.2]. Its covers are the maps Spa(S, S^+) → Spa(R, R^+) that factor as an inverse limit of finite étale surjections followed by an étale map. By the Tannakian formalism it suffices to glue finite projective B^+_dR,R-modules. Since B^+_dR,R is ξ-adically complete, ξ is a non-zero-divisor and B^+_dR,R/ξ = R, this reduces to gluing finite projective R-modules, which is [KL15, Thm 9.2.15]. By footnote 16, Gr^{B^+_dR}_G is also a sheaf for the stronger topologies of [Wei14].
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry: 'prove the torsor interpretation and descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings'. RF2:integral-divisors: 'v-descent for bundles on that divisor and its infinitesimal thickenings'. v-descent covers these pro-étale covers. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Griffiths transversality of the universal filtration on Fℓ_{G,µ} for minuscule µ
items.statement: Let µ be minuscule and V a representation of G. Let Fil_• be the universal ascending filtration on Fℓ_{G,µ}, and Fil^i = Fil_{−i} the corresponding descending one. Then the filtered vector bundle with integrable connection (V ⊗ O_{Fℓ_{G,µ}}, id ⊗ ∇, Fil^•) satisfies Griffiths transversality: ∇(Fil^i) ⊂ Fil^{i−1} ⊗ Ω^1_{Fℓ_{G,µ}}. The proof is the same as in the complex case [Del79, Prop. 1.1.14].
items.note: ShimuraData D3 proves transversality for homogeneous variations on Hermitian symmetric domains ('prove transversality using the adjoint Hodge types'). That is a complex-analytic statement. No stage states transversality on the rigid-analytic flag variety. The statement is used only in the paper's proof of surjectivity in Theorem 3.4.5. A proof of Theorem 3.4.5 from the stabilizer computation of GS0:Schubert-smoothness does not need it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze: the B^+_dR-local system of a filtered module with integrable connection
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over Spa(k, O_k), where k is a complete discretely valued extension of Q_p with perfect residue field. Let (E, ∇, Fil^•) be a filtered O_X-module with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality. Then M = Fil^0(E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR)^{∇=0} is a B^+_dR-local system on X_proét associated with E, meaning E ⊗_{O_X} OB_dR ≅ M ⊗_{B^+_dR} OB_dR compatibly with filtrations and connections. The functor E ↦ M is fully faithful [Sch13c, Thm 7.6]. Let M_0 = (E ⊗_{O_X} OB^+_dR)^{∇=0}. Then M ⊂ M_0 ⊗_{B^+_dR} B_dR, and (M ∩ Fil^iM_0)/(M ∩ Fil^{i+1}M_0) = Fil^{−i}E ⊗_{O_X} Ô_X(i) inside gr^iM_0 ≅ E ⊗_{O_X} Ô_X(i) for all i. M is the unique B^+_dR-submodule of M_0 ⊗ B_dR with this property [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9]. The construction is compatible with tensor products and short exact sequences, as the proof of Theorem 3.4.5 uses.
items.locator: §3.4, proof of Theorem 3.4.5, p. 686 ([Sch13c, Thm 7.6, Prop. 7.9])
items.note: P8 plans the period sheaves OB_dR, the relative Poincaré lemma and 'the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. That covers [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9] for the relative de Rham cohomology of a proper smooth family, which is Proposition 2.2.3. It does not cover the functor for an arbitrary filtered module with integrable connection. Theorem 3.4.5 applies that functor to the homogeneous bundles (V ⊗ O_{Fℓ_{G,µ}}, id ⊗ ∇, Fil_{−•}) on Fℓ_{G,µ}. The P8 blueprint should state Theorem 7.6(ii) and Proposition 7.9 in this generality, with Proposition 2.2.3 as an instance. They use only the local theory of the period sheaves (the relative Poincaré lemma), not the proper comparison. GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:Schubert-smoothness does not import P8, and it can prove Theorem 3.4.5 without this input. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Rapoport–Richartz: the order on Newton points is detected on representations
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p and ν, ν' ∈ (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom. Then ν ⪯ ν' if and only if ρ∘ν ⪯ ρ∘ν' in (X_*(GL(V)) ⊗ Q)_dom (after passing to dominant representatives) for every representation ρ : G → GL(V) defined over Q_p. Rapoport–Richartz [RR96, Lemma 2.2] state this equivalence over an algebraically closed field, with all representations and real coefficients. The remark after the lemma shows that for Galois-invariant points it suffices to test representations defined over the base field. Proposition 3.5.3 uses this to reduce ν_b ⪯ \overline{µ^{-1}} to GL_n. Proposition 3.5.7(1) uses it to reduce the semicontinuity of the Newton map to GL_n.
items.locator: §3.5, proofs of Proposition 3.5.3 (p. 687) and Proposition 3.5.7 (p. 690) ([RR96, Lemma 2.2])
items.note: In [RR96, Lemma 2.2] the order is defined by the obtuse Weyl chamber: the difference of the dominant representatives is a nonnegative real combination of positive coroots. BG1 plans 'the dominance comparison of Newton points, pinning its orientation'. BG2:uniformization plans to 'prove nu semicontinuous by faithful-representation HN theory', which needs this reduction, but no stage states it. BG1, which pins the order, is its destination. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: Dieudonné theory up to isogeny over f-semiperfect rings
items.statement: Let R be an f-semiperfect ring [SW13, Def. 4.1.2], with A_cris(R) and B^+_cris(R) = A_cris(R)[1/p]. The functor G ↦ 𝕄(G)(A_cris(R) → R)[1/p], from p-divisible groups over R up to isogeny to B^+_cris(R)-modules with Frobenius, is fully faithful [SW13, Thm A]. Lemma 4.1.8 uses it as follows. Let G, G' be p-divisible groups over a perfect field k and R an f-semiperfect k-algebra. Then Hom_R(G, G')[1/p] = (Hom(D(G)[1/p], D(G')[1/p]) ⊗ B^+_cris(R))^{ϕ=1}. For every p-divisible group H over k, H̃(R) = Hom_R(Q_p/Z_p, H)[1/p] = (D(H) ⊗ B^+_cris(R))^{ϕ=1}.
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Lemma 4.1.8, p. 695 ([SW13, Def. 4.1.2, Thm A]); through [SW13, Thm 5.1.4], Theorem 4.1.4, pp. 692–693
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans to 'Construct Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields' only, and no stage plans Dieudonné theory over semiperfect rings. A source route widens R07.2, which is upstream of both consumers: Lemma 4.1.8 (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0) and, through [SW13, Thm 5.1.4], Theorem 4.1.4 (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2). Lemma 4.1.8 gives the Dieudonné module of the Chai–Oort group H_{G,G'}. Corollary 4.1.10, Proposition 4.2.11 and the dimension counts of Propositions 4.2.22–4.2.23 rest on it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: rigidity of universal covers
items.statement: Let S → S' be a surjection of rings with nilpotent kernel. Then p-divisible groups over S and over S' up to isogeny are equivalent. The universal cover G̃ of a p-divisible group G over S' lifts canonically to a sheaf G̃_S over S, and G̃_S(S) = G̃(S') [SW13, Prop. 3.1.3(ii)]. In particular, for a p-adically complete ring R, S ∈ Nilp_R and a p-divisible group G over S, G̃(S) = G̃(S/p). For a p-divisible group X over F̄_p, a quasi-isogeny X ×_{F̄_p} S/p → G ×_S S/p therefore induces an isomorphism X̃_S ≅ G̃ over S. The paper deduces from [SW13, Prop. 3.1.3] that Aut_G(X̃_b)(R) = Aut_G(X̃_b)(R/p), and that Frobenius induces a bijection of Aut_G(X̃_b)(R) when R has characteristic p.
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Proposition 4.1.2, p. 691; §4.2, proofs of Theorem 4.2.4 (p. 700), Lemma 4.2.10 (p. 704) and Proposition 4.2.11 (p. 705) ([SW13, Prop. 3.1.3])
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 plans to 'Define a p-divisible group … Construct its Tate module', but neither universal covers nor their rigidity.
