A source route adds them to R07.1, beside Definition 4.1.1 and Proposition 4.1.2, whose parts (2)–(3) cite the same proposition. The rigidity lets the quasi-isogeny ρ of Definition 4.2.1 identify X̃_b with G̃, as used in Theorem 4.2.4 and for the action of Aut_G(X̃_b). It also gives the description of Aut_G(X̃_b) as locally Spf W(R) with R perfect (Lemma 4.2.10). The proof of Proposition 4.2.11 uses that description in the form 'all structures lift uniquely to W(F̄_p) by rigidity of perfect rings'. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: the Rapoport–Zink space at infinite level M_∞ and its description M'_∞
items.statement: For a p-divisible group X over F̄_p (here X_b), the Rapoport–Zink space at infinite level M_∞ of [SW13, §6.3] parametrizes deformations of X up to quasi-isogeny, without extra structures, together with a trivialization of the Tate module on the generic fibre. It is preperfectoid [SW13, Thm 6.3.4]. After base change to Spa(Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O_{Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞})}), M_∞ ≅ M'_∞ [SW13, Lemma 6.3.6]. Here M'_∞(R, R^+) is the set of maps V → X̃^ad_η(R, R^+) with two properties. (1) The quotient W of D(X)[1/p] ⊗_L R by the image of V ⊗_{Q_p} R is a finite projective R-module of the same rank as V_1. (2) For every geometric point Spa(C, C^+) of Spa(R, R^+), the sequence 0 → V → X̃^ad_η(C, C^+) → W ⊗_R C → 0 is exact.
items.note: HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas HS2 plans local shtuka moduli for general G and says 'do not restrict general local shtukas to classical Rapoport–Zink spaces'. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a plans only the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers ('Prove the infinite-level moduli description and duality isomorphism', following Scholze–Weinstein §§6–7). No stage plans M_∞ for an arbitrary p-divisible group. Theorem 4.2.4 exhibits M_{D^int,∞} as a closed subspace of M_∞. It deduces preperfectoidness and the description by the rational data from Theorem 6.3.4 and Lemma 6.3.6. The item goes to IG.3 with Theorem 4.2.4. IG.3's description names no Rapoport–Zink space and is written for the non-compact sequel's datum; this paper's source route adds them there. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Oort–Zink: completely slope divisible p-divisible groups
items.statement: (As used in Lemmas 4.2.10 and 4.2.16.) Every p-divisible group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p is quasi-isogenous to a completely slope divisible one. Such a group is a direct sum of slope divisible isoclinic p-divisible groups X_i defined over a finite field, with nonincreasing slopes. Over a perfect base, a completely slope divisible p-divisible group is the direct sum of its isoclinic pieces [OZ02, Prop. 1.3]. Let V be a valuation ring of characteristic p with fraction field K, and G a p-divisible group over V with constant Newton polygon such that G_K is completely slope divisible. Then G is completely slope divisible [OZ02, Prop. 2.3].
items.note: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0 plans to 'Construct completely slope-divisible representatives after isogeny and their finite-level truncations, with descent of all PEL tensors' only for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel. It plans neither the splitting over perfect bases nor the extension over valuation rings. This paper's source route adds them to IG.0. Lemma 4.2.10 and Proposition 4.2.11 compute Aut_G(X̃_b) from a completely slope divisible X_b. Lemma 4.2.16, and through it Lemma 4.2.15 and Proposition 4.2.14, reduce to completely slope divisible groups. §4.3 chooses X_b completely slope divisible as in [Man05, §3]. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Berthelot: Dieudonné theory over perfect valuation rings
items.statement: Let A be a perfect integral domain of characteristic p whose local rings are fields or valuation rings, for instance a perfect valuation ring V. Then the Dieudonné functor G ↦ M(G) = Hom(G, CW), defined with Witt covectors CW, is an anti-equivalence from p-divisible groups over A to left D_A-modules that are locally free of finite rank over Spf W(A), where D_A = W(A)[F, V]/(FV − p, VF − p) [Ber80, Cor. 3.4.3]. In particular the Dieudonné module functor over V is fully faithful. In the proof of Lemma 4.2.16 the groups are base changed from F̄_p. Full faithfulness then reduces extending a homomorphism from the fraction field K to V to the equality (D ⊗_{W(F̄_p)[1/p]} W(V)[1/p])^{ϕ=1} = (D ⊗_{W(F̄_p)[1/p]} W(K)[1/p])^{ϕ=1} for every isocrystal D over F̄_p.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.2.16, pp. 710–711 ([Ber80]; the full faithfulness is [Ber80, Cor. 3.4.3])
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans to 'Construct Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields' only; a source route widens R07.2 to perfect valuation rings. The 'main result of [Ber80]' in Remark 4.2.17 is a different statement, Theorem 4.7.2 (extension of homomorphisms over connected normal bases with constant Newton polygon). Lemma 4.3.15 uses the stronger full faithfulness over perfect rings (Gabber; [Lau13, Thm D]). Lemma 4.2.16 is the valuation-ring case of Lemma 4.2.15, which gives Proposition 4.2.14, the partial properness in Proposition 4.2.22 and the product formula (Lemma 4.3.20). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: the bundle of G ×_{O_C} O_C/p as a modification at ∞
items.statement: Let G be a p-divisible group over O_C and V = T_pG ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. Let E_V be the modification of V ⊗_{Q_p} O_{X_{C♭}} at ∞ by the B^+_dR-lattice Ξ, where V ⊗ B^+_dR ⊂ Ξ ⊂ V ⊗ ξ^{-1}B^+_dR and Ξ/(V ⊗ B^+_dR) = Lie G ⊗ C. Equivalently, E_V is the unique vector bundle fitting into 0 → O_{X_{C♭}} ⊗ V → E_V → i_{∞*}(Lie G ⊗ C) → 0 that maps to 0 → O_{X_{C♭}} ⊗ V → O(1) ⊗ V → i_{∞*}(V ⊗ C(−1)) → 0 through the Hodge–Tate filtration. Then E_V is the vector bundle E(G ×_{O_C} O_C/p) of Theorem 4.1.4. The paper derives this from the proof of [SW13, Prop. 5.1.6].
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.2.6, pp. 702–703, and proof of Lemma 4.2.18, p. 711 ([SW13, Prop. 5.1.6])
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2 plans to 'Prove the displayed Hodge–Tate exact sequence and its relative form on the pro-étale site' but not the bundle attached to a p-divisible group over O_C. A source route adds it to T2 with Theorem 4.1.4 and the classification by pairs (T, W). It identifies the G-bundle attached to π_HT(x) with the bundle of the p-divisible group. This puts π_HT into the b-stratum (Proposition 4.2.6) and gives surjectivity onto Fℓ^b_{G,µ} (Lemma 4.2.18), which underlie Theorem 1.15. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory
items.statement: Let S → R be a PD thickening, with nilpotent divided powers, of rings on which p is nilpotent. Lifting a p-divisible group G over R to S amounts to lifting its Hodge filtration to 𝕄(G)(S → R) [Mes72]. A homomorphism between p-divisible groups over R lifts to a homomorphism between given lifts over S exactly when the induced map on 𝕄(·)(S → R) preserves the lifted Hodge filtrations. Quasi-isogenies always lift uniquely, as quasi-isogenies, along nilpotent thickenings. The proof of Theorem 4.2.4 uses this over the Rapoport–Zink space of X_b. There the conditions that the O_B-action and the polarization lift to the universal p-divisible group depend only on preserving the Hodge filtration of D(G)[1/p], and so are closed.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Theorem 4.2.4, p. 700 ([Mes72]); used through [RZ96, Thm 3.25] in Theorem 4.2.2
items.note: R07.2 plans to 'Supply the deformation results needed for p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings', which covers the theory in this generality. CrystallineCohomology CR.7 exports its inputs to 'R07's Dieudonne crystal and Grothendieck–Messing construction'. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 imports it 'from R07.6', although R07.6's own description does not mention it. No stage plans the Grothendieck–Messing period morphism on Rapoport–Zink spaces. The theory underlies the representability of Rapoport–Zink spaces (Theorem 4.2.2) and the closed-embedding step of Theorem 4.2.4. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Rank-one points of the fibres of π_HT over Fℓ^b_{G,µ} lie in the good-reduction Newton locus 𝒮^b_{K^p}
items.statement: Assume 𝒮_{K_pK^p} is proper over O_{E,𝔭}. Let C/Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}) be complete and algebraically closed, b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}), x ∈ Fℓ^b_{G,µ}(C, O_C) a rank-one point, and 𝒮_{K^p,x} the fibre of π_HT over x. Then every geometric rank-one point y of 𝒮_{K^p,x} lies in 𝒮^b_{K^p}. By properness the abelian variety A_y has good reduction. By the argument of Lemma 4.2.18 (the G-bundle of A_y[p^∞] is ℰ_x ≅ ℰ_b, and Theorem 4.1.4 applies), its reduction is a point of 𝒮^b_{K_pK^p}. Consequently 𝒮^b_{K^p,x} = 𝒮_{K^p,x} ×_{𝒮_{K^p}} 𝒮^b_{K^p} is a quasicompact open subset of 𝒮_{K^p,x} with the same rank-one points, and Lemma 4.4.2 gives (R^iπ_HT* Z/ℓ^nZ)_x = H^i(𝒮^b_{K^p,x}, Z/ℓ^nZ). At rank-one points this makes precise the statement in §1 that the stratification of Fℓ_{G,µ} 'corresponds under π_HT to the Newton stratification (pulled back from the special fibre through the specialization map)'.
items.note: The paper's proof is one line: 'the argument of Lemma 4.2.18 shows that y ∈ 𝒮^b_{K^p}'. By Remark 4.2.8 and the proof of Proposition 4.2.6, the G-bundle that Theorem 4.1.4 attaches to A_y[p^∞] ×_{O_C} O_C/p is ℰ_x ≅ ℰ_b, so the reduction of A_y[p^∞] is quasi-isogenous to X_b. This step lets the product formula (Lemma 4.3.20), which is stated over 𝒮^b_{K^p}, compute the whole stalk of Rπ_HT* in Theorem 4.4.4 = Theorem 1.15, and Corollary 6.1.4 uses Theorem 4.4.4 on every stratum. The correspondence is asserted only at rank-one points: §1 relates the reversed closure relations of Theorem 1.11 to 'a subtle behaviour of π_HT on certain higher-rank points' (p. 655). The item is missing. IG.3 plans compatibility 'with prime-to-p Hecke action, passage between p-levels, flag Newton strata, and the good-reduction open part', but only for the split datum of the non-compact sequel. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Preperfectoid adic spaces and their strong completions (Scholze–Weinstein)
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field. An adic space X over Spa(K, O_K) is preperfectoid if it has a cover by open affinoids Spa(A_i, A_i^+) such that the completions (Â_i, Â_i^+) are perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebras. The completion is taken for the topology on A_i that gives A_i^+ the p-adic topology [SW13, Def. 2.3.4]. Such an X has a strong completion X̂. This is a perfectoid space over Spa(K, O_K) with the same underlying topological space, equal to Spa(Â_i, Â_i^+) on each such affinoid and universal for maps from perfectoid spaces over Spa(K, O_K) to X [SW13, Prop. 2.3.6]. A locally closed subspace of a preperfectoid space is preperfectoid [SW13, Prop. 2.3.7], and X̂ ~ X [SW13, Prop. 2.4.4]. The paper uses these facts over the completion of Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}) in four places. First, M_{D,∞} is preperfectoid as a closed subspace of Scholze–Weinstein's M_∞ (Theorem 4.2.4). Second, M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞} is preperfectoid as a closed subspace of M_{D,∞} ×_{Spa(Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} M_{D,∞} (before Proposition 4.2.14). Third, X^b_∞ is preperfectoid (Corollary 4.3.19), and X̂^b_∞ is formed in Lemma 4.3.20. Fourth, the proof of Theorem 4.4.4 identifies the fibre of X̂^b_∞ over a point z ∈ M^b_∞(C, O_C) with the fibre of X^b_∞, which Corollary 4.3.19 identifies with the perfectoid space (Ig^b_{O_C})^ad_η. This uses the universal property of the strong completion.
items.locator: §4.2, Theorem 4.2.4 and its proof, pp. 699–701, and the paragraph before Proposition 4.2.14, p. 709; §4.3, Corollary 4.3.19 and the paragraph before Lemma 4.3.20, pp. 724–725; §4.4, proof of Theorem 4.4.4, p. 728
items.note: Corollary 4.3.19, Lemma 4.3.20 and Theorem 4.4.4 = Theorem 1.15 are stated for X̂^b_∞. Without this notion there is no perfectoid space on which the product formula holds. The item is missing: no layer description mentions preperfectoid spaces or strong completions. The nearest owner is PerfectoidSpaces P7 ('Tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers', which derives 'the perfectoid Frobenius criterion'). P7 plans Huber tilde-limits, and X̂ ~ X is a statement of that kind. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Hecke equivariance of Poincaré duality and the dual ideal 𝔪^∨
items.statement: Let T^S = ⊗_{q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ})} Z[G(Q_q)//K_q] be the Hecke algebra of §6.3, ι its anti-involution induced by [K_q g K_q] ↦ [K_q g^{−1} K_q], and 𝔪^∨ = ι(𝔪) for a maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊂ T^S. Under the Poincaré duality pairing on the proper smooth Shimura variety S_K, the transpose of the action of t ∈ T^S is the action of ι(t). The same holds on the Igusa varieties I^b_{Mant,m} for the Hecke operators at primes q ≠ p, which act through G(A_f^p). Here p is the auxiliary prime chosen in the proof of Theorem 6.3.1, and localization of Igusa cohomology is taken with respect to T^{S ∪ {p}}. Hence, up to Tate twist, H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_𝔪 is dual to H^{2 dim S_K − i}(S_K, F_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨}. Likewise H^i_c(I^b_{Mant,m}, Q̄_ℓ)_𝔪 is dual to H^{2e−i}(I^b_{Mant,m}, Q̄_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨}, where e = dim I^b_{Mant,m}. Moreover, for a place v of F above q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), ι(T_{i,v}) = T_{n,v}^{−1}T_{n−i,v}. So if λ_1, …, λ_n are the roots of the Hecke polynomial of §6.3 modulo 𝔪, those modulo 𝔪^∨ are q_v^{n−1}λ_1^{−1}, …, q_v^{n−1}λ_n^{−1}. Consequently 𝔪^∨ satisfies the hypothesis of Theorem 6.3.1(2) whenever 𝔪 does. Hence ρ_{𝔪^∨} ≅ ρ_𝔪^∨ ⊗ ε̄^{±(n−1)}, where ε̄ is the mod-ℓ cyclotomic character and the sign depends on the Frobenius convention; so ρ_{𝔪^∨} is decomposed generic at 𝔭_i whenever ρ_𝔪 is.
items.locator: §5, introduction, p. 729; §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 759
items.note: The paper writes 'applying the same discussion with the “dual” set of Hecke eigenvalues' and 'the result for the “dual” ideal, which satisfies the same hypothesis' (p. 759), and proves neither. The computation of ι(T_{i,v}) is not in the paper. The double coset of diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1), with i entries ϖ_v, is sent by ι to that of ϖ_v^{−1}·diag(1, …, 1, ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v), with n − i entries ϖ_v, and T_{n,v} is invertible. Comparing the coefficients (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v} of the Hecke polynomial then gives the roots q_v^{n−1}λ_j^{−1}. Decomposed genericity is preserved because the condition λ_a/λ_b ∉ {1, q_v} ranges over all ordered pairs a ≠ b. Both parts of Theorem 6.3.1, and hence Theorem 1.1, use the item. Part (1) passes from ordinary to compactly supported Igusa cohomology through 𝔪^∨, which needs H^•(S_K, F_ℓ)_{𝔪^∨} ≠ 0. Part (2) obtains the vanishing above the middle degree from the result for 𝔪^∨. The item is missing. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2:pairings plans only the bare pairing. IG.5 ('Define the double-coset anti-involution iota([KgK])=[Kg^(-1)K] and m^vee=iota(m)') and IG.7 ('uses Poincaré duality and the dual Hecke ideal') cover only the unitary datum of the non-compact sequel, where this statement is planned. The Part II imports ι and 𝔪^∨ from IG.5 and must prove the duality statements for S_K and for the Igusa varieties of this paper. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The alternating Igusa cohomology [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] and its S-unramified part
items.statement: Fix b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) and X_b/F̄_p as in §4.3. The Igusa variety I^b_Mant is the projective system of the F̄_p-schemes I^b_{Mant,K^p,m} (K^p ⊂ G(A^p_f) sufficiently small, m ≥ 1), each a finite Galois cover of the leaf C_b in 𝒮^b_K, and [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] := Σ_k (−1)^k lim_{K^p,m} H^k_c(I^b_{Mant,K^p,m}, Q̄_ℓ) is a virtual representation in Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)), each summand being admissible. Let S be a finite set of places of Q containing p, ∞ and the places where F ramifies, and K^S = ∏_{q∉S} K_q with K_q ⊂ G(Q_q) hyperspecial. Every π ∈ Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) is a possibly infinite sum Σ_i n_iπ_i of irreducibles such that for each compact open K only finitely many i have n_i ≠ 0 and π_i^K ≠ 0; π^{S ur} := Σ_{i : π_i^{K^S} ≠ 0} n_iπ_i, Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p))^{S ur} is the subgroup of π with π = π^{S ur}, and the trace pairings Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) × C_c^∞(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) → C and Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p))^{S ur} × (H^ur(G(A^S)) ⊗ C_c^∞(G(A_{S_fin∖{p}}) × J_b(Q_p))) → C are nondegenerate.
items.note: IG.1 plans 'Define the common compactly supported cohomology complex as the specified filtered colimit over finite levels' and IG.5 'compute its alternating Q_ell-representation of J_b(Q_p)×T^S', both for the non-compact sequel's split datum. The virtual representation for the compact data of §§5.1 and 5.6 belongs in IG.1 once that layer is widened to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C), together with Mantovan's Igusa varieties I^b_Mant (Definition 4.3.6). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The archimedean test functions φ^n⃗_∞ and f^n⃗_∞ for an inner form of arbitrary signature
items.statement: Over R, G is an inner form of the quasi-split G_n, of arbitrary signature. For a discrete L-parameter φ_{G_n⃗} of G_n⃗ with L-packet Π(φ_{G_n⃗}), set φ_{φ_{G_n⃗}} := |Π(φ_{G_n⃗})|^{-1} Σ_{π ∈ Π(φ_{G_n⃗})} φ_π, φ_π a pseudo-coefficient of π; when φ_{G_n⃗} ∼ φ_ξ corresponds to the L-packet Π_disc(G_n⃗(R), ξ^∨) this is the Euler–Poincaré function φ_{G_n⃗,ξ}. The function φ^n⃗_∞ of Definition 5.2.2 (Kottwitz's construction [Kot90, §7], using Shelstad's real endoscopy) is an explicit linear combination of the φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} over the φ_{G_n⃗} for which η̃∘φ_{G_n⃗} corresponds to the trivial algebraic representation of G_C ([Shi11, (5.11)]), and f^n⃗_∞ is the corresponding linear combination of Labesse's Lefschetz functions for the representations Ξ(φ_n⃗) of 𝒢_n⃗ ([Shi11, (6.7)]); φ^n⃗_∞ and f^n⃗_∞ are BC-matching. In [Shi11] G_R has Harris–Taylor signature; here it is arbitrary, and q(G) = ½dim(G(R)/K_∞A°_∞).
items.note: ET.1 plans 'Prove real transfer and explicit discrete-series/Euler–Poincaré pseudocoefficient formulas in the unitary cases used below', and ET.4 'infinity pseudocoefficients' 'For CSnc's G_(n_i)'; both concern the non-compact sequel's groups, which are quasi-split at ∞. The paper stresses that its inner form G_R has arbitrary signature, unlike the group of Harris–Taylor type in [Shi11] (p. 738). ET.1 and ET.4 must be widened to that generality; Corollary 5.2.5 and Theorem 5.3.2 depend on it. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Shin: acceptable test functions determine virtual representations
items.statement: If Π_1, Π_2 ∈ Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) satisfy tr Π_1(φ) = tr Π_2(φ) for every acceptable φ, then Π_1 = Π_2 [Shi09, Lemma 6.4]. Its proof (twisting φ_p by powers Fr^N of a central Frobenius element of J_b(Q_p), which make it acceptable for N ≫ 0 by [Shi09, Lemma 6.3], and a linear-independence argument in N) extends a trace identity proved for acceptable φ_p to all φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)).
items.note: ET.5 plans 'Prove the acceptable-function shift/density argument extending precisely the linear trace identity to the source's full test-function class' only for 'IG.0–IG.1's finite-level Igusa varieties' of the non-compact sequel's datum. The proof rests on [Shi09, Lemma 6.3], which verifies conditions (ii)–(iii) of [Shi09, Def. 6.2] by Fujiwara's trace formula on the Igusa varieties of the datum at hand, so ET.5 must be widened to the compact data of §§5.1 and 5.6. The paper cites the lemma on p. 749 as 'Lemma 6.4 of [Shi11]', which does not exist, and on p. 743 speaks of twisting 'φ^p' where φ_p is meant. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Badulescu: the Langlands–Jacquet map and generic principal series
items.statement: Badulescu's Langlands–Jacquet map LJ : Groth(M_b(Q_p)) → Groth(J_b(Q_p)) [Bad07] extends the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence between the quasi-split Levi M_b (a restriction of scalars of a product of general linear groups) and its inner form J_b to Grothendieck groups; by its construction [Bad07, Thm 3.1, Prop. 3.3], an element of Groth(M_b(Q_p)) whose M_{b_i}(F_{p_i})-components are all generic principal series lies in the kernel of LJ whenever J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form of M_{b_i}.
items.locator: §5.4, step (3) of the definition of Red^b_n⃗, p. 739; proof of Lemma 5.4.3, p. 741
items.note: ET.6: 'Prove the Grothendieck-group extension and compatibility with Jacquet/induction operations used for J_b; this extension may vanish or carry signs … Derive the source's nontransfer obstruction for generic principal-series parameters to a nontrivial inner form', with 'Badulescu's extended Jacquet–Langlands' among its sources. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n and generic principal series
items.statement: For a p-adic field L, rec is the local Langlands correspondence between irreducible smooth representations of GL_n(L) and n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations of W_L, normalized as in [HT01], and it is compatible with normalized parabolic induction. If the Galois representation corresponding to π is a direct sum of characters χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n with χ_aχ_b^{-1} not the cyclotomic character for all a ≠ b, then π is a generic (irreducible) principal series representation of GL_n(L).
items.locator: §5.5, Theorem 5.5.4 and the proof of Corollary 5.5.5, pp. 744–746; Remark 5.5.6, p. 746; §6.2, Lemma 6.2.2, p. 756
items.note: ET.6: 'Construct the characteristic-zero local correspondence for GL_m(E), E a finite extension of Q_p, with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters and monodromy … Develop the needed supercuspidal/type and segment/Langlands-quotient theory; prove the classification and induction compatibilities'. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Moeglin–Waldspurger: the discrete spectrum of GL_m
items.statement: The discrete automorphic spectrum of GL_m(A_F) consists of the Speh representations: for a cuspidal σ of GL_{m/k}(A_F), the unique irreducible quotient of the normalized induction of σ|det|^{(k+1)/2−j}, j = 1, …, k [MW89]. Hence every Π_M in the discrete spectrum of a Levi M of GL_m or of 𝒢_n⃗ is isobaric and is determined by cuspidal data.
items.locator: §5.5, proofs of Lemma 5.5.1, p. 742, and Theorem 5.5.4, p. 744
items.note: ET.7a: 'Develop the required GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification and cyclic automorphic-induction/base-change steps from the Arthur–Clozel and Moeglin–Waldspurger proofs'. The paper also cites [Art13, Thm 1.3.3]. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika: strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations
items.statement: An isobaric automorphic representation of GL_m(A_F), and hence of a Levi subgroup of 𝒢_n⃗, is determined by its Satake parameters outside any finite set S of places [JS81] (also [Art13, Thm 1.3.2]).
items.note: No stage states it for GL_m: strong multiplicity one is planned only for GL_2 and modular forms (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.4 and R17.3; the Tau Ceti modular forms roadmap). AL.3 builds the Rankin–Selberg theory on which [JS81] rests ('Construct the GL_n×GL_m local zeta integrals … Prove unramified calculations and the global unfolding for cuspidal data'). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The µ-ordinary element of B(G, µ^{-1})
items.statement: The µ-ordinary element of B(G, µ^{-1}) (more accurately µ^{-1}-ordinary, footnote 29) is the unique b whose Newton point ν_b equals the Galois average of the dominant representative of µ^{-1} (Definition 3.1.2), that is, the unique maximal element of B(G, µ^{-1}). For GL_n over a p-adic field L and µ : t ↦ diag(t, …, t, 1, …, 1) with n − q entries t, it is the class of diag(ϖ^{-1}, …, ϖ^{-1}, 1, …, 1) with n − q entries ϖ^{-1}. Its slopes are −1 with multiplicity n − q and 0 with multiplicity q, and J_b ≅ GL_{n−q} × GL_q (Lemma 5.5.8).
items.locator: §1, Remark 1.17, p. 658; §3, introduction, p. 674; §5.5, Theorem 5.5.7 and footnote 29, p. 747, and Lemma 5.5.8, p. 748; §5.6, Corollary 5.6.3, p. 750; §6.3, proof of Theorem 6.3.1, p. 759
items.note: The paper uses the term without defining it. BG1 plans κ, ν and 'the partial order with equal kappa and the dominance comparison of Newton points', but no stage names the maximal element of B(G, µ); IG.5 speaks of 'ordinary' b only for the non-compact sequel's datum with p totally split. The definition belongs in BG1 with Lemma 5.5.8. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Shin: stable base change for Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties
items.statement: For the group G of a PEL datum as in §5.6 (B a division algebra with centre F = F^+·K, V a simple B-module, * of the second kind), the stable base change to GL_n of the automorphic representations π = π_fπ_∞ of G with π_∞ cohomological for the trivial algebraic representation exists (Shin, appendix to [Gol14]); hence such π have attached Galois representations r_{π,ℓ} : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: These representations define the summand [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]_r of Corollary 5.6.3 (the π with r_{π,ℓ} ≅ r), on the way to Case 1 of Theorem 6.3.1. The Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties imports this base change from AG2.2, which plans 'Apply stable unitary base change and endoscopic character identities from ET.4/ET.7a to identify the GL_n parameter realized by AG2.1'. ET.4 and ET.7a are written for the quasi-split groups G_n⃗ of the non-compact sequel ('For CSnc's G_(n_i)'), and no stage mentions base change from the unitary group of a division algebra. AG2.2 must be widened to cover Shin's theorem. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: The stable trace formula for S_K in the simple case and Red^b_n([H(S_K)])
items.statement: For the proper Shimura varieties S_K of §5.6, Arthur's formula for Lefschetz numbers of Hecke operators [Art89, Thm 6.1], which takes the stable form of [Shi12, Prop. 6.3] because G has no endoscopy, combined with Proposition 5.6.1 and Lemma 5.4.2 for G_n(Q_p) ≅ G(Q_p), gives Red^b_n([H(S_K, Q̄_ℓ)]) = ε_G · d(G_R) · [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] with nonzero constants ε_G and d(G_R), first for acceptable φ_p and then, by [Shi09, Lemma 6.4], for all φ_p ∈ C_c^∞(J_b(Q_p)).
items.note: No stage states Arthur's formula for Lefschetz numbers of Hecke operators [Art89] or its stable form [Shi12, Prop. 6.3] for these inner forms. The identity, which combines it with Proposition 5.6.1 and Lemma 5.4.2, is a step of the §5.6 route to Theorem 1.1 and belongs to the Part II roadmap for compact unitary Shimura varieties, which imports the compact-quotient trace formula with Euler–Poincaré functions from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.4–AS.6 (AS.6: 'Prove the invariant trace identity with its actual summation/convergence conditions') and ET.1. The paper cites the last step as 'Lemma 6.4 of [Shi11]'; it is [Shi09, Lemma 6.4]. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Matsushima's formula for the proper Shimura varieties S_K
items.statement: For the proper Shimura varieties S_K of §5.6, S_K being the disjoint union of |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety of (G, X), the comparison of étale and Betti cohomology and Matsushima's formula give, as Hecke modules, ι_ℓH^i(S_K, Q̄_ℓ) ≅ (⊕_π m(π) π_f^K ⊗ H^i(g, K_∞; π_∞))^{⊕|ker^1(Q, G)|}, the sum over automorphic representations π = π_f ⊗ π_∞ of G with multiplicities m(π), only π_∞ cohomological for the trivial algebraic representation contributing; this describes [ι_ℓH(S_K, Q̄_ℓ)] in terms of automorphic representations of G.
items.note: AS.4: 'For compact quotients specialize to a discrete Hilbert sum'; AS.5: 'compare relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of all smooth functions of the required growth … with algebraic coefficient systems and Hecke equivariance'; ALS.5: 'compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology in characteristic zero via local systems'; PELModuli M3: 'Describe these forms by the relevant pointed-set obstruction ker¹(Q,G)=ker(H¹(Q,G)→∏_v H¹(Q_v,G)) … Prove the actual indexing/comparison theorem and its nonempty classes', which gives the |ker^1(Q, G)| copies. All are stated for general groups. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: B(G) of a product and of a restriction of scalars
items.statement: For groups G_1, G_2 over Q_p, B(G_1 × G_2) = B(G_1) × B(G_2), compatibly with the sets B(·, µ) and with J_b. For a p-adic field L and a connected reductive group H over L, Shapiro's lemma gives a bijection B(Res_{L/Q_p} H) ≅ B(L, H) with the set of σ_L-conjugacy classes in H(L̆); for corresponding classes b and b', J_b ≅ Res_{L/Q_p} J_{b'}, and the conditions defining B(·, µ) match once the Kottwitz invariants and the normalizations of Newton points are identified. Consequently, in the setting of §5.1, write µ = ((µ_i)_{i=1}^m, µ_0) according to G_{Q̄_p} = ∏_i ∏_{τ: F_{p_i} ↪ Q̄_p} GL_{n,Q̄_p} × G_{m,Q̄_p}, µ_i = (µ_{i,τ})_τ, and G_i = Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} GL_n. Then B(G, µ^{-1}) = ∏_{i=1}^m B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}), the G_m-factor contributing a single class. If every µ_{i,τ} is central, B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}) has exactly one element; if exactly one µ_{i,τ} is not central, then B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}) = B(GL_n/F_{p_i}, µ_{i,τ}^{-1}), up to translation by a central element, which does not change J_b.
items.locator: §5.5, proof of Theorem 5.5.7 and footnote 30, pp. 747–748
items.note: Used in the proof of Theorem 5.5.7 (p. 748) to reduce to Lemma 5.5.8; the identification B(H/L) = B(L, H) is stated in the text, and footnote 30 remarks that only L = Q_p had been used before. BG1 plans 'behavior under group homomorphisms, central quotients and z-extensions, and their relation for tori and GL_n', but neither the identification for restriction of scalars nor its compatibility with B(G, µ) and J_b is stated. These facts belong in BG1 with Lemma 5.5.8. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Leray spectral sequence for π_HT and localisation away from p
items.statement: Consider the compact unitary Shimura varieties of §6.3 and a prime p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), and let π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} be the Hodge–Tate period map. There is a Leray spectral sequence E_2^{a,b} = H^a(Fℓ_{G,µ}, R^bπ_HT*F_ℓ) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ). Let T' ⊂ T^S be the subalgebra generated by the Hecke operators at the primes of Spl_{K/Q} outside S ∪ {p, ℓ}. These operators act on Rπ_HT*F_ℓ, because π_HT is equivariant for G(A_f^p) acting trivially on Fℓ_{G,µ}, and the spectral sequence is T'-equivariant. Let m' = m ∩ T'. Localisation at m' is exact and commutes with cohomology on the quasicompact quasiseparated space Fℓ_{G,µ}. Consequently, if (Rπ_HT*F_ℓ)_{m'} = 0 then RΓ(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_{m'} = 0. And if (R^bπ_HT*F_ℓ)_{m'} = 0 for all b < d, then H^i(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_{m'} = 0 for all i < d.
items.note: DiamondsAndVStacks D0 plans, for ordinary sites, the 'coherent and algebraic topos interfaces', 'exactness of sheafification and filtered colimits', 'derived global sections, Leray and Čech-to-sheaf spectral sequences'. These give the spectral sequence and the commutation of localisation with cohomology on Fℓ_{G,µ}. The proof of Theorem 6.3.1 uses the spectral sequence twice, on p. 758 for part (1) and on p. 760 for part (2). Each time it turns vanishing of the localised stalks, which Theorem 4.4.4 computes and Corollary 6.1.4 bounds, into vanishing of H^i(S_{K^p}, F_ℓ)_m. The paper localises at m itself. The Hecke operators at p do not act on S_{K^p}, so the contraction m' is meant; m' is again maximal because T'/m' is a subring of the finite field T^S/m. The Hecke equivariance of π_HT is Theorem 2.1.2(3). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Deligne–Serre lifting of Hecke eigensystems
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_ℓ, with uniformiser ϖ. Let M be a finite free O-module and T a commutative O-algebra acting O-linearly on M, so that the image T_M of T in End_O(M) is a finite O-algebra. Let m ⊂ T be a maximal ideal with M_m ≠ 0. Then m contains ϖ and the kernel of T → T_M, and M_m is a direct summand of M. Moreover, M ⊗_O Q̄_ℓ contains a nonzero common eigenvector of T whose eigencharacter T → Q̄_ℓ takes values in Z̄_ℓ and reduces to a homomorphism T → F̄_ℓ with kernel m. More precisely, M_m ⊗_O Q̄_ℓ is the sum of the generalised eigenspaces of M ⊗_O Q̄_ℓ for the eigencharacters that lift m.
items.note: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.5: 'Prove the Deligne–Serre eigenvalue-lifting lemma for a finite Hecke algebra'. The paper uses the lemma without naming it. It applies it to H^d(I^b_{Mant,m}, Z_ℓ)_m, which is flat and the only nonzero degree, to split [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S-ur} 'according to systems of Hecke eigenvalues lifting m'. This produces some Π^S as in Lemma 5.5.1 with Hecke eigenvalues lifting m. Corollary 5.5.5 attaches r_{Π^S,ℓ} to it, and the reduction of r_{Π^S,ℓ} is ρ_m. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Reduction and uniqueness of ρ_m (Brauer–Nesbitt and Chebotarev)
items.statement: (a) Let E be a finite extension of Q_ℓ with ring of integers O, and let r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(E) be continuous. Then r preserves an O-lattice. The semisimplification r̄ of its reduction does not depend on the lattice. At every place v where r is unramified, the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_v) is the reduction of that of r(Frob_v) (Brauer–Nesbitt). (b) Let ρ_1, ρ_2 : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) be semisimple continuous representations, unramified outside a finite set of places. Suppose the characteristic polynomials of ρ_1(Frob_v) and ρ_2(Frob_v) agree for all but finitely many places v of F of degree one over Q. Then ρ_1 ≅ ρ_2. Indeed, let L be the Galois closure over Q of the finite extension of F cut out by ρ_1 ⊕ ρ_2. For σ ∈ Gal(L/F), Chebotarev gives infinitely many rational primes p, unramified in L, each with a place w of L above p such that Frob_{w/p} = σ. Then v = w|_F has degree one over Q and Frob_v = σ. So ρ_1(σ) and ρ_2(σ) have the same characteristic polynomial for every σ ∈ Gal(L/F), and the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem in characteristic ℓ applies. (c) Let ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) be continuous. Let L be the Galois closure over Q of the compositum of F(ζ_ℓ) and the field cut out by ρ, and let p_0 be a rational prime unramified in L. Suppose either that ρ is decomposed generic at a place of F of degree one above p_0, or that p_0 is completely decomposed in F and ρ is decomposed generic at all places above p_0. Then the same holds for every rational prime p unramified in L whose Frobenius class in Gal(L/Q) equals that of p_0, and by Chebotarev there are infinitely many such p.
items.locator: §6.3, Theorem 6.3.1(1) and its proof, pp. 757–759; Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3, p. 758
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1: 'For field coefficients construct invariant lattices using compactness' and 'Define reduction followed by semisimplification and prove independence of lattice by characteristic polynomials and the characteristic-p Brauer–Nesbitt theorem'. Layer 10 of the Tau Ceti Chebotarev roadmap: 'hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet with value #C/#G over every number field K', and 'Derive, rather than reprove, the density of split-completely primes, the non-Galois statement via a Galois closure, infinitude of every Frobenius class'. The representations r_{Π^S,ℓ} used here are defined over a finite extension of Q_ℓ. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7 plans this ('Choose continuous invariant lattices only after proving a finite coefficient field of realization'). Part (b) gives the uniqueness in Theorem 6.3.1(1). Places of degree one over Q lie above primes split in K, so all but finitely many of them lie above primes of Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}). Part (c) needs ζ_ℓ ∈ L, so that p ≡ p_0 mod ℓ and the condition λ_a/λ_b ≠ q of Definition 6.2.1 is unchanged. It gives the 'many such p' of Remark 6.3.2 and the 'many such v' of Remark 6.3.3. Because Chebotarev is applied over Q, footnote 33 (only places with residue field F_p contribute to the Dirichlet density) is not needed. The pinned Tau Ceti library has only the Chebotarev infrastructure (Frobenius prime sets, ramified primes, the auxiliary prime), and Mathlib has only the definition of Dirichlet density. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Finiteness from the rank-one valuative criterion
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of affine schemes of finite type over F_p. Suppose the following holds for every algebraically closed field k with a rank-one valuation ring V ⊂ k: every V-point of Y, together with a k-point of X lifting its generic point, extends to a V-point of X. Then f is proper, and hence finite, being affine. Uniqueness of lifts is automatic because f is separated.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.3 uses this result to show that π_{HT,K_p,𝔘_s} is finite, so that pushforward along it preserves perversity: the map 'satisfies the valuative criterion of properness; i.e., it is finite' (p. 753). Mathlib has the valuative criterion over all valuation rings. AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.of_valuativeCriterion covers quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphisms locally of finite type; AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion covers universal closedness. It also has AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.iff_isProper_and_isAffineHom (finite = proper and affine). The reduction to rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field is valid for morphisms of finite type between noetherian schemes, because the existence part may be tested on discrete valuation rings after enlarging the fraction field. That reduction is in neither library, and no stage states it. The item belongs with the widening of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4, which plans the corresponding step only for the non-compact datum ('Prove affine formal-model descent to finite special-fiber maps'). Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

items.name: Perverse sheaves are concentrated in one degree at generic points of their support
items.statement: Let Y be a scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from ℓ, and let K be a perverse F_ℓ-sheaf on Y supported on a closed subset of dimension at most e. Then for every geometric point x̄ of Y whose closure has dimension e, the stalk K_x̄ is concentrated in degree −e.
items.locator: §6.1, discussion before and proof of Corollary 6.1.4, pp. 754–755
items.note: This is the step 'on the largest stratum where a perverse sheaf is nonzero, it is concentrated in one degree' (p. 754) in Corollary 6.1.4. Proof: on a dense open subset of each e-dimensional irreducible component of the support, K has locally constant cohomology sheaves. There the support condition allows only degrees ≤ −e, and the cosupport condition allows only degrees ≥ −e. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5 plans the middle perverse t-structure 'using dimension functions, stalk/costalk bounds', together with 'L[d] is perverse on a smooth pure d-dimensional scheme' and 'finite-map exactness'; the last is also used in Proposition 6.1.3. EDC.5 does not state this consequence, which belongs there. In the proof it is applied at finite level K_p, where the sheaves are constructible. The sheaf is Rλ_{U/K_p*}((R(π_HT/G(Q_p))_*F_ℓ)_m)|_{U_η̄/K_p}[⟨2ρ, µ⟩] on 𝔘_s̄, which is supported in dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − d, and the result gives concentration in degree d. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4 plans only the one-sided bound of the non-compact case. Added by the review REV-PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17.

routes.title: Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration, Part II: compact unitary Shimura varieties
routes.reason: Nothing in the atlas owns the compact endgame. IG.7 is fixed to the non-compact datum of the sequel ('Under the exact initial global hypotheses … Require a completely split p≠ell'), and IG.5 proves the sequel's obstruction 'for p totally split', the parent says its constructions 'do not assert results for every Hodge-type or arbitrary Shimura datum', and TC.4 rules out new terminal claims about Galois representations. No stage owns Theorem 6.3.1 and Theorem 1.1, the Igusa cohomology of Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties (§5.6), or the obstruction at a prime that is only split in 𝒦 (Theorem 5.5.7), which the sequel's U(n,n) never needs. The Part II keeps only these; the general Igusa geometry widens IG.0, IG.1, IG.3 and IG.4 by a source route, Shin's trace formula and the transfer at p widen EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison, and the Galois representations widen AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII. The title is the parent's title followed by ', Part II: compact unitary Shimura varieties', and the area is the parent's.
routes.brief:
This Part II of Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration proves the compact endgame of Caraiani and Scholze, On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), 649–766: the vanishing of generic Igusa cohomology outside the µ-ordinary stratum, its version for Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties, and the concentration theorem with its Galois representations. It starts where the parent stops: the parent's layers IG.0, IG.1, IG.3 and IG.4, widened by this paper's source route to unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C) and to compact Shimura varieties of Hodge type, supply the Igusa varieties, the fibres of the Hodge–Tate period map (Theorem 4.4.4) and the perversity and concentration results of §6.1; IG.5 and IG.7 remain tied to the non-compact datum of the sequel. Nothing here re-proves the general geometry.

Setting (§5.1, pp. 730–731; §6.3, pp. 756–757). F = F^+·𝒦 is a CM field with F^+ totally real and 𝒦 imaginary quadratic. Case 1: B is a central division algebra over F, V ≅ B, and * is of the second kind (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties). Case 2: B = F, F^+ ≠ Q, G is quasi-split at all finite places, and every rational prime ramified in F lies in Spl_{F/F^+}. S is a finite set of primes outside which F and G are unramified (in Case 2, S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+}); K = K_SK^S is sufficiently small with K^S hyperspecial; T^S = ⊗_{q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ})} Z[G(Q_q)//K_q]. For p = uu^c split in 𝒦, S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p^{−1}∘τ induces 𝔭_i} for the primes 𝔭_i of F above u (the paper prints ι_p∘τ, E86).

Final theorems.
(1) Theorem 5.5.7 (p. 747). Under the assumptions of §5.1, let r : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) be unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ}. Suppose each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and that for each i for which S_i contains such a τ, r|Gal(F̄_{𝔭_i}/F_{𝔭_i}) = χ_{i,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{i,n} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{−1} not cyclotomic for a ≠ b. Then BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S ur})_r = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, µ^{−1}) that is not µ-ordinary. The proof uses Lemma 5.4.3 (generic principal series die under Red^b), Lemma 5.5.8 (only the µ-ordinary class has quasi-split J_b, from BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1) and the Shapiro reduction to GL_n over F_{𝔭_i}, corrected as in E87. Red^b must be the twisted map of E74; the vanishing is unaffected.
(2) Proposition 5.6.1 and Corollaries 5.6.2–5.6.3 (pp. 749–750), in Case 1 with B split above p: tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| ι(G, G_n) ST^{G_n}_e(φ^{G_n}) for acceptable φ_p; the resulting formula for [ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] in terms of automorphic representations of G cohomological for the trivial representation; and the analogue of Theorem 5.5.7. Build the step between them (the stable Lefschetz formula of Arthur and Shin for the proper S_K) here.
(3) Lemma 6.2.2 (p. 756). If ρ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), L/Q_p finite, has decomposed generic reduction (Definition 1.9, routed to AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7, which must widen its decomposed-generic specialization to arbitrary p-adic fields), then ρ is a sum of characters with non-cyclotomic ratios and corresponds to a generic principal series.
(4) Theorem 6.3.1 (p. 757), in Case 1 or 2. (a) If H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some i, there is a unique continuous semisimple ρ_𝔪 : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ), unramified outside the places above S ∪ {ℓ}, such that for every place v of F above q ∈ Spl_{𝒦/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) the characteristic polynomial of ρ_𝔪(Frob_v) is X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} + ⋯ + (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i} + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{n,v} modulo 𝔪, with T_{i,v} the characteristic function of GL_n(O_{F_v}) diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) GL_n(O_{F_v}) × ∏_{w≠v} GL_n(O_{F_w}) × Z_q^× in G(Q_q) (the paper prints Z_p^× and Q_p^×, E12). (b) If for some p ∈ Spl_{𝒦/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) and some 𝔭 | p of the reflex field each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0 and ρ_𝔪 is decomposed generic at every 𝔭_i for which S_i contains such a τ, then H^j(S_K, F_ℓ)_𝔪 ≠ 0 only for j = dim S_K. Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3 give the two ways the hypothesis of (b) is met (Remark 6.3.3 as corrected in E95). Theorem 1.1 and Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1 (integral coefficients, twisted coefficient systems) are consequences.
Proof inputs to state exactly: the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence between finite level and the perfectoid Shimura variety at p, with localization at the contraction of 𝔪 to the Hecke operators away from p (E96, E97); the dual ideal 𝔪^∨ and Hecke-equivariant Poincaré duality on S_K and on the Igusa varieties (E98); Corollary 6.1.4 at a minimal stratum; the Leray spectral sequence for π_HT; and Deligne–Serre lifting of Hecke eigensystems.

Imports, by title and id: the parent, Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0, IG.1, IG.3, IG.4, and IG.5 for the anti-involution of the Hecke algebra); Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0, ET.1, ET.4, ET.5, ET.6, ET.7b) for Shin's trace formula for Igusa varieties, the transfer at p, the map Red^b (E74), Lemma 5.4.3, Lemma 5.5.1 (E77) and Corollary 5.5.2 (E79); Automorphic Galois representations, Part II (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0, AG2.2, AG2.5, AG2.7) for Theorem 5.5.4 (at finite places not above ℓ, E83), Corollary 5.5.5, Remark 5.5.6, Shin's stable base change for simple Shimura varieties and Definition 1.9; B(G) and Newton strata (BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1, BG3); automorphic spectral theory (AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.4–AS.6) for Matsushima's formula and the compact-quotient trace formula; the Leray and Čech spectral sequences (DiamondsAndVStacks D0); Deligne–Serre lifting (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.5); Brauer–Nesbitt and Chebotarev (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1, Tau Ceti Chebotarev, Layer 10); perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5).

Items: 1, 2, 88, 108, 110, 111, 112, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 147, 157. Tests: a compact unitary Shimura curve over F^+ ≠ Q (not the modular curve, which is not compact); Lemma 5.5.8 for n = 2 as a test of BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1.

Consumers: Allen et al., Potential automorphy over CM fields, and the non-compact sequel of Caraiani and Scholze, which reuse the Igusa and concentration arguments through the parent's layers; this Part II supplies the compact theorems they cite.

Its layers are written for the split unitary datum of the non-compact sequel, so this route widens them: IG.0, IG.1 and the local and product-formula parts of IG.3 must be blueprinted for unramified PEL data of type (A) or (C) with hyperspecial level at p, with no compactness (pp. 696–697, 713–714); Theorem 4.4.4 additionally assumes the integral model proper (p. 726), and Proposition 6.1.3 is for compact Shimura varieties of Hodge type (p. 751). For minuscule µ the weights of µ on Lie G lie in {−1, 0, 1}, the unipotent fibres are points and the Bialynicki-Birula map Gr_{G,µ} → Fℓ_{G,µ} is an isomorphism (Theorem 3.4.5), which the layer should derive from its stabilizer computation; Lemmas 3.4.4 and 3.4.6, minuscule cocharacters, Kedlaya–Liu's projectivity criterion and Griffiths transversality are its auxiliary inputs. The paper's sign conventions must be matched with Fargues–Scholze's P^-_µ. Items 37, 38, 39, 132, 133, 135.

P8 plans 'the relative Poincaré lemma' and to 'apply CohomologyComparisons CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection and tensor compatibility'. It takes the relative Hodge–Tate filtration with Corollary 2.2.4, Proposition 2.2.5 and Scholze's B^+_dR-local system of a filtered module with integrable connection; the blueprint must state the primitive comparison R^iπ_*Ô_X ≅ R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_S as an input (p. 666) and use the corrected sheaf OB^+_dR of Scholze's corrigendum (E18). T2 builds the Hodge–Tate sequence and filtration; it takes Theorem 4.1.4 (p-divisible groups over O_C/p and their vector bundles on X_{C♭}), the classification of p-divisible groups over O_C by pairs (T, W), and the modification description of G ×_{O_C} O_C/p. T2 must import VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1, VB2:ampleness and VB2:classification, none of which depends on it, and IG.0 and IG.1 must import T2 if they use these statements. Items 52, 53, 143.

R07.1 plans p-divisible groups and their Tate modules ('Define a p-divisible group … Construct its Tate module'); it takes the universal cover G̃ = T_pG[1/p] (Definition 4.1.1), Messing's representability and the properties of Proposition 4.1.2, and the rigidity of universal covers. R07.2 plans Dieudonné theory and 'deformation results needed for p-divisible groups over nilpotent thickenings'; it takes Scholze–Weinstein's Dieudonné theory up to isogeny over f-semiperfect rings and Berthelot's Dieudonné theory over perfect valuation rings. R07.1 is upstream of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 and of IG.0. Items 49, 50, 138, 139, 142.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison owns Shin's stable trace formula for Igusa varieties and the transfer at p (ET.5: 'prove the stable Igusa identity, including ker^1 and iota(G,H) factors'), elliptic endoscopic data (ET.0), pseudocoefficients (ET.1), base change and the twisted trace formula (ET.4), Badulescu's Jacquet–Langlands map with 'the source's nontransfer obstruction for generic principal-series parameters to a nontrivial inner form' (ET.6) and the expression of the Igusa representation by automorphic representations (ET.7b). Its stages are written for the sequel's group of even rank; this route widens them to the groups G_n⃗ of every rank n, inner forms of arbitrary signature at ∞ (p. 738) and both parities ε(n − n_i) (p. 745). The corrected definition of Red^b (E74), the corrected Lemma 5.5.1 (E77) and Corollary 5.5.2 (E79) must be used. Items 90, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, 149, 150.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII owns the Galois representations attached to regular algebraic automorphic representations (AG2.0, AG2.2: 'Construct the representation for each discrete constituent with its explicit algebraic twists'), local–global compatibility (AG2.5) and genericity (AG2.7: 'Compare a stronger decomposed-generic API only as a separate specialization'). It takes Definition 1.9 (decomposed generic, over an arbitrary p-adic field, which AG2.7 must widen from Q_p), Corollary 5.5.5, Remark 5.5.6 and Shin's stable base change for Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties. Theorem 5.5.4 is planned there already; its statement must be restricted to finite places not above ℓ (E83). Items 3, 106, 107, 156.

P7 constructs 'Huber tilde-limits with both the inverse-limit topology and affinoid density condition' and Frobenius-controlled towers. It takes Scholze–Weinstein's preperfectoid adic spaces and their strong completions, which Theorem 4.2.4 and Proposition 4.2.14 use for the infinite-level Rapoport–Zink space. Items 146.

VB1 defines bundles on the curve and compares them 'with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent'. It takes the Robba rings of §§3.2–3.3 and Kedlaya–Liu's comparison of bundles with φ-modules over them. Items 32.

C8 covers 'topological dimension, topological transcendence degree of complete fields … analytic dimension comparisons'; it takes the general dimension theory of partially proper analytic adic spaces of Propositions 4.2.19–4.2.21 and Remark 4.2.20. IG.3 already depends on C8 transitively, through DiamondSixOperations S1. Items 69.

IG.0 constructs 'the profinite automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers' and treats 'connected components and base-point change as explicit equivalences'. This route widens it to the pro-étale fundamental group of Bhatt–Scholze for connected, locally topologically noetherian schemes, with the equivalence between J_b(Q_p)-torsors on S_proét and continuous homomorphisms π_1^proét(S, x̄) → J_b(Q_p), used in Proposition 1.13 and Remark 4.3.14. Items 125.

B1 constructs the canonical principal bundles, which cuts G out of GL(V) by tensors. It takes Deligne's theorem that a reductive group is the stabiliser of finitely many tensors in a faithful representation, which §2.3 uses for the same purpose. Items 128.

C5 constructs the algebraic de Rham complex of a smooth complex variety, its analytification and the comparison; for proper smooth varieties it combines C2–C3. It takes Deligne's equivalence for flat connections with regular singular points, which §2.3 uses to see that the horizontal tensors are algebraic; for the proper S_K of the main theorems proper GAGA from C3 suffices. Items 131.

AL.3 constructs the GL_n × GL_m Rankin–Selberg zeta integrals and their factors. The proof of Lemma 5.5.1 uses Jacquet–Shalika's strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations, which Jacquet and Shalika derive from these Rankin–Selberg L-functions; the route asks AL.3 to add that consequence. Items 154.

EDC.5 constructs 'the middle perverse t-structure on the appropriate bounded constructible category' for finite-type schemes over a field. It takes the lemma that a perverse sheaf is concentrated in one degree at the generic points of its support, which Corollary 6.1.4 uses. Items 164.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.3, proof of Lemma 2.3.5, p. 671 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: 𝒢_dR is equipped with a canonical map to the flag variety Fl^std_{G,µ} ≃ G/P_µ. […] Proposition 3.5 of [Mil90] proves that automorphic vector bundles are obtained by pullback from Fl_{G,µ} to 𝒢_dR followed by descent to S_K.
sourceIssues.correction: Fl^std_{G,µ} ≃ G/P^std_µ, and 'by pullback from Fl^std_{G,µ} to 𝒢_dR'
sourceIssues.reason: By §2.1 (p. 660), Fl^std_{G,µ} parametrizes parabolics conjugate to P^std_µ, and a base point gives Fl^std_{G,µ}(ℂ) ≃ G(ℂ)/P^std_µ(ℂ). The quotient G/P_µ is the other flag variety, Fl_{G,µ}. The map out of 𝒢_dR comes from 𝒢_dR being the pushout of a P^std_µ-torsor, and it is the map in the diagram S_K ← 𝒢_dR → Fl^std_{G,µ} displayed between the two sentences. Automorphic vector bundles are built from P^std_µ-representations, viewed as G_ℂ-equivariant bundles on Fl^std_{G,µ} (p. 663).

sourceIssues.locator: §5.2, p. 732 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: An endoscopic triple is called elliptic if (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° ⊂ Z(G).
sourceIssues.correction: (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° ⊂ Z(Ĝ), with Z(Ĥ) viewed inside Ĝ through η, i.e. η((Z(Ĥ)^Γ)°) ⊂ Z(Ĝ).
sourceIssues.reason: The printed text has a roman G with no hat on the right-hand side, and arXiv v1 has the same. (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° is a subgroup of the complex dual group Ĥ, and η maps it into Ĝ. Ellipticity (Kottwitz, 7.4 of [Kot84]) asks that this subgroup lie in the centre of Ĝ, not in the centre of the group G over F. The same sentence has a smaller slip: the preceding definition Γ := Gal(Q̄/Q) should be Gal(F̄/F), since F is an arbitrary local or global field there. This does no harm, because the paper uses ellipticity only for F = Q.

sourceIssues.locator: §1, Introduction, p. 650, with “(so that l_0 = 0)” on p. 651 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: “The real group G(ℝ) acts on its associated symmetric domain X = G(ℝ)/K_∞, where K_∞ ⊂ G(ℝ) is a maximal compact subgroup. […] We assume that X_Γ is compact and that Γ is torsion-free. […] here l_0 = rk G − rk K_∞ and q_0 = ½(dim X − l_0). In particular, if l_0 = 0, then tempered representations occur only in the middle degree q_0. This happens when the X_Γ are complex algebraic varieties, e.g., when G gives rise to a Shimura variety.” (p. 650); “In the present paper, we deal with this question in the case where X_Γ is a Shimura variety (so that l_0 = 0).” (p. 651)
sourceIssues.correction: Take X = G(ℝ)/K_∞A_G(ℝ)°, where K_∞ is a maximal compact subgroup and A_G is the maximal ℚ-split torus in the centre of G, as the paper itself does on p. 738 (q(G) = ½ dim G(ℝ)/K_∞A°_∞); equivalently, compute l_0 and q_0 for G/A_G. For the unitary similitude groups of the paper (A_G = 𝔾_m, the scalars) X is then the Hermitian symmetric domain, X_Γ is compact, l_0 = 0 and q_0 = Σ_τ p_τq_τ = dim S_K. The phrase “when G gives rise to a Shimura variety” needs the same convention and, in general, that the centre have the same split rank over ℚ and over ℝ (for G = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_2 with F real quadratic one still has l_0 = 1).
sourceIssues.reason: The groups of the paper are unitary similitude groups; their centre contains the ℚ-split torus 𝔾_m of scalars, on which the similitude character is t ↦ t². With K_∞ merely maximal compact, ℝ_{>0} ⊂ Z(ℝ) is not in K_∞, so rk G(ℝ) − rk K_∞ = 1 and dim X = 1 + 2Σ_τ p_τq_τ is odd; hence l_0 = 1, contradicting “l_0 = 0”, and X_Γ cannot be a complex variety. Moreover |ν| is trivial on K_∞ and on every congruence subgroup Γ (ν(Γ) ⊂ ℚ^× ∩ Ẑ^× = {±1}), so it induces a continuous surjection X_Γ → ℝ_{>0}: X_Γ is never compact, contradicting the standing assumption used for Matsushima's formula. The paper uses the correct convention on p. 738. Nothing is affected: the passage is motivational, removing A_G lowers dim X and l_0 by the same amount so that q_0 = dim S_K either way, and Theorem 1.1 is proved for S_K through Theorem 6.3.1.

sourceIssues.locator: §1, Remark 1.14, p. 657; the same claim in §4.3, Remark 4.3.14, p. 721 (both also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: p. 657: “For example, if b is basic, then the image is a discrete cocompact subgroup of J_b(ℚ_p), related to the p-adic uniformization of the basic locus as in [RZ96].” p. 721: “For the basic Newton stratum, the image of the displayed homomorphism is a discrete cocompact subgroup of J_b(ℚ_p) related to p-adic uniformization.”
sourceIssues.correction: Let b be basic and let J_b(ℚ_p)^0 = ker(ht) be the open normal subgroup of self-quasi-isogenies of height 0. The image of π_1^proét(𝒮^b_K, x̄) → J_b(ℚ_p), well defined up to conjugacy, is a discrete subgroup contained in J_b(ℚ_p)^0, so it is never cocompact in J_b(ℚ_p). For K^p small, p-adic uniformization [RZ96] writes the basic locus as ⊔_i Γ_i∖𝔐_red; on Γ_i∖𝔐_red the image is the stabiliser in Γ_i of a connected component of 𝔐_red, which is cocompact in the open stabiliser of that component in J_b(ℚ_p) but not in J_b(ℚ_p). It is infinite when the connected components of 𝔐_red are not quasi-compact, and trivial when the basic locus is finite (e.g. for the Harris–Taylor Shimura varieties). The discrete subgroups cocompact (modulo the centre) in J_b(ℚ_p) are the uniformising groups Γ_i themselves, not the monodromy image.
sourceIssues.reason: The torsor of Proposition 1.13 (= Proposition 4.3.13, p. 720) parametrises quasi-isogenies ρ : A[p^∞] → 𝕏_b respecting the extra structures. The height of ρ is locally constant and ht(g∘ρ) = ht(g) + ht(ρ) for g ∈ J_b(ℚ_p), so over a connected base the monodromy lies in ker(ht). But p·id ∈ J_b(ℚ_p) is central, respects the extra structures (scaling the polarization by p²) and has height ht(𝕏_b) > 0; hence J_b(ℚ_p)/ker(ht) is an infinite discrete space onto which J_b(ℚ_p)/Γ′ surjects for every subgroup Γ′ ⊂ ker(ht), and no such Γ′ is cocompact. Concretely, in the Harris–Taylor case the basic stratum is finite, each connected component is a geometric point, the pro-étale fundamental group and hence the image are trivial, while J_b(ℚ_p) ⊃ ℚ_p^× is not compact. The remarks are expository and Proposition 4.3.13 is explicitly not used later, so nothing is affected.

sourceIssues.printed: The flag variety Fl_{G̃,µ̃} parametrizes totally isotropic subspaces W ⊂ V.
sourceIssues.correction: The flag variety Fl_{G̃,µ̃} parametrizes Lagrangian subspaces W ⊂ V, that is, maximal (g-dimensional) totally isotropic subspaces.
sourceIssues.reason: Fl_{G̃,µ̃} = G̃/P_µ̃ (p. 660). The Hodge structure on V has types (−1,0) and (0,−1), so µ̃ has two weights, each of multiplicity g, and both weight spaces are totally isotropic; hence P_µ̃ is a Siegel parabolic and Fl_{G̃,µ̃} is the Lagrangian Grassmannian of dimension g(g+1)/2. Totally isotropic subspaces of all dimensions form a disjoint union of isotropic Grassmannians, not one flag variety. The use on p. 662, where π_HT records the g-dimensional Hodge–Tate filtration Lie(A) ⊂ C^{2g}, confirms the intended meaning; nothing depends on the wording.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.3, proof of Lemma 2.3.6, pp. 671–672
sourceIssues.printed: In order to prove that 𝒫_p is a torsor, we note that the type of the Hodge-Tate filtration on 𝒱_p ⊗_{ℚ̂_p} Ô_{𝒮_K} is a discrete invariant, so it is constant on each connected component of 𝒮_K. Therefore, it suffices to check the statement above classical points. Thus, let x ∈ 𝒮_K(L, 𝒪_L) be a point defined over a finite extension L of E_𝔭 with completed algebraic closure C. […] The fact that s_{α,p} can be identified with s_α under the Hodge-Tate isomorphism is proved in [Bla94].
sourceIssues.correction: Apply [Bla94] only at points coming from points of S_K defined over number fields; these meet every nonempty open subset of 𝒮_K. Replace the “discrete invariant” sentence by a closedness argument: over the perfectoid Shimura variety 𝒮_{K^p}, the canonical section of 𝒢_p carries the relative Hodge–Tate filtration to a map 𝒮_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}; the preimage of the closed G(ℚ_p)-stable subvariety Fℓ_{G,µ} is closed and G(ℚ_p)-stable, hence descends to a closed subset of 𝒮_K, which contains all number-field points by [Bla94] and is therefore everything; since G → G/P_µ is Zariski-locally trivial, this gives local sections of 𝒫_p. Alternatively, first match s_{α,dR} and s_{α,p} under the relative p-adic de Rham comparison over all of 𝒮_K, deducing this from number-field points by horizontality exactly as in the proofs of Lemma 2.3.7 (p. 672) and Proposition 2.3.9 (p. 674), which do not use Lemma 2.3.6; the printed argument then applies at every classical point.
sourceIssues.reason: Blasius's theorem concerns abelian varieties over number fields, and the paper cites it only in that form elsewhere: “At points of S_K corresponding to abelian varieties defined over number fields, this follows from [Bla94]” (proof of Lemma 2.3.7, p. 672) and “… matched at points defined over number fields, and thus globally” (proof of Proposition 2.3.9, p. 674). Here it is applied at an arbitrary point over a finite extension L of E_𝔭, which in general is not defined over a number field (there are uncountably many L-points). In addition, the claim that the type of the Hodge–Tate filtration is locally constant presupposes that the filtration is a G-filtration at every point, which is what the lemma is to prove. The lemma is true and every ingredient of the repair is in §2.3, so only the proof is affected.

The same arguments as for Proposition 3.2.1 apply.
sourceIssues.correction: Write r = a/b and s = c/e with positive integers a, b, c, e, and let ℛ^{[s,r],+}_{R,R^+} be the p-adic completion of the integral closure of W(R^+)[p^a/[ϖ]^b, [ϖ]^e/p^c] in W(R^+)[p^a/[ϖ]^b, [ϖ]^e/p^c][1/p]. This describes the same rational subset {|p^a| ≤ |[ϖ]^b|, |[ϖ]^e| ≤ |p^c|}, and it agrees with the printed ring whenever ϖ^{1/r} and ϖ^{1/s} exist, since (p/[ϖ^{1/r}])^a = p^a/[ϖ]^b and ([ϖ^{1/s}]/p)^c = [ϖ]^e/p^c. Alternatively, allow only r, s with 1/r, 1/s ∈ ℤ[1/p]: these roots exist because R is perfect, such values are dense in (0, ∞) and stable under multiplication by p, and they suffice for the covering of 𝒴_{(0,∞)}(R, R^+), the Frobenius isomorphisms and the limits defining ℛ̃^r_R and ℛ̃_R on p. 683.
sourceIssues.reason: The translation into inequalities is correct. In Proposition 3.2.1 the field F is algebraically closed, so ϖ^{1/r} exists for every rational r. In §3.3, R is only a perfectoid algebra of characteristic p: it contains the p-power roots of ϖ but in general no others. For R the completed perfection of 𝔽_p((t)), with value group |t|^{ℤ[1/p]}, every pseudo-uniformizer has |ϖ| = |t|^{m/p^k}, and ϖ^{1/ℓ} ∉ R for every prime ℓ ≠ p with ℓ ∤ m; so for I = [1, ℓ] the displayed ring is undefined, whatever ϖ is chosen. Such R occur in the paper (tilts of perfectoid ℚ_p-algebras in §§3.4–3.5). The one-line proof does not address this. The spaces 𝒴_I are defined independently of the ring and nothing later uses the explicit generators, so no stated result is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.5, Proposition 3.5.7(1), p. 689, and the same word in its proof, p. 690 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: (1) The map b(·) : |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) is lower semicontinuous. […] It is then enough to show that the composite map |Spa(R, R^+)| → |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) is lower semicontinuous.
sourceIssues.correction: Read "upper semicontinuous" in both places, for the partial order ⪯ on B(G) defined on p. 677. That is, every point x has a neighbourhood on which b(·) ⪯ b(x). Since the image is the finite set B(G, µ^{−1}) by part (2), and κ is constant on it, this is equivalent to the following: for every b ∈ B(G), the set {x : b ⪯ b(x)} is closed. Corollary 3.5.9 (p. 690) and Theorem 1.11 (p. 655) use the proposition in exactly this form.
sourceIssues.reason:
The paper orders B(G) on p. 677 by b ⪯ b′ if ν_b ⪯ ν_{b′} and κ(b) = κ(b′). The basic element is the minimum for this order. Read with ⪯, lower semicontinuity would mean that every set {x : b(x) ⪯ b} is closed. In particular the basic stratum would be closed. Corollary 3.5.9 says it "follows immediately" from the proposition, but it states the opposite: the basic stratum is open, and each Fℓ^{⪰b}_{G,µ} = ⊔_{b⪯b′} Fℓ^{b′}_{G,µ} is closed. Theorem 1.11 says the same. The modular-curve example on p. 655 shows that the printed direction cannot hold. There Fℓ = ℙ^1, the strata are ℙ^1(ℚ_p) and Ω², and Ω² is open. Under the printed reading Ω² would also be closed, which is impossible because |ℙ^1| is connected and both strata are non-empty.

The word comes from [KL15, Th. 7.4.5]. There it refers to the y-coordinates of the convex slope polygon (Def. 7.4.1), and the proof shows that near β the polygon lies on or above the polygon at β. With the endpoints fixed, a higher polygon has less spread-out slopes, so it corresponds to a smaller Newton point for ⪯. This does not depend on the sign convention linking bundles to B(G), because ν ⪯ ν′ if and only if −w_0ν ⪯ −w_0ν′. So Kedlaya–Liu's result is exactly upper semicontinuity of b(·) for ⪯. The argument on p. 690 (reduce to representations by [RR96, Lemma 2.2], then apply [KL15, Th. 7.4.5] with Corollary 3.3.4) therefore proves the corrected statement.

Only the name of the property is wrong. The intended statement is clear from Corollary 3.5.9 and Theorem 1.11, it is proved, and it is used correctly. None of the paper's results change. The printed wording of Proposition 3.5.7(1) is still false under the paper's own order, so the misprint sits in a stated result. It should be recorded as a misprint, not as an error. As printed, the statement of Proposition 3.5.7(1) is false; items use the corrected direction.
sourceIssues.known: No erratum or published remark was found. The non-compact sequel (Caraiani–Scholze 2024, Theorem 2.7.3) restates the result directly as closedness of Fℓ^{≥b}, which agrees with the corrected reading, and does not repeat the word.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.1, proof of Lemma 4.1.8, p. 696 (also in arXiv v1, p. 41)
sourceIssues.printed: For this, using the Dieudonné-Manin classification, we have to see that there are no elements x ∈ A_cris(R) with p^aφ^b(x) = x, where a, b > 0 are positive integers.
sourceIssues.correction: … we have to see that there are no nonzero elements x ∈ A_cris(R) with p^aφ^b(x) = x, where a, b > 0 are positive integers.
sourceIssues.reason: The sentence is printed exactly as recorded on p. 696. This was checked on the page image, and the text layer agrees. Read literally, the claim is false, because x = 0 satisfies p^aφ^b(x) = x. What the proof needs is that every solution is zero. The reduction runs as follows. By the Dieudonné–Manin classification over F̄_p, it suffices to treat a simple isocrystal D of slope a/b > 0. It has a basis e_1, …, e_b with φ(e_i) = e_{i+1} for i < b and φ(e_b) = p^a e_1. An element Σ x_i ⊗ e_i of D ⊗ B^+_cris(R) is φ-invariant if and only if x_{i+1} = φ(x_i) for i < b and x_1 = p^aφ(x_b). That is, x_1 = p^aφ^b(x_1), and x_1 determines the other coordinates. Multiplying by a power of p puts x_1 in A_cris(R). So (D ⊗ B^+_cris(R))^{φ=1} = 0 is equivalent to the vanishing of every x ∈ A_cris(R) with p^aφ^b(x) = x. The next two sentences prove exactly this: iterating gives x = p^{ma}φ^{mb}(x) ∈ p^{ma}A_cris(R) for every m ≥ 1, and A_cris(R) is p-adically separated, so x = 0. The meaning is clear, and the correction only adds the word "nonzero". Lemma 4.1.8 and Corollaries 4.1.10–4.1.11 are unaffected. arXiv v1 (p. 41) has the same wording, so the slip predates the refereed revision.

For each λ_j > d/2, the pair {𝕏_i, 𝕏_j} contributes m_im_j(λ_j − d/2) exactly once to each side. On the dimension side, this is the dimension of the internal Hom 𝒪_F-module from 𝕏_i to 𝕏_j; the polarization determines the internal Hom from 𝕏_j^∨ to 𝕏_i^∨ ≅ 𝕏_i. On the root side, let k run over block j and l over the m_i/2 coordinates of block i among the first n/2. For each τ this gives m_jm_i/2 roots e_{τ,k} − e_{τ,l} and m_jm_i/2 roots e_{τ,k} + e_{τ,l} − c, each taking the value (λ_j − d/2)/d at ν_b, so the total over the d embeddings is m_im_j(λ_j − d/2). The block 𝕏_i paired with itself contributes 0 to both sides. With this change, items (1)–(3) and the new case partition both the dimension of Aut_G(𝕏̃_b) and ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩, and the matching holds case by case.

So one piece of Aut_G(𝕏̃_b), of dimension m_im_j(λ_j − d/2), is counted twice. The root-side matches claimed in (1) and (2) also fail for this pair. Only m_i/2 of the m_i coordinates of ν_b equal to 1/2 lie among the first n/2, so the roots e_{τ,k} − e_{τ,l} give only half the claimed value, and so do the roots e_{τ,k} + e_{τ,l} − c.

Example: take F = ℚ_p (d = 1), G = GSp_4 and ν_b = (1, 1/2, 1/2, 0), which is the p-divisible group of a principally polarized abelian surface of p-rank 1. The slopes are 1, 1/2, 0 with m = 1, 2, 1.

- Items (1)–(3) as printed give 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 on the dimension side. Items (1) and (2) each claim a root contribution of 1, where the true value is 1/2.

The printed steps are therefore false whenever d/2 is a slope and 𝕏_b is not isoclinic. In the isoclinic case, (1) and (2) are vacuous. The error cannot be fixed by changing ≥ to >: that leaves the middle-slope pairs uncovered, and they need the separate count given in the correction. Proposition 4.2.11 itself (p. 704) is true. I checked the corrected case division against both ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ and the orbit-by-orbit dimension count over many symmetric slope data, with and without a middle slope, and they agreed every time. sourceIssues.locator: §4.2, Remark 4.2.17, p. 710 (used in the proof of Lemma 4.3.15, p. 722; same text in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: Using this lemma, one can remove the noetherian hypothesis from the main result of [Ber80]; i.e., the same fully faithfulness result holds true for any integral domain R in place of V. Indeed, to check whether a homomorphism over K extends to R, one has to check whether certain matrices over K have entries in R, which can be checked on valuation rings.
sourceIssues.correction: … the same fully faithfulness result holds true for any integrally closed domain R of characteristic p (with G, H p-divisible groups over R of constant Newton polygon) in place of V. Indeed, to check whether a homomorphism over K extends to R, one has to check whether certain matrices over K have entries in R, which can be checked on the valuation rings of K containing R, since R is their intersection.
sourceIssues.reason:
The valuation rings of K containing R intersect in the integral closure of R, not in R itself, so the argument only shows that the matrix entries are integral over R. The theorem of [Ber80] being generalised (Th. 4.7.2) assumes the base is connected and normal; its proof uses R = ∩ R_𝔭 over height-one primes. Lemma 4.2.15 (p. 709) likewise assumes R⁺ integrally closed in R. So normality is the hypothesis that matters, and dropping it makes the claim false.

Counterexample: let R = {f ∈ F̄_p[t] : f(0) = f(1)}, the affine line with 0 and 1 glued, with K = F̄_p(t). Let G be the étale p-divisible group of height 1 whose Tate module is the rank-one ℤ_p-local system that is trivial on the normalization A¹ and glued at the node by some u ∈ ℤ_p^× with u ≠ 1. Let H = ℚ_p/ℤ_p. Both are étale, so both have constant Newton polygon. G_K is constant, so Hom_K(H_K, G_K) = ℤ_p. But Hom_R(H, G) = {v ∈ ℤ_p : uv = v} = 0. R is even noetherian, and the same example works after passing to perfections.

The remark is invoked only in the domain case of the proof of Lemma 4.3.15 (p. 722). There it is applied to strictly henselian perfect domains, which need not be normal: the perfection of the strict henselisation of the Whitney umbrella at its pinch point is an example. So that proof has a gap. Lemma 4.3.15 itself still holds, and the gap can be closed as follows. The normalization R′ of R is again a strictly henselian perfect domain with residue field k, and the corrected remark applies to it. Descend the resulting quasi-isogeny from R′ to R along the v-cover R → R′, as in the last paragraph of that proof. The uniqueness this needs comes from the Dieudonné-module computation already given there.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.2, proof of Proposition 4.2.22, pp. 712–713 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 4.2.22. For any complete nonarchimedean field K/O_Ĕ, the space Aut_G(𝕏̃_b)^ad ×_{Spa(O_Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} Spa(K, O_K) is partially proper over Spa(K, O_K), of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩. Proof. The adic generic fiber is partially proper by Lemma 4.2.15.
sourceIssues.correction: Lemma 4.2.15 covers only K of characteristic 0, but the statement also allows K of characteristic p, and the proof uses that case (“by tilting we can assume that K is of characteristic p”, p. 713). For all K, partial properness follows from Proposition 4.2.11: the space maps to the locally profinite set J_b(ℚ_p) with fibres the open perfectoid unit polydisc of dimension d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ over K, so a (K′, K′^+)-point is an element of J_b(ℚ_p) together with compatible p-power roots of d topologically nilpotent elements of K′; these lie in every K′^+, so the points do not depend on K′^+, which is the criterion of Remark 4.2.20.
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 4.2.15 concerns rings R = R^+[1/p] and extends homomorphisms from R to R^+. If K has characteristic p then K^+[1/p] = 0, the lemma says nothing, and the space lies over the special fibre of Spa(O_Ĕ, O_Ĕ), not the generic fibre. The missing case is easy, the dimension computation uses only the underlying topological space, and Proposition 4.2.23 applies Proposition 4.2.22 only over fields of characteristic 0, so nothing is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.3, Remark 4.3.14, p. 721 (also in arXiv v1)
sourceIssues.printed: We remark that the displayed map may have noncompact image in general, but the image is compact in case 𝕏 admits a slope decomposition (or is isogenous to such an 𝕏); this explains [OZ02, Ex. 4.2], where a p-divisible group over a nonnormal base is constructed that is not isogenous to one admitting a slope filtration.
sourceIssues.correction: … but the image is compact in case 𝕏 is completely slope divisible in the sense of [OZ02, Def. 1.2] (after passing to the perfection of S, such an 𝕏 is pro-étale locally isomorphic to a constant group, so the image lies in a compact open subgroup of J_b(ℚ_p)), or is isogenous to such an 𝕏; this explains [OZ02, Ex. 4.2], where a p-divisible group over a nonnormal base is constructed that is not isogenous to a completely slope divisible one.
sourceIssues.reason: A decomposition into isoclinic summands does not force compact image; an isoclinic group is its own slope decomposition. Take G = G_{1,2} (isoclinic of height 3, with a unique α_p ⊂ G and G/α_p ≅ G via Frobenius) and follow [OZ02, Ex. 4.2] with both factors equal to G: on T = ℙ^1 embed α_p(𝒪(−1)) into α_p × α_p ⊂ G × G by (ι_0, ι_∞), take the quotient X_T, and glue its fibres X_0 = G × G/α_p and X_∞ = G/α_p × G, both identified with G × G via Frobenius, over the nodal curve T/(0 ∼ ∞). The resulting isoclinic group has monodromy diag(Fr^{−1}, Fr) ∈ GL_2(D) = J_b(ℚ_p), D = End^0(G), whose powers are unbounded. The remark's own next sentence (cocompact image on the basic stratum, where the group is isoclinic) also contradicts it. For completely slope divisible 𝕏 over a perfect base the group splits canonically into isoclinic pieces, each pro-étale locally constant [OZ02, Prop. 1.3], so the torsor comes from a compact group, as on p. 657. [OZ02, Ex. 4.2] itself asserts only that there is no isogeny to a completely slope divisible group. Proposition 4.3.13 and the remark are not used later.
